definitions.note: Present tense (tú form) of "acabar".

definitions.note: Used in the expression “acabo de + infinitive” to say something happened a moment ago.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I just got home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acabo de llegar a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I just got home.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m bringing the chair closer to the table.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brought the chair closer to the table.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will accompany you to the doctor tomorrow.

definitions.note: Usually the formal command (usted) form, or the present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Señor, por favor, acompáñeme a la oficina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sir, please accompany me to the office.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo). Often used to mean “I’ll go with you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si quieres, te acompaño al médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you want, I’ll go with you to the doctor.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), 1st person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acompañé a mi amiga al médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accompanied my friend to the doctor.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she/it accompanied; you (formal) accompanied.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María acompañó a su abuela al médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María accompanied her grandmother to the doctor.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú): “accompany me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acompáñame al supermercado, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come with me to the supermarket, please.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “aire acondicionado” (“air conditioning”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche está acondicionado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is air-conditioned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te he aconsejado hablar con el profesor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have advised you to talk to the teacher.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “espero que…”), or as a formal (usted) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que el médico me aconseje descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the doctor advises me to rest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te aconsejo que hables con el profesor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I advise you to talk to the teacher.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aconsejé a mi amigo que descansara un poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I advised my friend to rest a little.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she advised; also used for usted (you, formal) advised.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico me aconsejó descansar unos días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor advised me to rest for a few days.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El concierto fue un acontecimiento muy importante para la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert was a very important event for the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los acontecimientos de ayer cambiaron la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday’s events changed the city.

definitions.note: Past participle of “acordar” meaning “to agree.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hemos acordado un precio justo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have agreed on a fair price.

definitions.note: Past participle of “acordar” meaning “to wake up.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El bebé ya ha acordado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby has already woken up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acordamos vernos mañana a las diez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agreed to see each other tomorrow at ten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer acordamos temprano para tomar el tren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we woke up early to catch the train.

definitions.note: Often used with “acordar + infinitive” (to agree to do something) or “acordar que + clause” (to agree that…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que acordar una fecha para la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to agree on a date for the meeting.

definitions.note: Commonly used with "de" (acordarse de + noun/infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito acordarme de llamar a mi mamá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to remember to call my mom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer acordaron reunirse a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they agreed to meet at six.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo toca el acordeón en las fiestas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandpa plays the accordion at parties.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acordé una reunión para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I scheduled/arranged a meeting for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El comité acordó cambiar la fecha de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The committee agreed to change the date of the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used with estar: estar acostado = to be lying down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy acostado en la cama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am lying down in bed.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to describe someone’s position (e.g., "estar acostado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano está acostado en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is lying down on the couch.

definitions.note: From "acostar" in the sense of putting someone to bed (not "going to bed" oneself, which is usually "acostarse").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cada noche acostamos a los niños a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every night we put the kids to bed at eight.

definitions.note: Often used as a reflexive verb (acostarse) meaning “to go to bed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a acostar al bebé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to put the baby to bed.

definitions.native: to lie down, to go to bed
definitions.note: Reflexive form with an object pronoun: “me” = myself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a acostarme temprano esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to go to bed early tonight.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me acuesto temprano porque mañana trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to bed early because I work tomorrow.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun “te” attached (“you” as the direct object). Often used with “ir a” (e.g., “voy a acostarte”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a acostarte temprano porque mañana tienes escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to put you to bed early because you have school tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense (él/ella/usted) of “acostumbrar”; often used with “a” + infinitive (e.g., “acostumbra a…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella acostumbra a levantarse temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She usually gets up early.

definitions.note: Imperfect past: describes a habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, acostumbraba ir al parque después de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to go to the park after school.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy acostumbrada a levantarme temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m used to getting up early.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" + infinitive or noun (e.g., "acostumbrado a levantarme temprano").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy acostumbrado a levantarme temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm used to getting up early.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" or in the phrase "estar acostumbrado a" + infinitive/noun (to be used to doing something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy acostumbrado a levantarme temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m used to getting up early.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (also used for mixed-gender groups). Often followed by “a” + infinitive or “a” + noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos acostumbrados a levantarnos temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are used to getting up early.

definitions.native: we usually do, we tend to
definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En mi familia, acostumbramos cenar juntos los domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In my family, we usually have dinner together on Sundays.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with "me" = "myself"; often used with "a" + infinitive or noun ("acostumbrarme a...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que acostumbrarme a levantarme temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get used to waking up early.

definitions.note: Reflexive: it’s used with a reflexive pronoun (me/te/se/nos/os/se) and often with “a” (e.g., acostumbrarse a algo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me estoy acostumbrando a levantarme temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m getting used to getting up early.

definitions.note: Future tense (informal “you”). Often used with “a” + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te acostumbrarás al clima en unas semanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will get used to the weather in a few weeks.

definitions.native: you get used to, you usually do
definitions.note: Present tense, informal singular (tú). Often used with “a” + infinitive: “acostumbras a + verb”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Te acostumbras a levantarte temprano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you get used to getting up early?

definitions.note: Present tense, first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acostumbro a levantarme temprano los días de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually get up early on weekdays.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me acostumbré al horario nuevo en una semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got used to the new schedule in a week.

definitions.native: got used to, became accustomed to
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se acostumbró al clima frío rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got used to the cold weather quickly.

definitions.native: I put (someone) to bed, I laid (someone) down
definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), first-person singular; often used reflexively as “me acosté” = “I went to bed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anoche acosté al bebé temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night I put the baby to bed early.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past). Often used reflexively as “se acostó” = “went to bed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mamá acostó al bebé temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mom put the baby to bed early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas una acreditación para entrar al evento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need an accreditation to enter the event.

definitions.note: Feminine singular adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La escuela está acreditada por el gobierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school is accredited by the government.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa llegó a un acuerdo con sus acreedores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company reached an agreement with its creditors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El acróbata hizo un salto increíble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The acrobat did an incredible jump.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el circo, los acróbatas hicieron un espectáculo increíble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the circus, the acrobats put on an incredible show.

definitions.note: Common in formal contexts (e.g., meetings, official sessions). Often used in the plural: “las actas”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La secretaria redactó el acta de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The secretary wrote up the minutes of the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta tu actitud positiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your positive attitude.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es muy activa y siempre está haciendo algo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very active and is always doing something.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy tenemos una actividad en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we have an activity in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos muchas actividades después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have many activities after class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo está muy activo y camina todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is very active and walks every day.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (also used for mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis abuelos siguen activos y salen a caminar todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are still active and go for a walk every day.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular: “he/she/it activated/turned on.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella activó el modo avión antes de despegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She turned on airplane mode before taking off.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts; it can refer to an action, an act in a play, or an official record ("acta") depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El primer acto de la obra es muy divertido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The first act of the play is very funny.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano quiere ser actor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother wants to be an actor.

definitions.note: plural of "actor" (male or mixed-gender group)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los actores llegan al teatro a las siete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actors arrive at the theater at seven.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los actos del festival empiezan a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The festival events start at eight.

definitions.note: Plural of "actriz" (female actors).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las actrices saludaron al público al final de la obra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actresses greeted the audience at the end of the play.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana quiere ser actriz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister wants to be an actress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La actriz ganó un premio por su actuación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actress won an award for her performance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su actuación en la película fue excelente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her performance in the movie was excellent.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts, especially for actions taken by institutions (e.g., the police or government).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La actuación de la policía evitó un accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police’s intervention prevented an accident.

definitions.note: In Spanish, "actual" usually means "current" (not "actual" in the sense of "real").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dirección actual es diferente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My current address is different.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los problemas actuales requieren soluciones nuevas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Current problems require new solutions.

definitions.note: Often used for software/app/system updates, or for updating information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una actualización del informe antes de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need an update to the report before the meeting.

definitions.note: Means “nowadays/these days” or “at the moment,” not “actually.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Actualmente vivo en Madrid, pero antes vivía en Valencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I currently live in Madrid, but before I lived in Valencia.

definitions.note: From the verb “actuar”; can mean acting (as in theater) or taking action, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no actuamos ahora, será demasiado tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we don’t act now, it will be too late.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ando form): often used for “(is/are) acting” or “while acting/doing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está actuando en una obra de teatro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is acting in a play.

definitions.note: Often used for acting in theater/film, or for how someone behaves in a situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella quiere actuar en una película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to act in a movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella actuó en una película el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She acted in a movie last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella actúa en una película nueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She acts in a new movie.

definitions.note: Often used in a general sense of behaving or responding in a situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando hay un problema, él actúa rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When there is a problem, he acts quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré acuarelas para pintar paisajes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought watercolors to paint landscapes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos un acuario con peces de colores en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have an aquarium with colorful fish in the living room.

definitions.note: Often used for going somewhere in response to a call/need or to seek help.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando escucha la alarma, acude rápidamente a la entrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he hears the alarm, he quickly goes to the entrance.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “they showed up” or “they came in response” (e.g., to help or to an event).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llamaron, acudieron de inmediato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they called, they came right away.

definitions.native: to go, to come (to a place or event)
definitions.note: Often used for going in response to a call, invitation, or need (e.g., to an appointment or to help).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a acudir a la reunión mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to go to the meeting tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite): he/she/you (formal) went/attended.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella acudió a la reunión a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She went to the meeting on time.

definitions.note: Often used with an object, especially in phrases like “acordar algo” (to agree on/arrange something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella acuerda el plan con su equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She agrees on the plan with her team.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively as “te acuerdas (de ...)” (informal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Te acuerdas de mi nombre?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you remember my name?

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., a plan, a time, a price).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tú acuerdas la hora con el doctor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You agree on the time with the doctor.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., a price, a date) and can be followed by “con” to say who you agree with.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo acuerdo el precio con el vendedor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agree on the price with the seller.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegamos a un acuerdo después de hablar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached an agreement after talking.

definitions.note: From "acostar". Can mean either "(he/she) puts (someone) to bed" or "(he/she) lies down," depending on context (reflexive: "se acuesta").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas las noches acuesta a su hijo a las nueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every night he puts his son to bed at nine.

definitions.native: I put to bed, I lay down
definitions.note: Commonly used reflexively as «me acuesto» = “I go to bed / I lie down.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acuesto al bebé a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the baby to bed at eight.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of “acumular” (also used for “usted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El polvo se acumula en la esquina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dust accumulates in the corner.

definitions.note: Past participle of "acumular"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He acumulado suficiente dinero para el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have accumulated enough money for the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acumuló mucha experiencia durante esos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accumulated a lot of experience during those years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo varias acusaciones contra el director.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were several accusations against the director.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La acusación fue muy grave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accusation was very serious.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with a feminine noun or a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mujer fue acusada de robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The woman was accused of theft.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts; can also describe someone blamed for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El acusado negó los cargos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accused person denied the charges.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El acusado habló con su abogado antes del juicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The defendant spoke with his lawyer before the trial.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle (e.g., with ser) and can also be used as an adjective or noun (“the accused/defendant”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El hombre fue acusado de robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was accused of theft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía lo va a acusar de robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to accuse him of theft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los periodistas acusaron al político de mentir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalists accused the politician of lying.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" before a person: "Acuso a Juan de mentir."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te acuso de haber tomado mi libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accuse you of having taken my book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abogado acusó al sospechoso de robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawyer accused the suspect of theft.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). Used with the reflexive pronoun “te” in “acordarse de”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acuérdate de llamar a tu mamá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Remember to call your mom.

definitions.note: Common in Latin America; in Spain, "aquí" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ven acá, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here, please.

definitions.note: Command (tú). "lo" = "it" (a direct object pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no puedes cambiarlo, acéptalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you can’t change it, accept it.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú); it literally means “bring yourself closer.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acércate, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come closer, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, acérquese a la ventana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, come closer to the window.

definitions.note: Reflexive: means adapting yourself/itself (often used with “a” + noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me cuesta adaptarme a la nueva ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard for me to adapt to the new city.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she adapted; it adapted; you (formal) adapted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella adaptó la historia para el teatro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She adapted the story for the theater.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta solución es adecuada para el problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This solution is suitable for the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debes vestirte adecuadamente para la entrevista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should dress properly for the interview.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este libro es adecuado para niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is suitable for children.

definitions.note: Often used for moving to the front or progressing; also used when someone gets ahead of others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella adelanta para abrir la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She goes ahead to open the door.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something that is ahead of schedule or more developed than expected.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El proyecto está muy adelantado para esta etapa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project is very advanced for this stage.

definitions.note: Often used to say something happens earlier than expected; it can look like English “advanced,” but here it usually means “early/ahead of time.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegué adelantado a la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arrived early to the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se adelantaron para ver mejor el desfile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They moved ahead to see the parade better.

definitions.note: Often used to encourage someone to proceed (like “go ahead”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sigue adelante y no te rindas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep going forward and don’t give up.

definitions.note: Often used to invite someone to enter or to encourage someone to continue speaking or acting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —¿Puedo pasar? —Sí, adelante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: “Can I come in?” “Yes, go ahead.”

definitions.note: Often used for money paid before the full amount is due.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me dieron un adelanto del sueldo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave me an advance on my salary.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche adelantó a la bicicleta en la carretera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car passed the bicycle on the road.

definitions.native: brought forward, moved up (to an earlier time)
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular (he/she/it/you formal).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting was moved up by an hour.

definitions.native: to lose weight, to slim down
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero adelgazar antes del verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to lose weight before summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Además, mañana podemos ir al parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Also, tomorrow we can go to the park.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion (e.g., entrar, meter) to mean “(to) inside.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold; you’d better stay inside.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" (e.g., "adhiere a la pared" = sticks to the wall).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La etiqueta se adhiere bien a la caja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The label sticks well to the box.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" to mean joining a group, plan, or idea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella se adhiere al programa de voluntariado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She joins the volunteer program.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su adicción al tabaco le afecta la salud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His addiction to tobacco affects his health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos información adicional para completar el formulario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need additional information to complete the form.

definitions.note: Plural form (more than one).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos recursos adicionales para terminar el proyecto a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need additional resources to finish the project on time.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (e.g., “adicto a”) to say someone is addicted to something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soy adicto al café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m addicted to coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un adicto al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a work addict.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vecina es adinerada y vive en una casa grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is wealthy and lives in a big house.

definitions.note: Common farewell; also said when leaving or ending a conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bueno, me voy; adios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Well, I'm leaving; goodbye.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command ("Guess!") or in the expression “Adivina qué” (“Guess what”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Adivina qué: mañana es mi cumpleaños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guess what: tomorrow is my birthday.

definitions.note: female form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La adivina leyó mi mano en la feria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fortune teller read my palm at the fair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo he adivinado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have guessed it.

definitions.note: Often used for guessing an answer, what someone is thinking, or predicting something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes adivinar la respuesta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you guess the answer?

definitions.native: to guess it, to figure it out
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo adivinarlo sin una pista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t guess it without a clue.

definitions.note: Used with ustedes (formal or plural “you”) as a command: “(you all) guess.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Adivinen qué pasó hoy en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guess what happened at school today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Adivino que hoy va a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guess it’s going to rain today.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “(he/she/you formal) guessed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella adivinó la respuesta sin ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She guessed the answer without help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bueno, me tengo que ir: adiós.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Well, I have to go: goodbye.

definitions.note: Used as a farewell (often with ¡Adiós!).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que irme; adiós.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go; goodbye.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "archivo adjunto" (attached file), especially in emails.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te envío el documento adjunto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sending you the attached document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella administra una pequeña tienda en el barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She manages a small shop in the neighborhood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La administración del hospital cambió las reglas de visita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hospital administration changed the visiting rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La administración del dinero es importante para ahorrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Managing money is important for saving.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who manages an organization, system, or property (e.g., a website or an apartment building).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El administrador del edificio vive en la planta baja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building manager lives on the ground floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella admira a su profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She admires her teacher.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (used for ongoing, repeated, or background actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, admiraba a mi abuelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I admired my grandfather.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all admired; also he/she/it admired in some regional uses of "vosotros"-less Spanish).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De niños, admiraban a su maestra por su paciencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As children, they admired their teacher for her patience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu trabajo es admirable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your work is admirable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento mucha admiración por mi profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of admiration for my teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es una científica muy admirada en su país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a very admired scientist in her country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene muchos admiradores por su música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has many admirers because of his music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los admiradores esperaron afuera del teatro para ver a la actriz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The admirers waited outside the theater to see the actress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Admiramos tu valentía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We admire your bravery.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present (they/you all admire).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muchos estudiantes admiran a su profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many students admire their teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Admiro tu paciencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I admire your patience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te admiro por tu valentía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I admire you for your bravery.

definitions.note: Often used for being allowed to enter a place or institution, or the process of being accepted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La admisión al museo es gratuita los domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission to the museum is free on Sundays.

definitions.note: Can mean “admits” (confesses/acknowledges) or “allows” (permits).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El museo no admite mascotas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum doesn't allow pets.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (present tense) of "admitir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En este cine admiten perros pequeños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this movie theater, they allow small dogs.

definitions.note: Past participle of “admitir.” It’s used with “haber” to form perfect tenses, or as an adjective meaning “admitted/accepted.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He admitido que me equivoqué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have admitted that I was wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finalmente, admitieron que estaban equivocados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Finally, they admitted that they were wrong.

definitions.note: Often used for admitting something is true, or admitting someone into a place or institution.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que admitir que me equivoqué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to admit that I was wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que admitirlo: estabas equivocado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to admit it: you were wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él admitió que estaba equivocado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He admitted that he was wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Admito que estaba equivocado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I admit that I was wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Admití que estaba equivocado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I admitted that I was wrong.

definitions.note: Often written in Spanish as “ADN” (ácido desoxirribonucleico).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: DNA contains genetic information.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La adolescencia puede ser una etapa difícil para algunos jóvenes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es adolescente y va al instituto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a teenager and goes to high school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los adolescentes suelen dormir hasta tarde los fines de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Teenagers often sleep in late on weekends.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “to where,” especially with verbs of movement. It can also appear without an accent as a relative adverb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Adonde vas después de clase?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are you going after class?

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of movement, like “ir” or “venir.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Adondequiera que vayas, te llamaré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wherever you go, I’ll call you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana adopta un perro del refugio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister adopts a dog from the shelter.

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of "adoptar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La niña fue adoptada cuando tenía dos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl was adopted when she was two years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hijo fue adoptado cuando era bebé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My son was adopted when he was a baby.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queremos adoptar un perro del refugio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to adopt a dog from the shelter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos adoptaron a un perro del refugio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They adopted a dog from the shelter.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for the formal command “usted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que adopte al perro del refugio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you adopt the dog from the shelter.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes/ellos/ellas); also used for affirmative commands with ustedes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que adopten un perro del refugio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you adopt a dog from the shelter.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es la madre adoptiva del niño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the child's adoptive mother.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she adopted; you (formal) adopted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Laura adoptó un perro del refugio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Laura adopted a dog from the shelter.

definitions.note: Present tense (él/ella/usted) of "adorar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella adora a su abuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She adores her grandmother.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, adoraba los helados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I loved ice cream.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esa época, adoraban a sus dioses en silencio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that time period, they worshipped their gods in silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Qué perro tan adorable!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What an adorable dog!

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los cachorros son adorables.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The puppies are adorable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos adoran a su perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They adore their dog.

definitions.note: Often used to express strong liking or enthusiasm, not necessarily religious worship.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Adoro esta canción!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love this song!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un hábito adquirido con el tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a habit acquired over time.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., acquiring skills, knowledge, property).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero adquirir más experiencia en este trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to acquire more experience in this job.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “he/she/it acquired/bought” or “you (formal) acquired/bought.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa adquirió una nueva máquina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company acquired a new machine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo hizo adrede para molestarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did it on purpose to annoy me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tuvimos que pasar por aduanas al llegar al aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had to go through customs when we arrived at the airport.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El adulterio puede destruir una relación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Adultery can destroy a relationship.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite the adversity, they kept going.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico me dio una advertencia sobre el azúcar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor gave me a warning about sugar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las advertencias en la etiqueta son importantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warnings on the label are important.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already warned you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Advertí un error en el informe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed an error in the report.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she/you (formal) warned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor nos advirtió sobre el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher warned us about the exam.

definitions.note: Used in questions (direct or indirect) to ask about a destination or direction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Adónde vas después de clase?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are you going after class?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos al aeropuerto temprano para tomar el vuelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to the airport early to catch the flight.

definitions.note: Plural of "aeropuerto".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two airports in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ruido afecta mi concentración.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise affects my concentration.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La zona afectada necesita ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The affected area needs help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pueblo fue afectado por la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The town was affected by the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cambio de horario afectará mi rutina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The schedule change will affect my routine.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of affection for my grandparents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me afeito todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shave every morning.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/you formal) in the past (preterite).

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone who is really into a hobby, sport, or activity.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This knife is very sharp.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los cuchillos están afilados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knives are sharp.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His statements don't match the facts.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are very lucky to have good friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aparentemente, el tren llega a tiempo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apparently, the train arrives on time today.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “aparecer” (used after expressions of doubt, desire, necessity, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que aparezca pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it appears soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La aparición del sol cambió el ánimo de todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The appearance of the sun changed everyone’s mood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su apariencia cambió mucho después del viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her appearance changed a lot after the trip.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “las apariencias engañan” (“appearances can be deceiving”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te fíes de las apariencias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t trust appearances.

definitions.native: separate, set apart, out of the way
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en un pueblo apartado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in a remote town.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busco un apartamento cerca del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for an apartment near work.

definitions.note: Often used as an adverb or in set phrases like “aparte de” = “apart from / besides.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deja ese libro aparte, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave that book aside, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano y yo vivimos aparte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother and I live apart.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed expressions like “aparte de” (besides/aside from) or “aparte” to mean “set aside.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aparte de eso, todo está bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Aside from that, everything is fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apartó la silla para que pudiéramos pasar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He moved the chair aside so we could pass.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (e.g., “Me apasiona…”), meaning “I’m passionate about…”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me apasiona la música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m passionate about music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habló apasionadamente sobre la importancia de la educación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke passionately about the importance of education.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un músico apasionado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a passionate musician.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" to mean being really into something or someone: "apasionado de la música".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy apasionado de la fotografía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m really into photography.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (apelar a algo / a alguien) meaning “to appeal to” (to request, to call on, or to rely on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abogado va a apelar la sentencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawyer is going to appeal the sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi apellido es García.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My last name is García.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apenas entiendo lo que dice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hardly understand what he says.

definitions.note: Used with time expressions to mean something happens immediately after something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apenas llegues, llámame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As soon as you arrive, call me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La apertura de la tienda es a las nueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store opening is at nine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa basura apesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That garbage stinks.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: describes an ongoing or habitual situation in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cocina apestaba a pescado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen stank of fish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tus zapatos apestan después del entrenamiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your shoes stink after training.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Apestas a humo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You stink of smoke!

definitions.note: Often used informally and can sound insulting when describing a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Qué calcetines tan apestosos!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What stinky socks!

definitions.native: feels like, sounds good, would like
definitions.note: Used to talk about what someone feels like doing or having (often with an indirect object like “me/te/le”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Te apetece un café?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you feel like a coffee?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo apetito hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have an appetite today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando vio al perro herido, se apiadó y lo llevó al veterinario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the injured dog, he took pity and took it to the vet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito apio para hacer la sopa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need celery to make the soup.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective (also the past participle of "aplastar").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche quedó aplastado después del accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car ended up crushed after the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aplastó la lata con el pie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She crushed the can with his/her foot.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): “they” form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando terminó el concierto, aplaudieron con entusiasmo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the concert ended, they applauded enthusiastically.

definitions.native: we applauded, we clap, we clapped
definitions.note: Can mean either the preterite (past) or the present tense “we applaud/clap,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aplaudimos al final del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We applauded at the end of the concert.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), third-person singular (he/she/you formal) of “aplaudir.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El público aplaudió al final del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience applauded at the end of the concert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El público le dio un aplauso al final del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience gave him/her applause at the end of the concert.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al final del concierto, hubo muchos aplausos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the concert, there was a lot of applause.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El partido fue aplazado por la lluvia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The game was postponed because of the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta regla aplica a todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This rule applies to everyone.

definitions.note: Often used for software (“app”), but can also mean an application (e.g., for a job or school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Descargué una aplicación para aprender español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I downloaded an app to learn Spanish.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who works diligently, especially in school or at a task.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es muy aplicado y siempre hace la tarea a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very hardworking and always does his homework on time.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (to apply to) or “para” (to apply for).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a aplicar para ese trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to apply for that job.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), third-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La enfermera aplicó la vacuna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurse applied the vaccine.

definitions.native: to take possession of, to seize
definitions.note: Often used with “de” (apoderarse de algo) to mean taking control or possession of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los rebeldes intentaron apoderarse de la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rebels tried to seize the city.

definitions.native: to take over, to take control
definitions.note: Can also be used for feelings or ideas that “take over” someone (apoderarse de alguien).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El miedo se apoderó de él en la oscuridad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fear took over him in the darkness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy apostando cinco euros a que gana el equipo rojo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m betting five euros that the red team will win.

definitions.note: Often used with "por" (to bet on something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a apostar por nuestro equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to bet on our team.

definitions.note: From the verb "apoyar". Often used for supporting a person, idea, or plan.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella apoya a su amiga en todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She supports her friend in everything.

definitions.note: Often used with “en” to mean “leaning against/on” (e.g., apoyado en la pared).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy apoyado en la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m leaning against the wall.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they/you all support).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigos me apoyan cuando tengo problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends support me when I have problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a apoyar tu idea en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to support your idea in the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes apoyar la bicicleta contra la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can lean the bike against the wall.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigos me apoyaron durante el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends supported me during the exam.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “apoyar”; also used for formal commands (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me apoye en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you support me in the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te apoyo en todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I support you in everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tu apoyo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for your support.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/it supported/helped.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella apoyó a su amiga cuando lo necesitaba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She supported her friend when she needed it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella aprecia mucho tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She really appreciates your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apreciamos tu ayuda con el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We appreciate your help with the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigos aprecian mucho tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends really appreciate your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprecio mucho tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really appreciate your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprecio mucho tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really appreciate your help.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (usted/él/ella) or affirmative command for usted ("Learn!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que usted aprenda español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to learn Spanish.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, ustedes form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que aprendan mucho este semestre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you learn a lot this semester.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú). Often used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es importante que…”, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que aprendas español conmigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to learn Spanish with me.

definitions.note: Also used for commands (informal): “learn!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana aprende español en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister learns Spanish at school.

definitions.note: Used with vosotros/vosotras (plural “you”) in Spain; present imperative (command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprended estas palabras para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Learn these words for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En clase aprendemos español todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In class we learn Spanish every day.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “aprender” (used for “they” and also “you all” in Latin America).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños aprenden rápido en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids learn quickly at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero aprender español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to learn Spanish.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it will learn) or formal you (usted) will learn.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella aprenderá español este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will learn Spanish this year.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprenderás mucho si practicas todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will learn a lot if you practice every day.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprendes rápido cuando practicas todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You learn quickly when you practice every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He aprendido mucho este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have learned a lot this year.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "aprender"; used for actions in progress (often with "estar").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy aprendiendo español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am learning Spanish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprendieron español en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They learned Spanish at school.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 1st person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer aprendimos mucho en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we learned a lot in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El aprendiz trabaja con su maestro todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apprentice works with his master every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El aprendizaje de un idioma toma tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Learning a language takes time.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she/you (formal) learned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprendió a nadar el verano pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She learned to swim last summer.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of “aprender”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprendo español todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learn Spanish every day.

definitions.note: Used with vos (voseo): present imperative in parts of Latin America (especially Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprendé estas palabras para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Learn these words for the exam.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer aprendí a cocinar arroz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I learned to cook rice.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su salida fue apresurada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her departure was hurried.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salió apresuradamente de la casa al escuchar el ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left the house hurriedly when he heard the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomamos una decisión apresurada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We made a hurried decision.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive form “apresurarse” meaning “to hurry up.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me apresuré para no llegar tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hurried so I wouldn’t arrive late.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “he/she/you (formal) hurried.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se apresuró para no llegar tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She hurried so as not to arrive late.

definitions.note: Informal singular command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apresúrate, que ya es tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hurry up, it's already late.

definitions.note: Feminine form of “apretado”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tapa está muy apretada y no puedo abrirla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lid is very tight and I can’t open it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos zapatos están muy apretados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are very tight.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los zapatos están demasiado apretados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoes are too tight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que apretar el tornillo con esta llave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to tighten the screw with this wrench.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella apretó el botón y la máquina empezó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She pressed the button and the machine started.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos dimos un apretón de manos al conocernos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We shook hands when we met.

definitions.note: Also used as an informal command (tú): “tighten/squeeze/press!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprieta el tornillo con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tighten the screw carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que comer aprisa porque ya nos vamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to eat quickly because we're leaving now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito tu aprobación para hacer el cambio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need your approval to make the change.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El presupuesto ya está aprobado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The budget is already approved.

definitions.note: Commonly used for tests or classes (e.g., “He aprobado el examen”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡He aprobado el examen de español!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I passed the Spanish exam!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito aprobar el examen de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to pass tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): used for a completed action in the past; commonly used for passing a class/exam or approving a proposal/law.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprobaron el examen final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They passed the final exam.

definitions.note: Future tense (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si estudia, aprobará el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he studies, he will pass the exam.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): first-person singular (“I”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprobé el examen de matemáticas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I passed the math exam.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “he/she/you (formal) approved/passed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor aprobó el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher approved the exam.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa ropa no es apropiada para el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That clothing is not appropriate for work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese lenguaje no es apropiado para una reunión de trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That language is not appropriate for a work meeting.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present (also used for commands like “Take advantage!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprovecha el tiempo y termina la tarea hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take advantage of the time and finish the homework today.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ando form), often used like “while taking advantage (of)” or “by making use (of)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy aprovechando el tiempo para estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking advantage of the time to study.

definitions.native: to take advantage (of), to make use (of)
definitions.note: Often used for taking advantage of an opportunity, time, or resource (usually in a positive sense: to use well).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero aprovechar el tiempo y terminar mi tarea hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to make use of the time and finish my homework today.

definitions.native: I took advantage (of), I made use (of)
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 1st person singular: “I …”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aproveché el tiempo libre para estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took advantage of my free time to study.

definitions.native: took advantage of, made use of
definitions.note: simple past (pretérito) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprovechó la oportunidad y consiguió el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She took advantage of the opportunity and got the job.

definitions.note: Also used for estimating numbers (e.g., “aproxima el total”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren se aproxima a la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train approaches the station.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren se aproximaba a la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train was approaching the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El viaje dura aproximadamente dos horas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trip lasts approximately two hours.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “he/she/it approached; you (formal) approached.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro se aproximó a la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog approached the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella aprueba el examen final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She passes the final exam.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) affirmative command. Often used like “aprenderse” = to learn/memorize something by heart.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apréndete esta canción antes del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Learn (memorize) this song before the concert.

definitions.note: Often used with “para” to mean “suitable/qualified for” something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este lugar es apto para niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This place is suitable for children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él apuesta diez euros a que llueve mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bets ten euros that it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hice una apuesta con mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a bet with my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hicimos apuestas sobre quién ganaría el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We made bets on who would win the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apuesto que va a llover mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bet it’s going to rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El actor es muy apuesto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actor is very handsome.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella apunta al mapa para mostrar dónde estamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She points at the map to show where we are.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apunta mi número de teléfono, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write down my phone number, please.

definitions.note: Usually means notes you write down to study or remember information (e.g., class notes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Me pasas tus apuntes de la clase?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you send me your class notes?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apunté tu número en mi teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote down your number in my phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apuntó mi número en su cuaderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wrote down my number in his notebook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apuntó la linterna hacia la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He aimed the flashlight toward the door.

definitions.note: Often used with estar to describe someone who is short on time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy apurado; tengo que salir ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm in a hurry; I have to leave now.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “en apuros” (“in trouble” / “in a tight spot”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy en un apuro y necesito ayuda.
