definitions.note: Used for the person in command (e.g., on a ship, in the military, or as the leader of a sports team).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El capitán del equipo habló con el árbitro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team captain spoke with the referee.

definitions.note: Often used for capturing something (e.g., a person, an image/screenshot, or a signal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía anunció la captura del sospechoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police announced the capture of the suspect.

definitions.note: Past participle of "capturar"; often used with "ser" (passive voice) or "haber" (perfect tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ladrón fue capturado por la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief was captured by the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía capturó al ladrón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police captured the thief.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los bomberos capturaron al perro que estaba atrapado en el pozo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The firefighters caught the dog that was trapped in the well.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía capturó al sospechoso ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police captured the suspect yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me puse la capucha porque hacía frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put my hood up because it was cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El capullo se abre y sale una mariposa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cocoon opens and a butterfly comes out.

definitions.note: Informal and offensive (common in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas capullo con tu hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be a jerk to your sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontramos capullos en las ramas del árbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found cocoons on the branches of the tree.

definitions.note: Often used for flower buds (capullos de flor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los capullos de las rosas se abren en primavera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rose buds open in spring.

definitions.note: Informal and insulting (commonly used in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas capullos; estamos intentando trabajar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be jerks; we’re trying to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leí el primer capítulo del libro anoche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the first chapter of the book last night.

definitions.note: Plural of "capítulo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro tiene diez capítulos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book has ten chapters.

definitions.note: Literary; it’s a conjunction, not the noun “car” (which in Spanish is “coche” or “carro”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No salí, car estaba lloviendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t go out, because it was raining.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo la cara fría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My face is cold.

definitions.note: Feminine form of “caro”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa es cara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontré un caracol en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a snail in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la lluvia, hay muchos caracoles en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, there are many snails in the garden.

definitions.note: Plural of “carácter”; often used for letters, symbols, or characters in text.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La contraseña debe tener al menos ocho caracteres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The password must have at least eight characters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las características de este teléfono son muy buenas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The features of this phone are very good.

definitions.note: Vulgar/strong profanity in many Spanish-speaking countries; use with caution.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Carajo, se me olvidaron las llaves!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn, I forgot my keys!

definitions.note: Vulgar slang (varies by country). Often used in exclamations like “¡carajo!” or in phrases like “al carajo” (“to hell with it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Carajo! Se me olvidaron las llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn! I forgot my keys.

definitions.note: Vulgar slang. Often used in exclamations like “¡Qué carajos…!” or “¿Qué carajos…?” to add strong anger or emphasis.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué carajos estás haciendo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What the hell are you doing?

definitions.note: An exclamation showing surprise, annoyance, or emphasis; often a mild substitute for stronger swear words.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Caramba! Se me olvidó la cartera en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow! I forgot my wallet at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré un caramelo para mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a candy for my sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré caramelos para los niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought candies for the kids.

definitions.note: Plural of “cara” (noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Veo muchas caras en la foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see many faces in the photo.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las entradas son muy caras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tickets are very expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos una caravana de camellos en el desierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a caravan of camels in the desert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Una caravana de coches cruzó la ciudad lentamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A caravan of cars crossed the city slowly.

definitions.note: In Spain, this meaning is common for a towed camper trailer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dormimos en la caravana cerca de la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We slept in the camper near the beach.

definitions.note: Mild exclamation (surprise, annoyance, emphasis); less strong than many swear words.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Caray, qué rápido pasó el tiempo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow, how quickly time passed!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El carbono es un elemento esencial para la vida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Carbon is an essential element for life.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En invierno, algunas casas todavía se calientan con carbón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter, some houses are still heated with coal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soltó una carcajada cuando escuchó el chiste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He let out a burst of laughter when he heard the joke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cardenal habló en la misa del domingo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cardinal spoke at Sunday Mass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los cardenales se reunieron en el Vaticano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cardinals met at the Vatican.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo cardenales en el brazo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have bruises on my arm.

definitions.note: Often used in medical contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tuvo un problema cardíaco y fue al hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had a heart problem and went to the hospital.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; used for groups of people or things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los pacientes cardíacos deben evitar el estrés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cardiac patients should avoid stress.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” (carecer de + noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este informe carece de detalles importantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This report lacks important details.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) of “carecer”; it’s usually used with “de” (e.g., “carecer de + noun”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muchos hogares carecen de agua potable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many households lack drinking water.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all lacked). Often used with "de" (e.g., "carecer de algo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En ese momento, carecían de información suficiente para decidir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At that moment, they lacked enough information to decide.

definitions.note: Often used for something heavy you carry or transport; also used for an amount a device (like a phone) can hold (a charge).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La carga del camión es muy pesada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck’s load is very heavy.

definitions.note: Present tense (he/she/it “loads”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi teléfono carga muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone loads/charges very fast.

definitions.note: Present tense (he/she/it “charges”), often used for charging a device or a battery.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La batería no carga bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The battery doesn’t charge well.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), for ongoing/repeated actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, siempre cargaba mi mochila al colegio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a kid, I always used to carry my backpack to school.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mochila está cargada y pesa mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The backpack is loaded and weighs a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El camión está cargado de cajas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck is loaded with boxes.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about a phone or battery having power.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi teléfono está cargado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone is charged.

definitions.note: Most commonly a device used to charge a phone or other battery-powered device.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito el cargador de mi teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need my phone charger.

definitions.note: Used for firearms; in many contexts people also say "cargador" for the whole clip/magazine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El policía revisó el cargador del arma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer checked the gun’s magazine.

definitions.note: Often used for a large load of goods (especially in transport by ship or plane).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cargamento llegó al puerto esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shipment arrived at the port this morning.

definitions.note: Often used for devices, apps, or files when something is in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La página está cargando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The page is loading.

definitions.note: Can describe physically carrying something (the -ing form of “to carry”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está cargando una caja pesada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She is carrying a heavy box.

definitions.note: Most commonly means putting things onto/into something (load). It also commonly means charging a battery/device (charge).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a cargar las maletas en el coche y luego cargar el móvil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to load the suitcases into the car and then charge my phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las cargas son muy pesadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The loads are very heavy.

definitions.note: Verb form of "cargar" (not the noun "cargo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cargo las cajas en el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I load the boxes into the car.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or work contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tiene un cargo importante en la empresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has an important position in the company.

definitions.note: Often refers to jobs or roles with responsibilities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay dos cargos disponibles en la empresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two positions available in the company.

definitions.note: Common in banking or bills (extra costs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El banco me cobró cargos por el servicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bank charged me fees for the service.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cargue el teléfono antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you charge the phone before leaving.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/it or you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El camión cargó la mercancía en una hora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck loaded the merchandise in an hour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La caridad es importante para ayudar a otras personas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Charity is important for helping other people.

definitions.note: Diminutive of “cara”; often used affectionately.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Qué carita tan linda tienes!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a cute little face you have!

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es muy caritativa con sus vecinos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very charitable with her neighbors.

definitions.note: Often used as a term of endearment (like “dear” or “sweetheart”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te tengo mucho cariño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of affection for you.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who shows affection (with words, hugs, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo es muy cariñoso con sus nietos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is very affectionate with his grandchildren.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En mi ciudad celebramos el carnaval en febrero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In my city we celebrate carnival in February.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No como carne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t eat meat.

definitions.note: Plural of "carne".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No comemos carnes rojas en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don't eat red meats at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un carnet para escribir mis ideas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a notebook to write my ideas.

definitions.note: Often used for an official card or document (e.g., student ID, library card, driving license).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito mi carnet de estudiante para entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need my student ID to get in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El carnicero corta la carne en trozos pequeños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The butcher cuts the meat into small pieces.

definitions.note: Commonly used for official ID (carné de identidad) or a membership/permit card (e.g., gym, library).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito mi carné de identidad para viajar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need my ID card to travel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este restaurante es muy caro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant is very expensive.

definitions.note: Used to address someone affectionately (like in letters or emails).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Querida Ana: gracias por tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear Ana: thank you for your help.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (also used for mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos zapatos son muy caros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are very expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dormimos en una carpa cerca del lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We slept in a tent near the lake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En este río hay mucha carpa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are a lot of carp in this river.

definitions.note: In Spain, “carpeta” commonly means a paper folder or binder; in many Latin American countries it can also mean “briefcase.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guarda los documentos en la carpeta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep the documents in the folder.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El carpintero hizo una mesa de madera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The carpenter made a wooden table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Corrí mi primera carrera de 5 kilómetros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran my first 5-kilometer race.

definitions.note: In this sense, it refers to a course of study at a university or college.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana estudia la carrera de medicina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is studying the medicine degree program.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiere cambiar de carrera y trabajar en tecnología.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She wants to change careers and work in technology.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchas carreras este fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many races this weekend.

definitions.note: Often used in the context of university studies (e.g., "carrera de medicina").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis hermanas estudian carreras diferentes en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sisters study different majors at the university.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomamos la carretera para llegar más rápido a la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took the highway to get to the city faster.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchas carreteras en esta región.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many roads in this region.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una carretilla para llevar la tierra al jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a wheelbarrow to carry the soil to the garden.

definitions.note: Used for a lane on a road or a marked lane/track for movement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conduce por el carril derecho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Drive in the right lane.

definitions.note: Often used for a shopping cart or a small cart; it can also mean a stroller in some places.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse la fruta en el carrito del supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the fruit in the supermarket cart.

definitions.note: Common in Latin America; in Spain, “coche” is more common for “car.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi carro está estacionado afuera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My car is parked outside.

definitions.note: Common in Latin America; in Spain, "coche" is more common for "car".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos carros en esta calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many cars on this street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escribí una carta a mi abuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote a letter to my grandmother.

definitions.note: Common in restaurants (especially in Spain) to mean the menu.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Me trae la carta, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring me the menu, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que escribir tres cartas hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to write three letters today.

definitions.note: Often refers to playing cards (naipes), but can also mean cards in general depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quieres jugar a las cartas?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to play cards?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pusieron un cartel en la puerta que dice “Cerrado”.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put a sign on the door that says “Closed.”

definitions.note: Often used to refer to a drug cartel.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó a varios miembros del cartel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested several members of the cartel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No encuentro mi cartera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't find my wallet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejé la cartera en el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left my purse in the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ten cuidado: hay un carterista en el metro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful: there’s a pickpocket on the subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el metro había varios carteristas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were several pickpockets on the subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cartero entrega el correo todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mail carrier delivers the mail every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La caja es de cartón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The box is made of cardboard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tiene un carácter muy fuerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a very strong personality.

definitions.note: Superlative of "caro" (expensive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese restaurante es carísimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That restaurant is very expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi casa está cerca de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My house is near the school.

definitions.note: Verb form of «casar» (often used as «casar(se)»).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez casa a Marta y Pablo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge marries Marta and Pablo today.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana está casada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is married.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis tías están casadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My aunts are married.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy casado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am married.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective (e.g., "Estoy casado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy casado desde 2018.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been married since 2018.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; also used for mixed-gender groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis padres están casados desde 1995.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents have been married since 1995.

definitions.note: Often used in Latin America for “wedding” (the ceremony).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El casamiento es el sábado a las cuatro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wedding is on Saturday at four.

definitions.note: Present tense, nosotros form. It can mean marrying each other ("we get married") or marrying someone ("we marry"), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos casamos en junio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got married in June.

definitions.note: From "casarse" (to get married).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se casan en junio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re getting married in June.

definitions.note: From "casar" meaning to marry someone (less common than "casarse").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez los casan esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge is marrying them this afternoon.

definitions.note: Often used in the reflexive form “casarse” to mean “to get married.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quieren casar en primavera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to marry in spring.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive form; often used in hypothetical sentences (e.g., after “si”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo me casara, invitaría a toda mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I got married, I would invite my whole family.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun “me” (to get married myself / to marry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero casarme el año que viene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to get married next year.

definitions.note: reflexive: “to get married” (literally “to marry ourselves”); often used with another verb like “querer” or “pensar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queremos casarnos en junio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to get married in June.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se casaron en abril.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They got married in April.

definitions.note: Reflexive: casarse con = to marry (someone) / to get married to (someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos vamos a casar el próximo año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to get married next year.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; usually used as “casarse con” (to marry / get married to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos vamos a casar el próximo año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to get married next year.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the reflexive pronoun “te” (= yourself/you), used when talking to someone (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quieres casarte conmigo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to get married to me?

definitions.note: Future tense (él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María se casará en junio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María will get married in June.

definitions.note: Future tense (yo). Often used with "me" for "I will get married" (me casaré).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me casaré el próximo año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will get married next year.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “casar.” Often used in formal contexts meaning to marry someone (e.g., a priest marrying a couple).

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "comprar"; often used in hypothetical or dependent clauses (e.g., after "si").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo comprara un coche, viajaría más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I bought a car, I would travel more.

definitions.native: to buy (something) for him, her, you (formal)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to/for him, to/for her, or to/for you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a comprarle un regalo a mi mamá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to buy my mom a gift.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached ("it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a comprarlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to buy it tomorrow.

definitions.note: This form includes the indirect object pronoun “me” (“for me/to me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes comprarme un café?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you buy me a coffee?

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): “they bought” / “you all bought” (Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer compraron pan y leche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they bought bread and milk.

definitions.note: Reflexive form of "comprar"; it often implies buying something for yourself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me voy a comprar un coche nuevo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to buy myself a new car.

definitions.note: Direct-object pronoun + indirect-object pronoun attached to the infinitive: comprar + te.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero comprarte un regalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to buy you a gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana compraré pan y leche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will buy bread and milk.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (used for polite requests or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo lo compraría, pero no tengo dinero ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would buy it, but I don’t have money right now.

definitions.note: Plural form of “compra.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hice las compras esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did the shopping this morning.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present tense of “comprar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué compras en el supermercado?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you buy at the supermarket?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), tú form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Compraste pan para el desayuno?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you buy bread for breakfast?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo) of "comprar"; also the formal command (usted) "buy".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que yo compre pan hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I buy bread today.

definitions.note: Usually the formal command (usted) form: “(you) understand.” It can also be present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, comprenda mi situación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please understand my situation.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present (also used for formal “you”: usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella comprende la lección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She understands the lesson.

definitions.note: Used to talk about what something contains or covers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El precio comprende el desayuno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price includes breakfast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No comprendemos la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t understand the question.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “comprender”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos no comprenden la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They don’t understand the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo comprender por qué está tan enojado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't understand why he is so angry.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun "lo" (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprenderlo antes de tomar una decisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to understand it before making a decision.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Comprendes la pregunta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you understand the question?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Has comprendido la pregunta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you understood the question?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/you (formal) understood.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finalmente comprendió la lección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Finally, he understood the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No comprendo la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand the question.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "comprender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por fin comprendí la lección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finally understood the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu explicación fue clara y comprensible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your explanation was clear and understandable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tu comprensión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your understanding.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "comprar"; also used as the negative informal command "don’t buy".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que compres pan hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you buy bread today.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of "comprar" ("I buy").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compro pan todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy bread every day.

definitions.note: Past participle of "comprobar"; often used as an adjective meaning something has been confirmed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El billete ya está comprobado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket has already been checked.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “comprobar” (often used with “estar” to mean “is/are checking”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy comprobando la información antes de enviarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m checking the information before sending it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a comprobar si la puerta está cerrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to check if the door is closed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El técnico comprobó la conexión antes de irse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The technician checked the connection before leaving.

definitions.note: Often used for being committed to a relationship, goal, or responsibility.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está comprometida con su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is committed to her work.

definitions.note: Used for being engaged to be married.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María está comprometida y se casa en junio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María is engaged and is getting married in June.

definitions.note: Often used for being dedicated to a person, relationship, cause, or responsibility.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy comprometido con mi trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am committed to my work.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: «se comprometió» = “(he/she) committed (himself/herself) / promised.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se comprometió a estudiar todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He committed to studying every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El error comprometió la seguridad del sistema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mistake compromised the system’s security.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un compromiso con mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a commitment to my family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo ir porque tengo otros compromisos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't go because I have other commitments.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprueba tu correo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Check your email, please.

definitions.note: Voseo imperative (informal) used in countries like Argentina and Uruguay; equivalent to “compra (tú)” / “buy!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprá pan, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Buy bread, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular: “I bought.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer compré pan en la panadería.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I bought bread at the bakery.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), third person singular (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella compró pan esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She bought bread this morning.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La palabra está compuesta de cinco letras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The word is made up of five letters.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” (compuesto de) to say what something is made up of.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El comité está compuesto de cinco personas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The committee is made up of five people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene un comportamiento compulsivo con las compras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has compulsive behavior with shopping.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "componer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El compositor compuso una canción nueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The composer composed a new song.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un computador para hacer la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a computer to do my homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi computadora está en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My computer is on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchas computadoras en la oficina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many computers in the office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la oficina hay muchos computadores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the office there are many computers.

definitions.note: Often used in music to talk about rhythm or musical time (meter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sigue el compás con las palmas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow the rhythm by clapping your hands.

definitions.note: Tool used to draw circles; in Spanish, the navigation instrument is usually "brújula".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dibuja un círculo con el compás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw a circle with the compass.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú): "Behave!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compórtate en clase, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Behave in class, please.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos intereses comunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have common interests.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La comunicación es clave en un buen equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Communication is key in a good team.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “comunicar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos se comunican por correo electrónico todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They communicate by email every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comunicar esta información al equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to communicate this information to the team.

definitions.native: to communicate with someone, to get in touch
definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun “me” (= “to me / with me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes comunicarme la información por correo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can send me the information by email.

definitions.note: Reflexive form: emphasizes communicating with someone (often “to get in touch”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me comuniqué con mi profesora por correo electrónico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I communicated with my teacher by email.

definitions.note: Often used with “con” to mean “to communicate with” someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante comunicarse con el médico si tienes síntomas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to communicate with the doctor if you have symptoms.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta comunidad es muy acogedora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This community is very welcoming.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchas comunidades en esta ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many communities in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El comunismo fue muy influyente en la política del siglo XX.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Communism was very influential in 20th-century politics.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo era comunista en su juventud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather was a communist in his youth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el siglo XX, muchos comunistas fueron perseguidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the 20th century, many communists were persecuted.

definitions.note: Used with vos (voseo): affirmative imperative (command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comé despacio, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eat slowly, please.

definitions.note: Used with vosotros/vosotras (informal plural “you” in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿A qué hora coméis hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What time do you eat today?

definitions.note: Common in voseo (used in Argentina, Uruguay, and parts of Central America); equivalent to “tú comes.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no comés ahora, vas a tener hambre después.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t eat now, you’ll be hungry later.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), 1st person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer comí una manzana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ate an apple.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, comía cereal todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to eat cereal every morning.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all were eating).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegué, comían en la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, they were eating in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un error común.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a common mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comúnmente llego a casa a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually get home at six.

definitions.note: Means “with” (not the English verb “to con,” meaning to trick).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy con mis amigos al cine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the movies with my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es difícil concebir una vida sin internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to imagine a life without the internet.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jefe le concedió un día libre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss granted him a day off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito concentración para estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need concentration to study.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este jugo está muy concentrado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This juice is very concentrated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy concentrado en el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m focused on the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito concentrar mi atención en el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to concentrate my attention on the exam.

definitions.note: Reflexive form (“me” = myself): to concentrate (myself), to focus.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito concentrarme para estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to concentrate to study.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; often used with “en” (concentrarse en algo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito concentrarme en mi tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to concentrate on my assignment.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an object pronoun: "-te" = "yourself" (informal "you"). Often used with "en" (e.g., "concentrarte en...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas concentrarte en la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to concentrate on the task.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entiendo el concepto de la gravedad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't understand the concept of gravity.

definitions.note: Plural of “concepto”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprendimos nuevos conceptos en la clase de ciencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We learned new concepts in science class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontré una concha en la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a shell on the beach.

definitions.note: Usually refers to seashells.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontré conchas en la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found shells on the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo la conciencia tranquila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a clear conscience.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression «en lo que concierne a…» (“as far as … is concerned”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eso no me concierne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That doesn't concern me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos al concierto esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We're going to the concert tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este verano hay muchos conciertos en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This summer there are many concerts in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a concluir la reunión a las cinco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to conclude the meeting at five.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al final del informe, escribimos las conclusiones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the report, we wrote the conclusions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi conclusión es que necesitamos más tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My conclusion is that we need more time.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La reunión concluyó a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting concluded at six.

definitions.note: Used to say something is in agreement or consistent with something else (often with "con" or "en").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His story doesn’t match the facts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Concuerdo contigo en que es una buena idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agree with you that it’s a good idea.

definitions.note: Often used for competitions with an evaluation or selection process (e.g., talent contests, job openings, grants).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana ganó un concurso de fotografía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister won a photography contest.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) meaning “focus (yourself).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Concéntrate en la tarea, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Focus on the task, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi familia vive en un condado rural.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My family lives in a rural county.

definitions.note: A male noble title; feminine is "condesa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El conde vive en un castillo antiguo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The count lives in an old castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez dictó una condena de cinco años de prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge handed down a five-year prison sentence.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa está condenada y no se puede entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is condemned and you can’t go in.

definitions.note: Often used for a person who has been found guilty in court.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El hombre condenado irá a prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The convicted man will go to prison.

definitions.note: Can be used more generally to mean “doomed” or, in religious contexts, “damned.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos condenados si no encontramos ayuda pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are doomed if we don’t find help soon.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (e.g., being sentenced to prison).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue condenado a diez años de prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was sentenced to ten years in prison.

definitions.note: Can be used more generally to mean strongly criticized or doomed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El edificio fue condenado por ser peligroso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building was condemned for being dangerous.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): refers to a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los jueces condenaron al acusado a cinco años de prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judges sentenced the defendant to five years in prison.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/it/you formal) of “condenar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez lo condenó a cinco años de prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge sentenced him to five years in prison.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La condesa vive en un castillo antiguo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The countess lives in an old castle.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Spanish, the conditional mood is used to talk about hypothetical situations.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accept the conditions of the contract.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una condición médica que requiere tratamiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a medical condition that requires treatment.

definitions.note: Often used in plural (condiciones) for the terms of an agreement or offer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa aceptó las condiciones del contrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company accepted the terms of the contract.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural in Spanish, especially when offering sympathy after someone dies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te doy mis condolencias por la muerte de tu abuelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I offer you my condolences for the death of your grandfather.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré condones en la farmacia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought condoms at the pharmacy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La conducción bajo la lluvia puede ser peligrosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Driving in the rain can be dangerous.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts, especially for leading or managing a process or group (e.g., la conducción de un proyecto).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La conducción del proyecto fue excelente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The management of the project was excellent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana conduce al trabajo todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister drives to work every day.

definitions.note: Present tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos conducen al trabajo todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They drive to work every day.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conduces muy rápido en la autopista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You drive very fast on the highway.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have driven home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy conduciendo al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am driving to work.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conducimos al trabajo todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drive to work every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Sabes conducir?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su conducta en clase fue excelente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior in class was excellent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El conductor del autobús maneja con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus driver drives carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los conductores esperan en el semáforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drivers wait at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conducía despacio porque estaba lloviendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was driving slowly because it was raining.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “conducir” (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer conduje hasta la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I drove to the beach.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "conducir"; often used after expressions like "quería que", "era importante que", or in "si" clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era importante que ella condujera despacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was important that she drove slowly.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Believe me, it wasn’t my intention.

definitions.note: Often used for raising children or animals.

definitions.note: Colloquial (especially in Spain).

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese cuadro es muy bonito.

definitions.note: Often appears with accent as “cuál” in questions/exclamations (e.g., “¿Cuál…?”).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus mejores cualidades son la paciencia y la honestidad.

definitions.note: Often used for jobs or roles; can also mean “skilled.”

definitions.note: Refers to a thing or choice; often used in phrases like “cualquier cosa”.

definitions.note: Usually written with an accent as “cuán”. It’s used in exclamations or indirect questions (not in direct questions, where “cuánto” is common).

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations (often written with an accent as “cuánto”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does this book cost?

definitions.note: Often written with an accent (cuánto) in direct or indirect questions/exclamations: ¿Cuánto cuesta? / No sé cuánto cuesta.

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations. It can change for gender/number (cuánta, cuántos, cuántas).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does this book cost?
