definitions.note: Present tense form of "cuidar" (also used as the "usted" command: "Take care of...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cuida a su abuela todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She takes care of her grandmother every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Cuidado! Hay un coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out! There’s a car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tu cuidado cuando estaba enfermo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your care when I was sick.

definitions.note: Often used as a warning (especially in "¡Cuidado!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Cuidado! El suelo está mojado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful! The floor is wet.

definitions.note: Past participle of "cuidar"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He cuidado a mi hermana toda la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have taken care of my sister all afternoon.

definitions.note: Plural of "cuidado"; often used in phrases like "tener cuidados" (to take care) or "con cuidados" (with care).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tus cuidados durante mi enfermedad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your care during my illness.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es muy cuidadosa con los detalles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very careful with details.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lee las instrucciones cuidadosamente antes de empezar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Read the instructions carefully before you start.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who pays attention to details or avoids mistakes/accidents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sé cuidadoso cuando cruces la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful when you cross the street.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los conductores son muy cuidadosos en esta carretera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drivers are very careful on this road.

definitions.native: we take care of, we look after
definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros/nosotras).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuidamos a los niños mientras sus padres trabajan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We take care of the children while their parents work.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "cuidar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos cuidan a sus abuelos los fines de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They take care of their grandparents on the weekends.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "cuidar"; used to talk about an ongoing action ("while taking care of...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy cuidando a mi hermano esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking care of my brother this afternoon.

definitions.native: to take care of, to look after
definitions.note: Often used with "de" (cuidar de + person/thing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que cuidar de mi hermano esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take care of my brother this afternoon.

definitions.native: took care of, would take care of
definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form; often used after phrases like “quería que…” or “si…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que ella cuidara a los niños esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted her to take care of the kids this afternoon.

definitions.native: we will take care of, we will look after
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuidaremos a tu perro mientras estás de viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will take care of your dog while you are traveling.

definitions.native: to take care of him, to look after him/it
definitions.note: "-lo" is a direct object pronoun meaning "him" or "it" (masculine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito cuidarlo esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to take care of him this afternoon.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun “me” (“myself”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito cuidarme más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to take better care of myself.

definitions.native: to take care of us, to look after us
definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun “nos” (us).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que cuidarnos más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to take better care of ourselves.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used for self-care or being careful (e.g., "Cuídate").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que cuidarte si quieres sentirte mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to take care of yourself if you want to feel better.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun “te” attached (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero cuidarte cuando estés enfermo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to take care of you when you’re sick.

definitions.native: will take care of, will look after
definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal "you" (usted) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cuidará a los niños esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will take care of the children tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuidaré a tu perro este fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will take care of your dog this weekend.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for hypothetical situations or polite offers).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo cuidaría a tu perro este fin de semana si lo necesitas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would take care of your dog this weekend if you need it.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo) or formal command (usted) of "cuidar."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cuide bien a su hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you take good care of your sister.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for formal commands with ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que cuiden a su abuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's important that you take care of your grandmother.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of “cuidar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo cuido a mi hermana después de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take care of my sister after school.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer cuidé a mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I took care of my sister.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/it took care of; you (formal) took care of.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cuidó a su hermano pequeño toda la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She took care of her little brother all afternoon.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/it looked after; you (formal) looked after.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abuelo cuidó a los niños mientras yo trabajaba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Grandpa looked after the kids while I was working.

definitions.note: Vulgar/informal word.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Siéntate en el culo y deja de quejarte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit on your butt and stop complaining!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No fue mi culpa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It wasn’t my fault.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento mucha culpa por lo que dije.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of guilt about what I said.

definitions.note: From the verb «culpar». It can also be used as an informal command (tú): «¡Culpa a...!» = “Blame ...!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él siempre culpa a los demás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always blames others.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sintió mucha culpabilidad después de mentir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt a lot of guilt after lying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él se siente culpable por lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He feels guilty about what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía ya encontró al culpable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police already found the culprit.

definitions.note: Past participle of "culpar"; often used in passive constructions with "ser".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue culpado por el accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was blamed for the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me culpes por tu error.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't blame me for your mistake.

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun “me” is attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedes culparme por lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can't blame me for what happened.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): third-person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Culparon al árbitro por la derrota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They blamed the referee for the loss.

definitions.note: Direct-object pronoun "te" is attached to the verb (common with infinitives).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero culparte por lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to blame you for what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te culpo por lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't blame you for what happened.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she/it blamed; also used with usted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jefe culpó a Marta por el error.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss blamed Marta for the mistake.

definitions.note: Present tense form of «cultivar» (also used for the formal command «you grow/cultivate»).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela cultiva tomates en su jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandma grows tomatoes in her garden.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "cultivar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta granja cultivan tomates y pimientos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On this farm they grow tomatoes and peppers.

definitions.note: Often used for growing plants/crops; also used figuratively for developing a quality or relationship (e.g., ‘cultivar la paciencia’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis abuelos cultivan tomates en su jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents grow tomatoes in their garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cultivo tomates en mi jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I grow tomatoes in my garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cultivo de arroz necesita mucha agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rice cultivation needs a lot of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los cultivos necesitan agua y sol para crecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Crops need water and sun to grow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cultura de este país es muy diversa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The culture of this country is very diverse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La diversidad cultural es muy importante en esta ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cultural diversity is very important in this city.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchas diferencias culturales entre los dos países.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many cultural differences between the two countries.

definitions.note: Plural of “cultura”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta ciudad conviven muchas culturas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city, many cultures live together.

definitions.note: Often used for the top of a mountain; it can also mean the highest point of something in a more general sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegamos a la cumbre después de tres horas de caminata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached the summit after three hours of hiking.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “cumplir”. Often used after expressions of desire, necessity, or doubt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cumpla su promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he keeps his promise.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "cumplir"; often used after expressions like "espero que", "quiero que", "es importante que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cumplas tu promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you keep your promise.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "cumplir"; it can mean either "he/she/it" or "you" (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cumple todas sus promesas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He keeps all his promises.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy es mi cumpleaños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is my birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cumplen con todos los requisitos para el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They meet all the requirements for the job.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person who is responsible about arriving on time or meeting obligations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es muy cumplida; siempre llega a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very punctual; she always arrives on time.

definitions.note: Common with things like promises or goals (e.g., “una promesa cumplida”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue una promesa cumplida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a promise kept.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por el cumplido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for the compliment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He cumplido mi promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have fulfilled my promise.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ing form) of "cumplir"; used to talk about an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy cumpliendo mi promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fulfilling my promise.

definitions.note: Preterite tense. Can mean “they” (ellas/ellos) or formal “you plural” (ustedes), depending on the region/context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cumplieron la promesa que me hicieron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fulfilled the promise they made me.

definitions.note: Often used for following rules/laws (compliance) or carrying out a duty/requirement (fulfillment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa revisó el cumplimiento de las normas de seguridad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company reviewed compliance with the safety regulations.

definitions.note: Often used with obligations, promises, or requirements (e.g., cumplir una promesa, cumplir con la ley).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que cumplir mi promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to fulfill my promise.

definitions.native: to turn (an age), to have (a birthday)
definitions.note: Used to say someone reaches an age (e.g., cumplir 18 años).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana voy a cumplir 18 años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’m going to turn 18.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of “cumplir” (he/she/it will).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cumplirá su promesa mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will fulfill her promise tomorrow.

definitions.native: I will do, I will fulfill
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cumpliré mi promesa mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will keep my promise tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular preterite (simple past) of "cumplir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cumplió 18 años ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She turned 18 yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for fulfilling a duty/promise or meeting a requirement or goal (e.g., “cumplo 18 años” = “I turn 18”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy cumplo con mi trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I do my job (I fulfill my work duties).

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cumplí mi promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kept my promise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El bebé duerme en la cuna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby sleeps in the crib.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche se salió de la carretera y cayó en la cuneta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car went off the road and fell into the ditch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No existe una cura para ese virus todavía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There isn't a cure for that virus yet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico cura la herida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor heals the wound.

definitions.note: Often used for cured foods like cheese or ham; it can also mean someone has recovered/healed depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prefiero el queso curado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer cured cheese.

definitions.note: Past participle of “curar”; often used with “estar” to describe a healed wound or cured illness.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La herida ya está curada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound is already healed.

definitions.note: Often used for curing illnesses or healing wounds; also used for healing emotionally or in the sense of recovering.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico dice que esta medicina puede curar la infección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor says that this medicine can cure the infection.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used for someone recovering from an illness or injury.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me estoy curando de la gripe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m getting better from the flu.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) future tense of “curar” (to heal/cure).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico curará la herida con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor will heal the wound carefully.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es muy curiosa y siempre hace preguntas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very curious and always asks questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo curiosidad por saber qué pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m curious to know what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy curioso por saber qué pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm curious to know what happened.

definitions.note: Can be used negatively to describe someone who asks too many questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas tan curioso; es un asunto privado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't be so nosy; it's a private matter.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están curiosos por saber qué hay en la caja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are curious to know what’s in the box.

definitions.note: In Spanish it’s commonly used for the spice blend or a curry dish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a preparar pollo al curry para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to make curry chicken for dinner.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression “currículo (vitae)” to mean a résumé/CV.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Envié mi currículo para el puesto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent my résumé for the job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy tomando un curso de español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking a Spanish course.

definitions.note: Plural of "curso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este semestre estoy tomando tres cursos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This semester I’m taking three courses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La carretera tiene una curva peligrosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road has a dangerous curve.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La carretera tiene muchas curvas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road has many curves.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/it cured/healed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico curó la herida rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor healed the wound quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy cenamos cuscús con verduras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re having couscous with vegetables for dinner.

definitions.note: Often used for a protective case for an object (like a phone, instrument, or glasses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una custodia para mi teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a case for my phone.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “cuyo”; used to express possession (“whose”) and agrees with the thing possessed (not the owner).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conocí a una chica cuya hermana vive en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met a girl whose sister lives in Madrid.

definitions.note: Means “whose” in relative clauses and agrees with the noun it refers to (cuyo, cuya, cuyos, cuyas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conocí al chico cuyo padre es médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met the boy whose father is a doctor.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used to link something to its owner (e.g., “the students whose books…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conocí a los estudiantes cuyos libros están en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met the students whose books are on the table.

definitions.note: Used in questions (direct or indirect). It agrees in number: cuál (singular), cuáles (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuál prefieres?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which one do you prefer?

definitions.note: Plural form of "cuál"; used in questions and indirect questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuáles son tus libros favoritos?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which are your favorite books?

definitions.note: Formal or literary; often used before an adjective or adverb (e.g., “cuán importante”, “cuán rápido”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sabes cuán importante eres para mí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t know how important you are to me.

definitions.note: Used in direct or indirect questions and exclamations; it has an accent mark (cuándo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuándo empieza la clase?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When does the class start?

definitions.note: Feminine singular form, used with feminine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuánta agua necesitas?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much water do you need?

definitions.note: Feminine plural form (used with feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuántas personas vienen a la fiesta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How many people are coming to the party?

definitions.note: Feminine form; used with feminine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La física cuántica estudia el comportamiento de las partículas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Quantum physics studies the behavior of particles.

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations to ask about quantity or amount.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuánto cuesta este libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does this book cost?

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations to ask about quantity or price.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuánto cuesta este libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does this book cost?

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations to ask about an amount or quantity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuánto cuesta este libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does this book cost?

definitions.note: masculine plural form; used with masculine plural nouns or as a masculine plural pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuántos libros tienes?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How many books do you have?

definitions.native: tell him, tell her, tell them
definitions.note: Command (tú) form of "contar" used with the indirect object pronoun "le".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuéntale la verdad a tu hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell your sister the truth.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) with an indirect object pronoun (me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuéntame qué pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me what happened.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command form meaning “tell me it” (me + lo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entiendo la historia; cuéntamelo otra vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand the story; tell it to me again.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) with an indirect object pronoun: “us”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuéntanos qué pasó ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell us what happened yesterday.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuénteme qué pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me what happened.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú); reflexive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuídate mucho y llámame cuando llegues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take good care of yourself and call me when you arrive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi cuñado vive en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother-in-law lives in Madrid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito hacer algunos cálculos antes de comprar el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to do some calculations before buying the car.

definitions.note: In Spanish, this can also refer to the school/university subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la universidad, tuve que hacer cálculos y álgebra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In university, I had to do calculus and algebra.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noche está cálida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The night is warm.

definitions.note: Often used for weather, temperature, or a friendly/affectionate atmosphere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy es un día cálido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is a warm day.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los días aquí son cálidos en verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The days here are warm in summer.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) meaning “be quiet.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cállate y escucha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shut up and listen.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cálmate, todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calm down, everything is going to turn out fine.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command; literally “calm yourself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cálmate, todo va a estar bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calm down, everything is going to be fine.

definitions.note: Formal or plural command (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, cálmense y escuchen las instrucciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please calm down and listen to the instructions.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted); reflexive with “se”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Señor, cálmese, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sir, calm down, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una cámara para tomar fotos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a camera to take photos.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay cámaras de seguridad en la entrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are security cameras at the entrance.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with a reflexive pronoun; used to tell someone to change their clothes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hace frío; cámbiate antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold; change your clothes before going out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo tuvo cáncer, pero ahora está mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather had cancer, but now he is better.

definitions.note: Plural form of "cántaro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llenaron los cántaros con agua del pozo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They filled the pitchers with water from the well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomo una cápsula cada mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take a capsule every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo metieron en la cárcel por robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put him in prison for robbery.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command; reflexive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cásate conmigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marry me.

definitions.note: Often refers to the outer covering of a fruit/vegetable (peel) or an egg/nut (shell).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tira la cáscara del plátano a la basura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Throw the banana peel in the trash.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or written contexts; in everyday speech, "famoso/a" is very common too.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un autor célebre en toda España.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a famous author throughout Spain.

definitions.note: Plural of “célula”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El microscopio muestra las células con claridad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The microscope shows the cells clearly.

definitions.note: Often used for the “cent” part of the euro (céntimo de euro).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solo me faltan diez céntimos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only need ten cents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El césped del parque está muy verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grass in the park is very green.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dibuja un círculo en el papel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw a circle on the paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dibujé tres círculos en la pizarra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drew three circles on the board.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomamos un cóctel antes de la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a cocktail before dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito el código para abrir la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need the code to open the door.

definitions.native: pick it up, grab it, take it
definitions.note: Informal (tú) command with the object pronoun “lo” (“it”). In some countries (especially parts of Latin America), “coger” can be vulgar; “tomar” is often used instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cógelo del suelo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pick it up from the floor, please.

definitions.note: Also means “cholera” (a disease), but that meaning is less common in everyday conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sintió una cólera enorme cuando vio la mentira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt enormous anger when he saw the lie.

definitions.note: Affirmative tú command with the pronoun “te” (common in “comerse” to mean eating something up/entirely).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cómete la manzana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eat the apple up.

definitions.note: Plural of “cómic”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gustan los cómics de superhéroes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like superhero comics.

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations. The accent distinguishes it from “como” (“like/as”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cómo estás?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you?

definitions.note: Used to introduce an indirect question or an exclamation; it carries an accent (cómo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé cómo hacerlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know how to do it.

definitions.note: Can be confused with English “commode,” which often means a toilet.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse la ropa en la cómoda del dormitorio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the clothes in the bedroom dresser.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta silla es muy cómoda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chair is very comfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos sentamos cómodamente en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sat comfortably on the sofa.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estas sillas son muy cómodas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These chairs are very comfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este sofá es muy cómodo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sofa is very comfortable.

definitions.note: masculine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos zapatos son muy cómodos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are very comfortable.

definitions.note: Often used with "ser" (e.g., "ser cómplice de").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él fue cómplice del robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was an accomplice in the robbery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó al ladrón y a su cómplice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the thief and his accomplice.

definitions.note: Affirmative tú command + direct object pronoun (lo = it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cómpralo hoy si está en oferta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Buy it today if it’s on sale.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). It means “buy me (something)” or “buy it for me,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cómprame un café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Buy me a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). Reflexive: the buyer is also the beneficiary (for yourself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cómprate un abrigo para el invierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Buy yourself a coat for the winter.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). Often used to tell someone to cover up (for warmth, modesty, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hace frío; cúbrete con una chaqueta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold; cover yourself with a jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella me da un libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gives me a book.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past habitual/ongoing): can mean “was giving” or “used to give,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo me daba caramelos cuando era niño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather used to give me candies when I was a child.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past habitual/ongoing); also used for formal "you (plural)" in Spain (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos los días me daban un vaso de leche antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every day they gave me a glass of milk before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Usually used with nouns like “huellas” (fingerprints): “huellas dactilares”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía encontró huellas dactilares en la ventana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found fingerprints on the window.

definitions.note: Command form (vosotros) + object pronoun “me”. Used in Spain; in Latin America, “denme” is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dadme un minuto, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me a minute, please.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to something that is specified or assumed (e.g., “una fecha dada” = “a given date”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En un momento dado, todo cambió.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At a given moment, everything changed.

definitions.note: Used in the fixed expression “dado que” meaning “given that / since.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dado que está lloviendo, nos quedamos en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Given that it’s raining, we’re staying at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te he dado mi número de teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have given you my phone number.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tira los dados y avanza tres casillas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Roll the dice and move three squares.

definitions.note: Command form of “dar” with the indirect object pronoun “le” (“to him/her/you (formal)”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dale el libro a María, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give the book to María, please.

definitions.note: Very common informal expression used to encourage someone or tell them to start/continue.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Estás listo? ¡Dale!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you ready? Go ahead!

definitions.note: Command form (tú) used with an indirect object pronoun (les = “to them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dales las llaves ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give them the keys now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La dama llevaba un vestido rojo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lady was wearing a red dress.

definitions.note: Plural of "dama".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buenas tardes, damas y caballeros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) meaning “give me …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dame un vaso de agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me a glass of water, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te damos las gracias por tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We thank you for your help.

definitions.note: Can mean “they give” (ellos/ellas/ustedes) or “you all give” (vosotros, Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre dan buenos consejos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They always give good advice.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "dar"; often used with "estar" to express an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy dando una clase ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving a class now.

definitions.note: Affirmative tú command (imperative) of “dar” with the indirect object pronoun “nos” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danos un minuto, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give us a minute, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La danza es una parte importante de la cultura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dance is an important part of culture.

definitions.note: Used with the pronoun “os” (you all); common in Spain (vosotros form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Daos un abrazo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give each other a hug.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te doy mi palabra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I give you my word.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana daremos una respuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will give an answer.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (e.g., "te", "les") to say who receives it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te daremos un regalo por tu cumpleaños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will give you a gift for your birthday.

definitions.native: to give (to him, to her, to you [formal], to it)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to him/her/you [formal]/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero darle el libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to give him the book.

definitions.note: Direct/indirect object pronoun “les” can mean “to them” or “them,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a darles un regalo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to give them a gift tomorrow.

definitions.note: Infinitive of “dar” with the attached indirect object pronoun “me” (“to me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes darme un vaso de agua?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me a glass of water?

definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “nos” (= to us).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes darnos más tiempo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give us more time?

definitions.note: Used with “vosotros/vosotras” (Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero daros las gracias por vuestra ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to thank you for your help.

definitions.note: Often used to mean giving yourself something (like a break): “darse un descanso”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito darme un descanso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to give myself a break.

definitions.note: Usually appears in the phrase “darse cuenta (de)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al darse cuenta del problema, ella llamó a la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Upon realizing the problem, she called the police.

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun + indirect object pronoun attached to the infinitive: dar + te.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero darte un regalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to give you a gift.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it will give); also used for formal "you" (usted) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella me dará el libro mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will give me the book tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (ellos/ellas/ustedes) future tense of "dar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana darán una charla en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will give a talk at the university.

definitions.note: Second person singular (tú) in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana me darás tu respuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will give me your answer.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) future tense of "dar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te daré el libro mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will give you the book tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “dar”; used to talk about what someone would give in a hypothetical situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te daría mi asiento si estuvieras cansado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would give you my seat if you were tired.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (they/you all would give).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tuvieran más dinero, darían más a la caridad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they had more money, they would give more to charity.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present indicative form of "dar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me das tu número, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You give me your number, please.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) of "dar". Often used with a pronoun: "date" = "give yourself" (e.g., allow yourself, treat yourself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Date un descanso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give yourself a break.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un dato más para completar el formulario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need one more piece of information to complete the form.

definitions.note: Plural of "dato".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito más datos para tomar una decisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need more data to make a decision.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "dañar" (he/she/it damages).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El humo daña los pulmones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smoke damages the lungs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche está dañado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is damaged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El granizo puede dañar el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hail can damage the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El humo del cigarrillo es dañino para la salud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cigarette smoke is harmful to your health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El fuego causó mucho daño a la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire caused a lot of damage to the house.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche tiene daños en la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car has damage on the door.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “(he/she/it) damaged/harmed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tormenta dañó el techo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm damaged the roof.

definitions.note: Often used to express origin ("from") or possession/relationship ("of").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soy de México.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm from Mexico.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of «deber», often used after «que» to express necessity or obligation in an uncertain/subjective context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es posible que deba trabajar mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s possible that I may have to work tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato está debajo de la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is under the table.

definitions.native: we should, we ought to, we must
definitions.note: Commonly used with another verb in the infinitive (e.g., «debamos ir» = «we should go»).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debamos estudiar más para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should study more for the exam.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) form of the auxiliary verb “deber,” often used after expressions of advice, doubt, or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que debas estudiar más para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you should study more for the exam.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “deber” used after expressions of doubt, emotion, advice, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No creo que debas hacerlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't think you should do it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo un debate sobre el cambio climático en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a debate about climate change at the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a debatir este tema en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to debate this topic in class.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to express obligation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debe terminar la tarea hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: must finish the homework today.

definitions.note: From the verb "deber"; it expresses obligation or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debe estudiar para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She must study for the exam.

definitions.note: Also used to talk about owing money or a debt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me debe diez euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She owes me ten euros.

definitions.note: Used to express obligation or what is advisable; often followed by an infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debemos estudiar para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must (should) study for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debemos estudiar para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must study for the exam.

definitions.note: Used to talk about owing money or something to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debemos veinte euros al camarero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We owe the waiter twenty euros.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) form of "deber".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deben estudiar para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They must study for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mi deber ayudar a mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is my duty to help my family.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural (los deberes) to mean school homework.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchos deberes para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of homework for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Future tense form; often expresses obligation or a strong supposition about what will happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana deberá entregar el informe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will have to turn in the report.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) future tense, often used to express obligation or a strong assumption.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deberán terminar el proyecto antes del viernes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will have to finish the project before Friday.

definitions.note: Often used to give advice or make a polite suggestion (conditional form of "deber").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Creo que debería llamar a mi madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think I should call my mother.

definitions.note: Conditional form; often used to give advice or express what would be best.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deberías hablar con tu profesor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should talk to your teacher.

definitions.note: Conditional tense, 2nd person plural (vosotros/vosotras); mainly used in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deberíais estudiar más para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should study more for the exam.

definitions.note: Often used to express advice, obligation, or what would be the right thing to do.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deberíamos estudiar más para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should study more for the exam.

definitions.note: Conditional form often used to make suggestions or express what would be advisable.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deberíamos estudiar más para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should study more for the exam.

definitions.note: Conditional form; often used to make polite suggestions or express what would be advisable.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deberían estudiar más para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They should study more for the exam.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) form, often used to give advice or make a suggestion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deberías hablar con tu profesor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should talk with your teacher.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "deber"; often used to give advice or make a suggestion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deberías estudiar más para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should study more for the exam.

definitions.note: Informal “tú” form (you, singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debes estudiar para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must study for the exam.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present tense of “deber.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debes hacer tu tarea antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must/should do your homework before going out.

definitions.note: Past participle of "deber"; often used to mean that something is owed or due.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese dinero es debido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That money is owed.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “debido a” = “due to / because of.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pago está debido mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The payment is due tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) in the simple past; often expresses obligation or a strong conclusion about the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debieron salir temprano para llegar a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had to leave early to arrive on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su mayor debilidad es que se distrae fácilmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His greatest weakness is that he gets distracted easily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos tenemos debilidades, pero podemos trabajar en ellas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We all have weaknesses, but we can work on them.

definitions.native: we had to, we were supposed to
definitions.note: Past (preterite) form of "deber" used to express obligation in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debimos salir temprano para llegar a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had to leave early to arrive on time.

definitions.note: Used to express what someone was expected to do in the past (tú form).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to leave them here.

definitions.native: to leave me, to let me
definitions.note: Object pronoun "me" = "me" is attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes dejarme en paz?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you leave me alone?

definitions.note: Object pronoun "nos" can mean "us" or "ourselves" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes dejarnos en paz, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you leave us alone, please?

definitions.native: they left, they let, they allowed
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): third person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejaron las llaves en la mesa y se fueron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left the keys on the table and left.

definitions.native: to let oneself, to allow oneself
definitions.note: Often used with adjectives or passive ideas (e.g. dejarse llevar = to let oneself be carried away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es fácil dejarse llevar por la emoción.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s easy to let yourself be carried away by emotion.

definitions.native: to leave you, to let you
definitions.note: Direct object pronoun "te" = "you" (informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero dejarte solo en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to leave you alone at home.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) future tense of “dejar” (to leave, to let).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana dejará las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) future tense of “dejar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana dejarán el coche en el garaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will leave the car in the garage.

definitions.native: I will leave, I will let
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te dejaré un mensaje después de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will leave you a message after the meeting.

definitions.native: would leave, would let, would allow
definitions.note: Conditional form of “dejar.” Often used for polite requests or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo no lo dejaría entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wouldn’t let him in.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (they/you all formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tuvieran tiempo, dejarían a los niños en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they had time, they would leave the kids at home.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) present tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué dejas la puerta abierta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you leave the door open?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form; often used in sentences like “if (someone) left/let …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me dejase en paz, estaría más tranquilo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he left me alone, I’d be calmer.

definitions.native: you left, you let, you allowed
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of "dejar" for "tú".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejaste las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No lo deje aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t leave it here, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive used as a “let’s …” (nosotros) command/suggestion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejemos esto para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s leave this for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes) or formal command (ustedes) of "dejar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejen las maletas aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave the suitcases here, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) form of "dejar"; also used in negative commands (tú): "no dejes" = "don’t leave/let".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no dejes las llaves aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don’t leave the keys here.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo) of "dejar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejo las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Informal command form used with "vos" (common in Argentina/Uruguay).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejá eso aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave that here, please.

definitions.native: I left, I stopped (doing), I let
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) preterite form of “dejar” (past action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejé las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, used with "vosotros" (Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no dejéis la puerta abierta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don't leave the door open.

definitions.native: let's leave it, let's stop it
definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros) affirmative command (imperative) with the object pronoun “lo” = “it.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya es tarde; dejémoslo para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's already late; let's leave it for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “dejar” (he/she/you-formal left; it left).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejó las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Contraction of "de + el" (used before the masculine singular article "el").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tapa del libro es roja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cover of the book is red.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me pongo el delantal para cocinar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on the apron to cook.

definitions.note: Often used with "de": "delante de" = "in front of".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche está delante de la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is in front of the house.

definitions.note: Often used as “delante de” + noun/pronoun (“in front of”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche está delante de la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is in front of the house.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective; also commonly used in sports to refer to a forward (female) or the forward line.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevo una mochila en la parte delantera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I carry a backpack on the front part.

definitions.note: Used to describe something that is in the front (e.g., the front part/seat).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siéntate en el asiento delantero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit in the front seat.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/you (formal) reported someone; it often implies betraying someone’s trust.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella lo delató a la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reported him to the police.

definitions.note: Commonly used as a formal command (usted). It’s often written with an accent: «déle».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dele el dinero a María.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give the money to María.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La delegación llegó a la conferencia esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delegation arrived at the conference this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los delegados votaron a favor de la propuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delegates voted in favor of the proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos delfines cerca de la costa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw dolphins near the coast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos un delfín cerca de la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a dolphin near the beach.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es delgada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is thin.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las ramas delgadas se rompieron con el viento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thin branches broke in the wind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es muy delgado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very thin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo hizo deliberadamente para llamar la atención.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did it deliberately to get attention.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situación es delicada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is delicate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trató el tema con delicadeza para no herir a nadie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She handled the topic with delicacy so as not to hurt anyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ten cuidado con ese vaso; es muy delicado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful with that glass; it’s very delicate.

definitions.note: Often used for people or topics that require tact or can be easily upset.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un tema delicado, así que hablemos con calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a sensitive topic, so let’s talk calmly.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sopa está deliciosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is delicious.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las galletas son deliciosas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cookies are delicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este pastel está delicioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is delicious.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos tacos están deliciosos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These tacos are delicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La delincuencia ha aumentado en este barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Crime has increased in this neighborhood.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the criminal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó a los delincuentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the criminals.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Robbery is a crime.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía investiga varios delitos en el barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating several crimes in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts; in legal contexts it can also mean a lawsuit/claim.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La demanda de electricidad aumenta en verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The demand for electricity increases in the summer.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (to take someone to court).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa va a demandar al proveedor por incumplimiento de contrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is going to sue the supplier for breach of contract.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus demandas son muy claras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their demands are very clear.

definitions.note: Common in legal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa enfrenta varias demandas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is facing several lawsuits.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El trabajo demandó mucho tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The job demanded a lot of time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella demandó a la empresa por despido injustificado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sued the company for unfair dismissal.

definitions.note: feminine singular form; used with feminine singular nouns

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are too many people here.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; used before feminine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay demasiadas personas aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are too many people here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estás hablando demasiado rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re talking too fast.

definitions.note: As a determiner, it goes before a noun (e.g., “demasiado dinero”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes demasiado trabajo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have too much work today.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used with masculine plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay demasiados coches en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are too many cars on the street.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) form of “dar”. Often used with an indirect object pronoun like “me”, “le”, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deme un vaso de agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me a glass of water, please.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean “crazy” (can be insulting depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eso sería una idea demente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That would be an insane idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La democracia es importante para proteger los derechos de todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Democracy is important to protect everyone’s rights.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: España es una sociedad democrática.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spain is a democratic society.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elegimos un líder de manera democrática.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We chose a leader in a democratic way.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dicen que hay un demonio en esa casa vieja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They say there is a demon in that old house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dicen que hay demonios en esa casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They say there are demons in that house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo una demora en el vuelo por la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a delay in the flight because of the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que demos una buena impresión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope we give a good impression.

definitions.note: Often used for a public protest or for showing/proving something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo una demostración en la plaza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a demonstration in the square.

definitions.note: Past participle of "demostrar"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha demostrado que tiene razón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has shown that he is right.

definitions.native: to show, to demonstrate, to prove
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que demostrar que eres responsable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to show that you are responsible.

definitions.native: to prove it, to show it
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no me crees, puedo demostrarlo con pruebas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t believe me, I can prove it with evidence.

definitions.native: I will show, I will prove
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te demostraré que digo la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will prove to you that I’m telling the truth.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/it demonstrated; you (formal) demonstrated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella demostró que tenía razón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She proved that she was right.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “demostrar” (also used for formal “you” and for “he/she/it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este ejemplo demuestra la idea claramente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This example shows the idea clearly.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form (also used for the formal command “show/demonstrate”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que usted demuestre su identidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to show your identity.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll pay for the coffee, and the others will pay for the food.

definitions.note: Often used with a definite article: "los demás" = "the others/the rest".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los demás ya llegaron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The others have already arrived.

definitions.note: Often used with an article: «los demás» = “the others / everyone else.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los demás ya terminaron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The others have already finished.

definitions.note: Usually used with the article: "los/las demás".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los demás quieren ir al cine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The others want to go to the movies.

definitions.note: Used for “they give” in the present subjunctive, and also as a command for “you all (ustedes) give”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they give me the book tomorrow.

definitions.native: give him, give her, give it

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La densidad del agua es mayor que la del aceite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The density of water is greater than that of oil.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La niebla es muy densa hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fog is very dense today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana tengo una cita con el dentista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have an appointment with the dentist.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" ("dentro de") to mean "inside/within" a place or time period.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is inside the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato está dentro de la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is inside the house.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective, it agrees with a feminine noun (e.g., “pasta dentífrica”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new toothpaste.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se me acabó el dentífrico, así que voy a comprar más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran out of toothpaste, so I'm going to buy more.

definitions.note: Commonly used for reporting a crime or wrongdoing to the authorities.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reported him to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El departamento de ventas está en el segundo piso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sales department is on the second floor.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My apartment is small but comfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los departamentos de la empresa trabajan juntos en este proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company's departments work together on this project.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It depends on the day.

definitions.note: Present tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños dependen de sus padres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children depend on their parents.

definitions.note: Often used with “de”: “depender de” = “to depend on.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todo depende del clima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything depends on the weather.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is dependent on his parents.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need sportswear for the gym.
