definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a misfortune to miss the flight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desgraciadamente, no puedo ir a la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, I can't go to the party.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult meaning “wretched” or “bastard,” depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pobre hombre está desgraciado desde que perdió su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The poor man has been miserable since he lost his job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del accidente, la familia vivió muchas desgracias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the family went through many misfortunes.

definitions.note: Often used for undoing something that was done (like an action, a mistake, or a knot).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a deshacer el nudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to undo the knot.

definitions.note: Common in phrases like “deshacerse de” + noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito deshacerme de estas cajas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to get rid of these boxes.

definitions.note: Commonly used with "de" ("deshacerme de algo" = "get rid of something").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero deshacerme de esta ropa vieja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to get rid of these old clothes.

definitions.note: Commonly used with “de” + noun: “deshacernos de algo”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que deshacernos de esta ropa vieja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to get rid of these old clothes.

definitions.note: Often used with "de": "deshacerse de" + noun/pronoun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero deshacerme de esta ropa vieja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to get rid of these old clothes.

definitions.note: Commonly used with "de" ("deshacerte de algo" = "get rid of something").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que deshacerte de esas cosas viejas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to get rid of those old things.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú); used with reflexive pronoun “te.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deshazte de esa ropa vieja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get rid of those old clothes.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), 1st person singular: “I undid.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deshice el nudo con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I undid the knot carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La calle estaba desierta por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street was deserted at night.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it describes a place with no people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pueblo está desierto por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The town is deserted at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El desierto es muy caluroso durante el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The desert is very hot during the day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La desigualdad económica ha aumentado en los últimos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Economic inequality has increased in recent years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy desilusionado con los resultados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m disillusioned with the results.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño se deslizó por el tobogán.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy slid down the slide.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El vestido es deslumbrante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dress is dazzling.

definitions.native: to dismantle it, to take it apart
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a desmantelarlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to dismantle it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective meaning someone is unconscious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegué, él estaba desmayado en el suelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, he was passed out on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se desmayó en el autobús, pero ya está mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She fainted on the bus, but she’s better now.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está desnuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is naked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El bebé está desnudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby is naked.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños corren desnudos por la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids run naked on the beach.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/you (formal) did it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El enfermero desnudó al paciente para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurse undressed the patient for the exam.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La habitación está desocupada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is unoccupied.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está desocupada desde mayo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been unemployed since May.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who doesn't have a job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano está desocupado desde el mes pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother has been unemployed since last month.

definitions.note: In some regions, it can mean someone is available (not occupied).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy desocupado esta tarde, ¿quieres tomar un café?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m free this afternoon—do you want to have a coffee?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay mucho desorden en tu habitación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a lot of mess in your room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu habitación está desordenada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your room is messy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del accidente, estaba desorientado y no sabía dónde estaba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he was disoriented and didn't know where he was.

definitions.note: Often refers to a private office, like a lawyer’s or doctor’s office, or an office/room in a home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abogado me espera en su despacho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawyer is waiting for me in his office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habla despacio, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak slowly, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La despedida fue muy emotiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The farewell was very emotional.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" (e.g., "está despedido").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Juan está despedido desde ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Juan has been fired since yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about losing a job (being fired).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He sido despedido de mi trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been fired from my job.

definitions.note: Past participle of "despedir" in the sense of saying goodbye.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya nos hemos despedido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have already said goodbye.

definitions.note: Can mean either saying goodbye (despedirse) or dismissing/firing someone (despedir), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos despedimos al final de la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We said goodbye at the end of the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Despedimos a dos empleados la semana pasada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We fired two employees last week.

definitions.note: Often used for ending someone's employment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa decidió despedir a veinte empleados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company decided to fire twenty employees.

definitions.native: to say goodbye (to), to see off
definitions.note: Used when you part from someone or when you accompany someone as they leave.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fuimos a la estación para despedir a Marta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went to the station to say goodbye to Marta.

definitions.native: to fire him, to dismiss him
definitions.note: Refers to ending his employment; “-lo” means “him.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a despedirlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to fire him tomorrow.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an object pronoun: “despedir + me” = “say goodbye (to others) / take my leave.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que despedirme, ya es tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to say goodbye; it’s already late.

definitions.native: to say goodbye, to take leave
definitions.note: Reflexive verb: you say goodbye to someone (e.g., “despedirse de alguien”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que despedirme de mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to say goodbye to my friends.

definitions.note: This form includes the object pronoun “te” (you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero despedirte antes de irme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to say goodbye to you before I leave.

definitions.note: This form is 1st person singular, simple past (pretérito). It can mean saying goodbye (despedirse) or firing someone (despedir a alguien); context decides.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer me despedí de mis amigos en el aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I said goodbye to my friends at the airport.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: "despedí a + person".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Despedí a un empleado por llegar tarde todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fired an employee for arriving late every day.

definitions.note: Used for planes/rockets and also for things like stickers or tape coming unstuck (in that case, often "despegarse").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El avión va a despegar en diez minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane is going to take off in ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El avión despegará a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane will take off at eight.

definitions.note: Often used for aircraft; also used more generally for the start of rapid growth or improvement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El despegue del avión fue puntual.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane's takeoff was on time.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form; used for planes/rockets, or for starting suddenly (e.g., a career).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El avión despegó a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane took off at eight.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy la mente está despejada y puedo concentrarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today my mind is clear and I can concentrate.

definitions.note: Often used to describe the sky or the weather (e.g., "cielo despejado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy el cielo está despejado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the sky is clear.

definitions.note: Often used for clearing an area/space (e.g., a table, a room) or when the weather clears up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, despeja la mesa después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please clear the table after dinner.

definitions.note: Used as a command to more than one person (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, despejen la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please clear the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La despensa está llena de arroz y pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pantry is full of rice and pasta.

definitions.note: Often used for wasting time, money, food, or opportunities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero desperdiciar mi tiempo en eso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to waste my time on that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un desperdicio de comida tirar tanto pan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a waste of food to throw away so much bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya he despertado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already woken up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse el despertador a las seis para levantarme temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I set the alarm clock for six to get up early.

definitions.native: we wake up, we wake (someone) up
definitions.note: Can mean either “we wake up” (reflexive: despertarse) or “we wake (someone) up” (non-reflexive: despertar), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos despertamos temprano para ir al aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wake up early to go to the airport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy despertando y todavía tengo sueño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m waking up and I’m still sleepy.

definitions.note: Often used as "despertarse" when the subject wakes up (reflexive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suelo despertar a las siete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually wake up at seven.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero despertar al bebé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to wake the baby up.

definitions.native: woke up, were to wake up
definitions.note: Often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., after "si" meaning "if").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me despertara temprano, tendría más tiempo para desayunar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I woke up early, I would have more time for breakfast.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “me” (= me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que despertarme a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to wake me up at six.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used for waking up from sleep.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me despierto a las siete todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wake up at seven every day.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “te” (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a despertarte a las siete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to wake you up at seven.

definitions.note: Can also be used reflexively with “te” (“yourself/you”), meaning “to wake up.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito despertarte temprano para ir al aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need you to wake up early to go to the airport.

definitions.note: First-person singular, simple past (pretérito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me desperté temprano para ir al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up early to go to work.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) in the past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se despertó temprano para ir al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He woke up early to go to work.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "despedir"; used after expressions like "es posible que", "quiero que", etc. "Ustedes" is Latin America; "vosotros" is Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es posible que despidan a dos empleados esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s possible that they will fire two employees this week.

definitions.native: they fired, they said goodbye to
definitions.note: Can mean “they fired (someone)” or “they said goodbye / sent off (someone),” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A Juan lo despidieron ayer de la empresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fired Juan from the company yesterday.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite): “he/she/it said goodbye.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se despidió de sus amigos antes de irse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She said goodbye to his/her friends before leaving.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite): “he/she/it fired (someone).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa despidió a dos empleados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company fired two employees.

definitions.note: It can mean “(he/she/it) wakes up” (present) or an informal command “wake up!” (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María se despierta temprano todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María wakes up early every day.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana está despierta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is awake.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for formal commands with “usted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que usted se despierte temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you wake up early.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "despertar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que despiertes temprano mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you wake up early tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me despierto a las siete todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wake up at seven every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy despierto desde las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been awake since six o’clock.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están despiertos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are awake.

definitions.note: Often describes someone who is a bit forgetful or not paying attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy muy despistado hoy; se me olvidaron las llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm very absent-minded today; I forgot my keys.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with the pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Despiértame a las siete, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake me up at seven, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (él/ella/usted): it describes something/someone collapsing or falling suddenly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El techo se desplomó durante la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The roof collapsed during the storm.

definitions.note: Past participle of “despojar”; often used with “ser/estar” or in passive constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue despojado de sus pertenencias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was stripped of his belongings.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of “despreciar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él desprecia a sus compañeros de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He despises his classmates.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (could mean an ongoing past action or a habitual past action: “was …-ing” / “used to …”). Often confused with English “depreciate,” but it means “to despise.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era joven, despreciaba la comida picante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was young, I despised spicy food.

definitions.native: we despise, we look down on
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No despreciamos a nadie por su origen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t look down on anyone because of their background.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muchas personas desprecian a los demás sin conocerlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people despise others without knowing them.

definitions.native: to despise, to look down on
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No debes despreciar a las personas por su acento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn't look down on people because of their accent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo desprecio las mentiras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I despise lies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sintió desprecio por la mentira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt contempt for the lie.

definitions.note: Often written with an accent: “después”. It’s frequently used with “de” (después de + noun/verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después vamos a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Afterward we’re going home.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" ("después de" + noun/infinitive) to mean "after".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablamos después.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll talk later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese color destaca mucho en la pared blanca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That color stands out a lot on the white wall.

definitions.note: Past participle of "desterrar"; often used with "ser/estar" (e.g., "fue desterrado" = "was exiled").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El escritor fue desterrado por el gobierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The writer was exiled by the government.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ayuda está destinada a las familias con bajos ingresos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The aid is destined for families with low incomes.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta sala está destinada a reuniones y presentaciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This room is intended for meetings and presentations.

definitions.note: Often used with “a/para” to say what something is intended for (e.g., “destinado a/para…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este dinero está destinado a la educación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This money is intended for education.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos fondos están destinados a la educación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These funds are intended for education.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuál es tu destino final?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your final destination?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cree que el destino le tenía preparada una sorpresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He believes fate had a surprise in store for him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos varios destinos para elegir este verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have several destinations to choose from this summer.

definitions.note: Can refer to what happens to someone in life (their fate), not just a travel destination.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nadie conoce nuestros destinos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nobody knows our fates.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un destornillador para apretar este tornillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a screwdriver to tighten this screw.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas destreza para tocar el piano bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need skill to play the piano well.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean someone is very tired or emotionally devastated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del accidente, el coche quedó destrozado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the car was wrecked.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective to describe something badly damaged or ruined; can also describe a person feeling emotionally devastated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del accidente, el coche quedó destrozado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the car was wrecked.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; often used literally (physically ruined) or figuratively (emotionally devastated).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del accidente, los coches quedaron destrozados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the cars were wrecked.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "destrozar"; often used with "estar" to describe an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Están destrozando la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are destroying the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La destrucción del puente causó muchos problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The destruction of the bridge caused many problems.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (agrees with a feminine noun, often used with ser/estar or as an adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ciudad quedó destruida después del terremoto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city was left destroyed after the earthquake.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle; often used with "ser" for the passive voice or with "estar" to describe a state
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las casas fueron destruidas por el huracán.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The houses were destroyed by the hurricane.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective meaning something has been ruined or damaged completely.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del incendio, el edificio quedó destruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the fire, the building was left destroyed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El puente fue destruido por la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bridge was destroyed by the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El fuego puede destruir la casa en minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire can destroy the house in minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tormenta destruirá muchas casas cerca de la costa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm will destroy many houses near the coast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El fuego destruye la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire destroys the house.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Destruyeron el puente durante la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They destroyed the bridge during the storm.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) of “destruir” (to destroy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El incendio destruyó la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire destroyed the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La luz se desvanece al amanecer.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drive to work every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjenlo aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave it here, please.

definitions.note: Command form used with ustedes (you all / formal you). Often used to mean “leave me alone.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjenme en paz, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave me alone, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted/ustedes) with an attached indirect object pronoun: “nos” = “us.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, déjenos entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please let us come in.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) of “dar” with the pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déme su pasaporte, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me your passport, please.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) of "dar" for "yo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer le dí el libro a mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I gave the book to my sister.

definitions.note: From the verb “dar” (not “decir”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dí el libro a Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gave Ana the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy es un buen día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is a good day.

definitions.note: Plural of “día”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trabajo de lunes a viernes, pero los fines de semana descanso dos días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work Monday to Friday, but on the weekends I rest for two days.

definitions.native: tell him, tell her, tell you (formal)
definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with an indirect object pronoun (-le).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, dígale que llego tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell him/her that I’m arriving late.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with an indirect object pronoun (-les).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, dígales que la reunión empieza a las nueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell them that the meeting starts at nine.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with the object pronoun "lo" (= it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si sabe la verdad, dígalo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you know the truth, say it now.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted); also used to get someone's attention (“Excuse me?” / “Yes?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dígame la verdad, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me the truth, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted): “Tell me it.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, dígamelo otra vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell me again.

definitions.note: Affirmative command (ustedes) with an indirect object pronoun (le).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, díganle la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell him/her/them the truth.

definitions.note: Formal command to more than one person (ustedes); also used with ustedes in many Latin American countries.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, díganme la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, tell me the truth.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) of "decir"; also used as the polite "you" form with "nos" (us).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, díganos la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell us the truth.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command meaning “tell it to me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dímelo ahora, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me now, please.

definitions.note: Command form meaning “tell it to us.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dínoslo ahora, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell it to us now, please.

definitions.native: tell it to him, tell it to her, tell it to them
definitions.note: Command (tú): «di» + indirect object «se» (to him/her/them) + direct object «lo» (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Díselo ahora mismo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell it to him/her/them right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro es muy dócil y aprende rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is very docile and learns quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este libro cuesta diez dólares.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book costs ten dollars.

definitions.note: Plural form of “dólar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo veinte dólares en efectivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have twenty dollars in cash.

definitions.note: Used in questions (direct or indirect). It carries an accent to distinguish it from the relative adverb “donde” (“where/that/which”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Dónde está el baño?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where is the bathroom?

definitions.note: Loanword from English; in Spanish it’s common to see both “dónut” and “donut.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero un dónut de chocolate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a chocolate donut.

definitions.note: Used instead of "y" before words that start with the "i" sound (e.g., i-, hi-).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero té e infusiones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want tea and herbal infusions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La palabra «elefante» empieza con e.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The word "elephant" starts with E.

definitions.note: Used instead of “y” before words that start with the “i” sound (like “i-” or “hi-”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito pan e ingredientes para la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need bread and ingredients for dinner.

definitions.note: More formal than "borrachera".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conducir en estado de ebriedad es peligroso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Driving while drunk is dangerous.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal; common synonym: “borracho”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estaba ebrio y no podía caminar bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was drunk and couldn’t walk well.

definitions.note: Often used with "la basura" to mean "throws away" (e.g., "echa la basura"). It can also be the informal (tú) command form: "¡Echa!" = "Throw!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella echa la basura todas las noches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She throws out the trash every night.

definitions.native: was throwing, was putting, was pouring
definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "echar" (used for ongoing or repeated past actions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, echaba la pelota muy lejos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a kid, I used to throw the ball very far.

definitions.native: was kicking out, was firing, was sending away
definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "echar" (often used with people: "echar a alguien" = to kick someone out).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El dueño del bar echaba a los clientes que gritaban.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bar owner used to kick out the customers who shouted.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La gata está echada en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is lying down on the sofa.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to describe someone or an animal in a lying position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro está echado en la alfombra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is lying down on the rug.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to describe someone/something in a lying-down position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro está echado en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is lying down on the sofa.

definitions.note: Also commonly used in set phrases like “echar de menos” (to miss) or “echar una mano” (to help).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echamos la pelota al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We throw the ball to the dog.

definitions.note: Present participle (gerund) of "echar"; often used with "estar" to describe an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy echando agua en el vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m pouring water into the glass.

definitions.note: Very common verb with many meanings depending on context (e.g., “echar de menos” = “to miss”), but the basic meaning is “to throw.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tires la basura al suelo; échala en el cubo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t throw the trash on the ground; throw it in the bin.

definitions.native: we will throw, we will put, we will pour
definitions.note: Often used very broadly in Spanish (e.g., echar = to throw, to put/add, or to pour depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echaremos azúcar al café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will put sugar in the coffee.

definitions.native: to pour on (it), to put on (it)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (“to him/her/it/you formal”), often used with “a + noun” (e.g., echarle agua a la planta).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a echarle agua a la planta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to pour water on the plant.

definitions.native: to fire me, to kick me out
definitions.note: Infinitive of "echar" with the object pronoun "me" attached (“me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a echarme del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to fire me from my job.

definitions.note: Often used with “la basura” (the trash) or similar things you discard.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echaron la basura después de la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They threw away the trash after the party.

definitions.native: to throw you out, to kick you out
definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “te” = “you” (informal singular). Often used with “de” (e.g., “echarte de…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a echarte del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to fire you from your job.

definitions.native: I will throw, I will toss
definitions.note: Future tense (yo). Often used in expressions like "echar una mano" (to lend a hand) or "echar de menos" (to miss), but the core meaning is "to throw/toss".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echaré la pelota al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will throw the ball to the dog.

definitions.native: would throw, would put, would pour
definitions.note: Conditional form of "echar". Often used for placing/adding something (like adding salt) or pouring (like pouring water).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo le echaría más sal a la sopa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would add more salt to the soup.

definitions.native: you throw, you put, you add
definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense of “echar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Echas sal a la sopa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you add salt to the soup?

definitions.native: you threw, you poured, you put (in), you kicked out
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): informal singular “you” (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué echaste la leche en el café?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you pour the milk into the coffee?

definitions.note: Form of “echar” used with the present subjunctive (e.g., after “que”) or as a formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que eche la basura hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you throw out the trash today.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “echar la basura” (to throw away/take out the trash).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que echen la basura hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they take out the trash today.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “echar” (used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es posible que…”, “para que…”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que eches la carta al buzón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to put the letter in the mailbox.

definitions.note: From the verb "echar"; this form is also commonly used as "I add/put" in some contexts (e.g., echar sal = add salt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echo la pelota a mi hermano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I throw the ball to my brother.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular of “echar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eché la carta al buzón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I threw the letter into the mailbox.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/it threw.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echó la pelota al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She threw the ball to the dog.

definitions.note: Often used with things like salt, sugar, or ingredients.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le echó sal a la sopa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She added salt to the soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana habrá un eclipse solar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there will be a solar eclipse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El eco de su voz llenó la cueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The echo of his voice filled the cave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La economía del país está mejorando este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country's economy is improving this year.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situación económica del país es complicada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country's economic situation is complicated.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busco una opción económica para viajar este fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking for an affordable option to travel this weekend.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las medidas económicas del gobierno afectaron a muchas familias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government’s economic measures affected many families.

definitions.note: Can describe something low-priced or something that saves money/resources.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este hotel es muy económico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This hotel is very cheap.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; also used for mixed-gender groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos zapatos son muy económicos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are very affordable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ecuador divide la Tierra en dos hemisferios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The equator divides the Earth into two hemispheres.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuál es tu edad?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your age?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta es la edición de 2024.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the 2024 edition.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about editing a text, video, or photos.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La edición del video tomó muchas horas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The editing of the video took many hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese edificio es muy alto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That building is very tall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta calle hay muchos edificios altos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On this street there are many tall buildings.

definitions.note: Often refers to a magazine/newspaper editor or a film/book editor (not just a text editor program).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El editor revisó el artículo antes de publicarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The editor reviewed the article before publishing it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La educación es importante para el futuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Education is important for the future.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es muy educada con los demás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very polite with others.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of “educar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella fue educada en una escuela pública.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was educated in a public school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habló educadamente con la profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke politely with the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es muy educado con sus profesores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very polite with his teachers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es muy educada y le encanta aprender.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very educated and she loves learning.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone’s manners (how they behave), not their level of schooling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño es muy educado con los invitados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy is very polite with the guests.

definitions.note: Plural form; used for a group of men or a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños son muy educados con sus profesores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are very polite with their teachers.

definitions.note: Often used for raising/bringing up children (teaching behavior and values) as well as formal education.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante educar a los niños con respeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to raise children with respect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este programa es muy educativo para los niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This program is very educational for children.

definitions.note: Often used to confirm that something is true (like “yes, indeed”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Efectivamente, la tienda está cerrada hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Indeed, the store is closed today.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “en efectivo” = “in cash.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo pagué en efectivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I paid for it in cash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese medicamento tiene un efecto rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That medicine has a fast effect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los efectos de esta medicina son rápidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The effects of this medicine are fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este tratamiento es eficaz para el dolor de cabeza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This treatment is effective for headaches.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este método es muy eficiente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This method is very efficient.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su ego no le deja admitir que se equivocó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His ego won’t let him admit he was wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas egoísta; comparte tus juguetes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't be selfish; share your toys.

definitions.note: Can be used for a man or a woman.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas egoísta; comparte con tu hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be selfish; share with your sister.

definitions.note: Used to ask for confirmation, show surprise, or prompt someone to respond; common in casual speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Eh? No entendí lo que dijiste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Huh? I didn't understand what you said.

definitions.note: Not standard Spanish; appears to be a typo for «el» (masculine singular definite article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ei perro está en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is in the yard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo dos ejecuciones en la prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were two executions in the prison.

definitions.note: Often used for carrying out a plan, task, or process; it can also mean the death penalty in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ejecución del proyecto terminó a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The execution of the project finished on time.

definitions.note: Often used with “ser” in the passive voice to mean something was done according to a plan or order.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El proyecto fue ejecutado según el plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project was carried out according to the plan.

definitions.note: Used especially in news or historical contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El prisionero fue ejecutado al amanecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner was executed at dawn.

definitions.note: Often used to describe people or things related to business management (e.g., un cargo ejecutivo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana tiene un puesto ejecutivo en una empresa grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister has an executive position at a big company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solo tenemos un ejemplar de este libro en la biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We only have one copy of this book in the library.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este es un ejemplo fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is an easy example.

definitions.note: plural form of "ejemplo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos ejemplos son fáciles de entender.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These examples are easy to understand.

definitions.note: Often used for practicing a profession or exercising a right/authority (e.g., ejercer la medicina, ejercer un derecho).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiere ejercer la medicina en España.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She wants to practice medicine in Spain.

definitions.note: Often used for physical exercise or for practice activities (e.g., homework exercises).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hago ejercicio todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I exercise every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hago ejercicios todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do exercises every day.

definitions.note: Often appears with an accent as “ejército.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ejército llegó a la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army arrived in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ejército llegó a la ciudad por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army arrived in the city in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los ejércitos avanzaron hacia la frontera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The armies advanced toward the border.

definitions.note: masculine singular definite article (used before masculine singular nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro está en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is on the table.

definitions.note: As a pronoun, it is normally written with an accent: «él». Without the accent («el»), it is usually the masculine definite article “the.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El es mi hermano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is my brother.

definitions.note: Subject pronoun; has an accent to distinguish it from the article "el" (= "the").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él vive en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lives in Madrid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las elecciones son el próximo domingo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The elections are next Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La elección será el domingo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The election will be on Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buena elección: este restaurante es excelente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good choice: this restaurant is excellent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No hay electricidad en mi casa ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is no electricity in my house right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos un electricista para arreglar las luces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need an electrician to fix the lights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los electrones tienen carga negativa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Electrons have a negative charge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un libro electrónico en mi tableta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an electronic book on my tablet.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; used with masculine plural nouns (or mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprar dos dispositivos electrónicos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy two electronic devices.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El elefante es muy grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The elephant is very big.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el zoo vimos elefantes muy grandes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the zoo we saw very big elephants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevaba un vestido muy elegante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was wearing a very elegant dress.

definitions.note: Plural form (more than one person/thing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los vestidos son muy elegantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dresses are very elegant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él es el elegido para el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is the chosen one for the job.

definitions.note: Past participle of "elegir"; used as an adjective or with "haber" to form perfect tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Han elegido a Marta como presidenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have chosen Marta as president.

definitions.note: Can mean either present (we choose) or simple past (we chose), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy elegimos un restaurante nuevo para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we choose a new restaurant for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes elegir el color que quieras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can choose the color you want.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) for tú.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué elegiste ese libro?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you choose that book?

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) of "elegir" for "yo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer elegí el libro más corto.
