definitions.note: Feminine form. Often used as a polite way to say “nice to meet you” (usually said by a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encantada de conocerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nice to meet you.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite greeting after meeting someone: “Encantado/Encantada.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encantado de conocerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Delighted to meet you.

definitions.note: Often used in greetings: “Encantado de conocerte/conocerle” = “Nice to meet you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encantado de conocerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nice to meet you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un pueblo encantador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a charming town.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La guía es muy encantadora y nos ayuda mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide is very charming and helps us a lot.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; agrees with a masculine plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los anfitriones fueron muy encantadores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hosts were very charming.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; often used when greeting someone as “Encantados” (“Nice to meet you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encantados de conocerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nice to meet you.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les): “Me encantan…” = “I love…”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me encantan los helados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love ice cream.

definitions.note: Often used like "Me encanta..." = "I love..." (literally "It enchants/delights me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me encanta esta canción.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love this song.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (e.g., "te encantará" = "you’ll love it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te encantará este libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’ll love this book.

definitions.note: Conditional form; often used to express a polite desire (similar to “I’d love to…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me encantaría ir al cine contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d love to go to the movies with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su encanto es irresistible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her charm is irresistible.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les) to mean “(something) delighted (someone)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A Marta le encantó la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marta loved the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El periodista estuvo encarcelado durante dos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist was imprisoned for two years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El periodista fue encarcelado por decir la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist was imprisoned for telling the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mamá encarga una pizza para la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mom orders a pizza for dinner.

definitions.note: Often used with "encargar" meaning to place an order for something (e.g., food, products).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encargamos una pizza para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ordered a pizza for dinner.

definitions.note: Often used with "de": "encargarse de" = to be in charge of / to take care of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos encargamos de la limpieza después de la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are in charge of the cleaning after the party.

definitions.note: Often used with "encargar algo" (to order something) or "encargar algo a alguien" (to order something from someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encargar una pizza para la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to order a pizza for dinner.

definitions.native: to put in charge of, to assign
definitions.note: Often used with "encargar a alguien de algo" (to put someone in charge of something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jefe me encargó de organizar la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss put me in charge of organizing the meeting.

definitions.native: we will take care of, we will handle
definitions.note: Often followed by “de” + noun/infinitive (e.g., “encargarse de”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos encargaremos de la comida para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will take care of the food for the party.

definitions.native: to take care of, to be in charge of
definitions.note: Often used with “de” (encargarme de + noun/verb) to say what you will take care of.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encargarme de la comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take care of the food.

definitions.native: I will take care of, I will arrange
definitions.note: First person singular (yo), future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo me encargaré de llamar al médico mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will take care of calling the doctor tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for ordering food or requesting something to be made or delivered.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encargo una pizza para esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I order a pizza for tonight.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer encargué una pizza para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ordered a pizza for dinner.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/you-formal) of “encargar”; often used for placing an order or commissioning work.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mamá encargó una pizza para la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mom ordered a pizza for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes un encendedor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a lighter?

definitions.note: Used for switching on devices (lights, TV, etc.) or lighting a fire/candle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encender la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to turn on the light.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La luz está encendida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is on.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las luces están encendidas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lights are on.

definitions.note: Often used for devices, lights, or engines that are operating.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deja el móvil encendido por si te llamo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave your phone on in case I call you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encendió la luz del pasillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She turned on the hallway light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encendí la luz porque estaba oscuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned on the light because it was dark.

definitions.note: Often used to describe being confined indoors (e.g., at home).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estuve encerrado en casa todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was shut in at home all day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía lo encerró en una celda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police locked him up in a cell.

definitions.note: Most commonly refers to an electrical plug or the place you plug something in.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No hay enchufes cerca de la cama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are no outlets near the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busqué la información en una enciclopedia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked up the information in an encyclopedia.

definitions.note: plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la biblioteca hay muchas enciclopedias antiguas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the library there are many old encyclopedias.

definitions.note: Used for formal commands (usted) and for the present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, encienda la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn on the light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, enciende la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn on the light.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" ("encima de") to mean "on top of / over".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro está encima de la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is on top of the table.

definitions.native: in addition, on top of that
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy llegué tarde y encima olvidé las llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I arrived late and on top of that I forgot the keys.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al oír el ruido, encogió los hombros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he heard the noise, he shrugged his shoulders.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted). Often used for ongoing or habitual past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre encontraba mis llaves en el mismo cajón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always used to find my keys in the same drawer.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (third person plural). Often used for ongoing or habitual past actions, or to set the scene in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños encontraban conchas en la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were finding shells on the beach.

definitions.note: Past participle of "encontrar"; commonly used with "haber" to form the present perfect (e.g., "he encontrado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He encontrado mis llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have found my keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los documentos fueron encontrados en la oficina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were found in the office.

definitions.note: Present tense (“we find”) or preterite (“we found”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finalmente encontramos el hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We finally found the hotel.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of “encontrar”; often used with “estar” to talk about something happening right now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy encontrando las llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am finding the keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo encontrar mis llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't find my keys.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form; often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., after "si" = "if").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lo encontrara, te llamaría de inmediato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I found it, I would call you right away.

definitions.note: Used in hypothetical or uncertain situations (imperfect subjunctive), often after “si” (if).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si ellos encontraran el libro, me llamarían.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they found the book, they would call me.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (tú). Often used after “si” to mean “if you found / if you were to find.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si encontraras mis llaves, me ayudarías mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you found my keys, you would help me a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana encontraremos una solución.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will find a solution.

definitions.native: to find her, to find it
definitions.note: Direct object pronoun "la" can mean "her" or "it" (feminine object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encontrarla mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to find her tomorrow.

definitions.native: to find him, to find her
definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “le” (= him/her). In some regions (especially Spain), “le” can be used for a male direct object (where other regions often use “lo”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encontrarle en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to find him in the park.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun "lo" (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encontrarlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to find it tomorrow.

definitions.native: to meet (up with), to find myself
definitions.note: Reflexive form (me). Often used for arranging to meet someone: “encontrarme con…” = “to meet up with…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quedé en encontrarme con Ana a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agreed to meet up with Ana at six.

definitions.native: to meet up, to find ourselves
definitions.note: Reflexive form with "nos" (we/us). Often used as "to meet up" when talking about people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Podemos encontrarnos en la cafetería a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can meet up at the café at six.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) preterite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontraron las llaves debajo del sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found the keys under the couch.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used to say where someone/something is located or in a certain state.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El museo se encuentra en el centro de la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum is in the city center.

definitions.native: to find you, to meet up with you
definitions.note: Includes the reflexive pronoun “te” (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero encontrarte mañana después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to meet up with you tomorrow after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontrará la respuesta en el libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will find the answer in the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana encontrarán la solución.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will find the solution.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontrarás las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will find the keys on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te encontraré mañana en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will find you tomorrow in the park.

definitions.note: Conditional ("would" form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si buscara un poco más, lo encontraría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I looked a little more, I would find it.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Encontraste las llaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you find the keys?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (nosotros); often used for suggestions or after expressions like “espero que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontremos una solución juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s find a solution together.

definitions.note: Used with vosotros/vosotras (Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Encontráis las llaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you all find the keys?

definitions.native: we might find, we might meet
definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (nosotros); used in hypotheticals, wishes, or after certain past expressions (e.g., "quería que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si encontráramos las llaves, podríamos irnos ya.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we found the keys, we could leave now.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontré mis llaves en la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my keys in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person singular (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella encontró sus llaves en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She found her keys on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El agente encubierto entró al edificio sin llamar la atención.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The undercover agent entered the building without drawing attention.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) present tense of “encontrar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella encuentra sus llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She finds her keys on the table.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “encontrar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos encuentran las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They find the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Dónde encuentras las llaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you find the keys?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) or formal command (usted) of "encontrar."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que encuentre las llaves pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you find the keys soon.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used as an imperative for “you all” in Latin America).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que encuentren las llaves pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you find the keys soon.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú form) of "encontrar"; often used after expressions like "quiero que", "espero que", "cuando", etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que encuentres tus llaves pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you find your keys soon.

definitions.note: Often means “find” (an object). It can also mean “meet” in the sense of “run into” someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre encuentro mis llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always find my keys on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos un encuentro mañana por la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a meeting tomorrow afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El encuentro con el perro fue inesperado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The encounter with the dog was unexpected.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos encuentros todos los lunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have meetings every Monday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa hizo una encuesta para conocer la opinión de los clientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company did a survey to learn the customers' opinion.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command form; often used with de + noun (encárgate de...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encárgate de la cena esta noche, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take care of dinner tonight, please.

definitions.note: Plural of "encía" (gum in your mouth).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me sangran las encías cuando me cepillo los dientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My gums bleed when I brush my teeth.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used for a woman or female opponent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es mi enemiga desde la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been my enemy since school.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las tropas enemigas avanzaron al amanecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The enemy troops advanced at dawn.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it means “hostile” or “enemy” (e.g., “enemy forces/territory”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las fuerzas enemigas avanzaron durante la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The enemy forces advanced during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi enemigo vive en la casa de al lado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My enemy lives in the house next door.

definitions.note: plural form of "enemigo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero tener enemigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to have enemies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo energía hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have energy today.

definitions.note: Plural of "energía".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito más energías para terminar el trabajo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need more energy to finish the work today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi cumpleaños es en enero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in January.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "enfadar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ruido me enfada mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise annoys me a lot.

definitions.note: feminine form (used with feminine nouns or to refer to a woman)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enfadada contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm angry with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enfadado contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m angry with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enfada cuando la gente llega tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It annoys me when people arrive late.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive ("-ra" form), often used in conditional sentences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No creí que eso te enfadara tanto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't think that would annoy you so much.

definitions.native: to get angry, to get upset
definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used for becoming angry (rather than making someone else angry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te enfades conmigo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t get angry with me, please.

definitions.note: Often used for being upset or annoyed (a “fit of anger” or “being mad”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su enfado duró todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His anger lasted all day.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "enfadar" (él/ella/usted). Depending on context, it can be intransitive (got angry) or transitive (made someone angry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enfadó cuando escuchó la noticia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got angry when he heard the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor enfatizó la importancia de estudiar todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher emphasized the importance of studying every day.

definitions.note: Can be used for someone becoming ill (present tense, he/she/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana enferma a menudo en invierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister gets sick often in winter.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana está enferma hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is sick today.

definitions.native: to get sick, to make (someone) sick
definitions.note: Can be used intransitively (to get sick) or transitively (to make someone sick).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enfermé la semana pasada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got sick last week.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis hermanas están enfermas hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sisters are sick today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una enfermedad y necesito descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an illness and I need to rest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En invierno, hay más enfermedades respiratorias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter, there are more respiratory illnesses.

definitions.note: female form (used for a woman nurse)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es enfermera en el hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a nurse at the hospital.

definitions.note: feminine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las enfermeras trabajan en el hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurses work at the hospital.

definitions.note: Refers to a male nurse; the feminine form is “enfermera”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El enfermero trabaja en el hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The (male) nurse works at the hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana estudia enfermería en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister studies nursing at the university.

definitions.note: Often used for the medical room or clinic inside a school, workplace, or institution.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ve a la enfermería si no te sientes bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go to the infirmary if you don’t feel well.

definitions.note: Often used with the verb "estar" to describe someone who is unwell.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enfermo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sick today.

definitions.note: Often used for a man; for a woman, you’ll usually hear “enferma.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El enfermo necesita descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sick person needs to rest.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also be used for a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están enfermos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are sick.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el hospital hay muchos enfermos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many sick people in the hospital.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also refer to a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los enfermos esperan al médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sick patients are waiting for the doctor.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she got sick.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enfermó después de comer mariscos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She got sick after eating seafood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos un enfoque diferente para resolver el problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a different approach to solve the problem.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “enfrentar” (he/she/it faces; you formal face).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella enfrenta muchos retos en su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She faces many challenges at her job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He enfrentado muchos problemas este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have faced many problems this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfrentamos muchos retos este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We face many challenges this year.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they/you plural) present tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos enfrentan muchos problemas cada día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They face many problems every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enfrentando un problema difícil en el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am facing a difficult problem at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que enfrentar el problema ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to face the problem now.

definitions.native: we will face, we will confront
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana enfrentaremos un nuevo desafío en el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will face a new challenge at work.

definitions.native: to confront you, to face you
definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “-te” (= you, informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero enfrentarte en público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to confront you in public.

definitions.note: Often used with "de": "enfrente de" = "in front of / across from".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La farmacia está enfrente del banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pharmacy is across from the bank.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular: “he/she/it faced.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella enfrentó muchos desafíos el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She faced many challenges last year.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for formal commands: usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que el café se enfríe pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the coffee cools down soon.

definitions.note: Often used informally, especially for being addicted to a substance or to something like a TV show or a game.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enganchado a esa serie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m hooked on that show.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él engaña a la gente para conseguir dinero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deceives people to get money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me siento engañado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel deceived.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense: “they” (or “you” plural in Spain) deceive/trick.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A veces nos engañan con promesas falsas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes they deceive us with false promises.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ing form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está engañando a sus amigos con esa historia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is deceiving his friends with that story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero engañar a nadie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to deceive anyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me engañaron con una oferta falsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tricked me with a fake offer.

definitions.native: to trick you, to deceive you
definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun “te” (“you”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero engañarte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to trick you.

definitions.native: you tricked, you deceived, you cheated (on)
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me engañaste y ahora no confío en ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You deceived me, and now I don't trust you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su historia era un engaño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His story was a deception.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El anuncio es engañoso y no dice toda la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ad is misleading and doesn’t tell the whole truth.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te engañé y lo siento mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tricked you, and I'm very sorry.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/you (formal) tricked/deceived.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me engañó con una excusa y nunca volvió.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tricked me with an excuse and never came back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pobreza engendra violencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Poverty creates violence.

definitions.note: Past participle of "engordar"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect (e.g., "he engordado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He engordado cinco kilos este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I've gained five kilos this year.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "engordar"; often used with "estar" to talk about an ongoing change.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Últimamente, estoy engordando un poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lately, I'm gaining a little weight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desde que dejé de correr, empecé a engordar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since I stopped running, I started to gain weight.

definitions.note: Used to congratulate someone (often for good news or an achievement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Enhorabuena por tu nuevo trabajo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Congratulations on your new job!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su desaparición sigue siendo un enigma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His disappearance is still a mystery.

definitions.note: Often used for a swarm of bees or other insects; can also be used metaphorically for a crowd.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos un enjambre de abejas cerca del árbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a swarm of bees near the tree.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los animales estaban enjaulados y no podían moverse mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The animals were caged and couldn’t move much.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular: “he/she/it rinsed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enjuagó los platos después de lavarlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She rinsed the dishes after washing them.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a web link or hyperlink.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te envío el enlace por correo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sending you the link by email.

definitions.note: Often used for a connection between things or people (more general than an internet link).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay un enlace directo entre el centro y el aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a direct connection between downtown and the airport.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted), especially in the phrase “enllave la puerta”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, enllave la puerta al salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please lock the door when you leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando perdió el trabajo, enloqueció por completo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he lost his job, he went completely crazy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enmarqué la foto de mi familia y la colgué en la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I framed my family photo and hung it on the wall.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “enojar” (also commonly: “gets (someone) angry”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese ruido me enoja mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise annoys me a lot.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está enojada porque llegaste tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is angry because you arrived late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enojado contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m angry with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese comentario me enoja mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That comment annoys me a lot.

definitions.native: to get angry, to be upset
definitions.note: Reflexive form; commonly used for becoming angry/upset.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enojé porque llegaste tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got angry because you arrived late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enojo cuando llegas tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get angry when you arrive late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su enojo duró todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His anger lasted all day.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of "enojar" for he/she/it/you (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enojó conmigo porque llegué tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got angry with me because I arrived late.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les): “Me enorgullece...” = “It makes me proud...”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enorgullece tu esfuerzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your effort makes me proud.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El edificio es enorme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building is huge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me ayudaste enormemente con la mudanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You helped me enormously with the move.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los perros son enormes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dogs are huge.

definitions.note: Common misspelling of “entonces” in informal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enronces, ¿qué hacemos ahora?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So, what do we do now?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a pedir una ensalada para el almuerzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to order a salad for lunch.

definitions.note: Often used for practicing a performance (a play, concert, speech, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que ensayar la obra antes del estreno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to rehearse the play before the premiere.

definitions.note: Used for trying a method, plan, or idea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a ensayar una nueva receta este fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to try out a new recipe this weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que escribir un ensayo para la clase de historia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to write an essay for history class.

definitions.note: Used especially for theater, music, or dance practice before a performance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ensayo empieza a las seis y termina a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rehearsal starts at six and ends at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los ensayos empiezan a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rehearsals start at six.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que entregar tres ensayos esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to turn in three essays this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy para allá enseguida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going there right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella enseña español en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She teaches Spanish at school.

definitions.note: Also used as a formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Señor, enseña la lección otra vez, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sir, teach the lesson again, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela me enseñaba a cocinar cuando era niño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother used to teach me to cook when I was a child.

definitions.note: Past participle of “enseñar”; used with “haber” (e.g., “he enseñado”) or as an adjective (e.g., “está enseñado”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya he enseñado la lección de hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already taught today’s lesson.

definitions.note: From "enseñar"; can also mean "we show" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enseñamos español a los niños los lunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We teach Spanish to the children on Mondays.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "enseñar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta escuela, enseñan matemáticas y ciencias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At this school, they teach math and science.

definitions.note: present participle/gerund of "enseñar"; often used with "estar" to describe an ongoing action
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enseñando español a mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am teaching Spanish to my sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La enseñanza de español en esta escuela es muy buena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teaching of Spanish at this school is very good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi padre me enseñó a nadar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father taught me to swim.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (yo/él/ella/usted). Often used in "if" clauses (si...) or after expressions that trigger the subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo enseñara español, trabajaría en una escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I taught Spanish, I would work at a school.

definitions.native: to teach him, to teach her, to teach you (formal)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun "le" (to him/her/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enseñarle a mi hermana cómo usar la aplicación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to teach my sister how to use the app.

definitions.native: to teach them, to show them
definitions.note: The ending “-les” means “to them” (indirect object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enseñarles español a mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to teach my friends Spanish.

definitions.note: Infinitive + indirect object pronoun "me" (to me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes enseñarme cómo se hace.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you teach me how it’s done?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural (they/you all taught).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enseñaron a los niños a leer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They taught the children to read.

definitions.native: to teach you, to show you
definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun “te” attached (“to you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero enseñarte a cocinar pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to teach you how to cook pasta.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal "you" (usted) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La profesora enseñará español mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher will teach Spanish tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo), simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te enseñaré a cocinar una tortilla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will teach you how to cook an omelet.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Me enseñas a cocinar esta receta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you teach me how to cook this recipe?

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope that…”) or as a formal (usted) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me enseñe español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you teach me Spanish.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal (usted) command meaning “show.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, enseñe su pasaporte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please show your passport.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "enseñar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me enseñes cómo hacerlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you teach me how to do it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te enseño a cocinar pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I teach you how to cook pasta.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer enseñé español a mi amigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I taught Spanish to my friend.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/you formal) in the past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor nos enseñó a leer en español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher taught us to read in Spanish.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro ensució la alfombra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog made the carpet dirty.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) with the object pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enséñame cómo se hace, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Show me how it’s done, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted): “Teach/Show me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, enséñeme cómo llegar a la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please show me how to get to the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entendemos la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t understand the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entiendo esta pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand this question.

definitions.native: understand him, understand her, understand you
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (often meaning “him/her/you (formal)”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo entenderle cuando habla tan rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't understand him when he speaks so fast.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo entenderlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t understand it.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal you (usted) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo entenderá cuando sea mayor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He'll understand it when he's older.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lo explicas despacio, entenderán la idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you explain it slowly, they will understand the idea.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo entenderás cuando seas mayor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will understand it when you are older.

definitions.note: Conditional form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo lo entendería si me lo explicaras con calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would understand it if you explained it to me calmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me escucharas con calma, entenderías lo que quiero decir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you listened to me calmly, you would understand what I mean.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todo está entendido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is understood.

definitions.note: Often used on its own to mean “understood/OK” (like “got it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Está entendido?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that understood?

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "entender"; often used with "estar" to express an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy entendiendo mejor la lección hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am understanding the lesson better today.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted form) of “entender”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo entendiera la pregunta, podría responderla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I understood the question, I could answer it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entendieron la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They didn't understand the question.

definitions.note: Often refers to understanding in the sense of comprehension or mutual agreement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegamos a un entendimiento después de hablar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached an understanding after talking.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): used for a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Entendiste la tarea?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you understand the assignment?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella entendió la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She understood the question.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entendí la explicación al final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understood the explanation in the end.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (I/he/she/you formal) of “entender”; often implies an ongoing or habitual understanding in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, no entendía las instrucciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I didn’t understand the instructions.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object and "de" (e.g., "me entera de..." = "informs me about...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella me entera de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She informs me about the meeting.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me comí la pizza entera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate the whole pizza.

definitions.note: Often used with “estar” (e.g., “estar enterado de…” = to be aware of…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enterado de lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m aware of what happened.

definitions.note: Often used with estar/quedar (e.g., “estar enterado de…” = “to be aware of…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enterado de la noticia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m aware of the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enteramente de acuerdo contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I completely agree with you.

definitions.note: Commonly used with the reflexive form: “nos enteramos (de...)” = “we find out (about...)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos enteramos de la noticia ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found out about the news yesterday.

definitions.note: Most commonly used as the pronominal verb “enterarse (de)” meaning “to find out / to hear about.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enterar a mi jefe de lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to inform my boss about what happened.

definitions.native: to find out, to hear about
definitions.note: Usually used with “de” (e.g., “enterarse de algo” = to find out about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enteré de la noticia ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found out about the news yesterday.

definitions.note: Commonly used with "de" ("enterarse de algo" = to find out about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enteré de la noticia ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found out about the news yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used as “enterarse (de)” meaning “to find out (about).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enterará de la noticia mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will find out about the news tomorrow.

definitions.note: feminine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me comí dos manzanas enteras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate two whole apples.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (who you inform) and sometimes with “de” to introduce what they are informed about.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que entere a su jefe de los cambios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you inform your boss about the changes.

definitions.native: I find out, I hear about
definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive form: me entero (enterarse).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me entero de la noticia por mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find out about the news from my sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me comí el pastel entero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate the whole cake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El vaso llegó entero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass arrived intact.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ciudad quedó enterrada bajo la nieve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city was buried under the snow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontraron la caja enterrada en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found the box buried in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tesoro estaba enterrado bajo el árbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The treasure was buried under the tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tesoro está enterrado cerca del río.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The treasure is buried near the river.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; it can describe people or things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los tesoros quedaron enterrados bajo la arena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The treasures were left buried under the sand.

definitions.native: we bury, we bury (something), we bury (someone)
definitions.note: Also commonly used figuratively: “we bury” (e.g., an idea, the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enterramos el tesoro en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bury the treasure in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a enterrar a su abuelo mañana.
