definitions.note: Combination of the auxiliary verb "haber" + the object pronoun "te" (you). It’s used with an infinitive or a past participle, depending on the construction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento haberte llamado tan tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm sorry to have called you so late.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the past perfect (pluperfect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya había terminado la tarea cuando llegaste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already finished the homework when you arrived.

definitions.note: Past participle of “haber”, used in perfect tenses; often in “ha habido” = “there has been”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha habido muchos cambios este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There have been many changes this year.

definitions.note: Used to form the gerund/perfect constructions (e.g., "habiendo + past participle").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habiendo terminado el trabajo, nos fuimos a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Having finished the work, we went home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene una gran habilidad para aprender idiomas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She has a great ability to learn languages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas habilidades de comunicación para este trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need communication skills for this job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El hotel tiene muchas habitaciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel has many rooms.

definitions.note: Often used for a bedroom (e.g., in a house or hotel).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La habitación es pequeña, pero cómoda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is small, but comfortable.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los habitantes de la ciudad quieren más parques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The inhabitants of the city want more parks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mi lugar habitual para estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s my usual place to study.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habitualmente voy al gimnasio por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually go to the gym in the morning.

definitions.note: Often refers to the act or manner of speaking (e.g., someone’s way of talking) as well as a speech or spoken language in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su habla es muy clara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her way of speaking is very clear.

definitions.note: Can also be used as a formal command (usted): “Speak!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella habla español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks Spanish.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted). Often describes an ongoing past action or a habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegaste, yo hablaba por teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you arrived, I was talking on the phone.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegué, ellos hablaban de sus planes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, they were talking about their plans.

definitions.native: you were talking, you used to talk
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando eras niño, hablabas mucho en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were a kid, you used to talk a lot in class.

definitions.note: Used with vosotros/vosotras (Spain); affirmative command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablad más despacio, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak more slowly, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El español hablado puede ser diferente del español escrito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spoken Spanish can be different from written Spanish.

definitions.note: Past participle of "hablar"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He hablado con ella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have spoken with her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es muy hablador y siempre tiene una historia que contar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very talkative and always has a story to tell.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros/as) form of "hablar". It can also be used for "we spoke" in the simple past, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablamos español en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We speak Spanish at home.

definitions.note: Third-person plural ("they") present tense of "hablar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos hablan español en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They speak Spanish at home.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "hablar"; used with "estar" to talk about what’s happening right now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy hablando con mi profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am talking with my teacher.

definitions.note: Used for a person who speaks a language (often with a language name: "hablante de inglés").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es hablante de español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a Spanish speaker.

definitions.note: Usually refers to people who speak a particular language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos hablantes de español en esta ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many Spanish speakers in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta hablar con mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to talk with my friends.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “hablar”; often used after expressions like “querer que…”, “pedir que…”, or in conditional-style sentences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que hablara más despacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted him to speak more slowly.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form, often used in “si…” (if…) sentences and other hypothetical/uncertain contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si hablaras más despacio, te entendería mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you spoke more slowly, I would understand you better.

definitions.native: we will talk, we will speak
definitions.note: Simple future (nosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana hablaremos con el profesor después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will talk with the teacher after class.

definitions.native: to talk to him/her, to talk to you (formal)
definitions.note: "le" is an indirect object pronoun meaning "to him," "to her," or "to you" (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a hablarle mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to talk to him/her tomorrow.

definitions.native: to talk to them, to speak to them
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “les” (“to them” / “to you all” in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hablarles mañana después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to talk to them tomorrow after class.

definitions.native: to talk about it, to speak it
definitions.note: Infinitive form with the direct object pronoun “lo” attached (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hablarlo contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to talk about it with you.

definitions.native: talk to me, speak to me
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “me” (= to/with me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes hablarme mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you talk to me tomorrow?

definitions.native: to talk to us, to speak to us
definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached indirect object pronoun “nos” (“to us”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes hablarnos después de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can talk to us after the meeting.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer hablaron con el profesor después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they spoke with the teacher after class.

definitions.native: to talk to you, to speak to you
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “te” (“to you,” informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito hablarte un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to talk to you for a moment.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense (he/she/it will speak).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana hablará con el médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he will talk with the doctor.

definitions.native: I will speak, I will talk
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana hablaré con mi profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will talk with my teacher.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "hablar" (used for hypotheticals, polite requests, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo hablaría con el profesor si tuviera tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would talk to the teacher if I had time.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablas muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You speak very fast.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “hablar”; often used in conditional or hypothetical sentences (can sound more formal/literary than “hablara”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si él hablase más despacio, lo entendería mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he spoke more slowly, I would understand him better.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular “you” (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer hablaste con tu profesor después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday you spoke with your teacher after class.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) of “hablar”; also used as the formal (usted) command “speak/talk” and after “que” (e.g., “que hable”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que hable con el profesor hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you speak with the teacher today.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, 1st person plural; often used to make a suggestion (“let’s …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablemos de tu plan para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s talk about your plan for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes) or affirmative command (ustedes) of “hablar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que hablen más despacio, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to speak more slowly, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú form); often used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es importante que…”, “no creo que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que hables más despacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to speak more slowly.

definitions.note: Present tense, first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablo español en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak Spanish at home.

definitions.native: we were talking, we used to talk
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): can describe an ongoing past action or a habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando éramos niños, hablábamos mucho en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we used to talk a lot in class.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer hablé con mi profesor después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I spoke with my teacher after class.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer habló con su profesor después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she spoke with his/her teacher after class.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros/nosotras) future tense of the auxiliary verb “haber,” used to form the future perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para mañana, ya habremos terminado el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By tomorrow, we will have finished the project.

definitions.note: Impersonal future form of "haber" used to say that something exists or will happen (it doesn’t change for singular/plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana habrá una reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there will be a meeting.

definitions.note: Impersonal form of "haber" used to say something exists/will exist; it stays singular even with plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana habrá una reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there will be a meeting.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the future perfect (e.g., "habrá terminado" = "will have finished").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para las cinco, ya habrá terminado el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By five o’clock, he/she will have finished the work.

definitions.note: Third-person plural, future (used to say something will exist or happen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana habrán más asientos disponibles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there will be more seats available.

definitions.note: Used with a past participle to form the future perfect (e.g., "habrás comido" = "you will have eaten").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana a esta hora, ya habrás terminado el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow at this time, you will have already finished the work.

definitions.note: Future tense (yo). Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the future perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para mañana, habré terminado el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By tomorrow, I will have finished the work.

definitions.note: Conditional form of the auxiliary verb “haber”, used to form the conditional perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habría llegado antes, pero había mucho tráfico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would have arrived earlier, but there was a lot of traffic.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "haber" used impersonally (often translated as "there would be").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si llegáramos más temprano, habría más tiempo para hablar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we arrived earlier, there would be more time to talk.

definitions.note: Conditional form of the auxiliary verb “haber”, used to form the conditional perfect (e.g., “habríamos + past participle”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habríamos llegado antes, pero había mucho tráfico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would have arrived earlier, but there was a lot of traffic.

definitions.note: Conditional form used with a past participle to form the conditional perfect (e.g., “habrían comido” = “would have eaten”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habrían llegado antes, pero había mucho tráfico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would have arrived earlier, but there was a lot of traffic.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) conditional form, used to form the conditional perfect with a past participle (e.g., "habrías hecho").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Habrías venido si te lo hubiera dicho antes?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you have come if I had told you earlier?

definitions.note: Used with the vosotros/vosotras form (informal plural “you” in Spain) as an auxiliary to form perfect tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Ya habéis comido?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you eaten already?

definitions.note: Infinitive of the auxiliary "haber" with the attached pronouns "me" (to me) + "lo" (it). Often used in phrases like "por habérmelo + past participle" (e.g., "por habérmelo dicho" = "for having told me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por habérmelo dicho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for having told me.

definitions.note: Infinitive of the auxiliary “haber” with the attached pronouns “te” (to you) + “lo” (it). Often used in perfect infinitive structures like “haberte lo + past participle”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento habértelo dicho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm sorry to have told you that.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the past perfect (pluperfect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegué, ya había terminado la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, I had already finished the homework.

definitions.note: Impersonal form of "haber" used to say something existed in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Había mucha gente en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were a lot of people in the street.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle (había + participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya había comido cuando llegaste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already eaten when you arrived.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary verb to form compound tenses (past perfect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya habíamos comido cuando llegaste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had already eaten when you arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes) of the auxiliary verb "haber"; commonly used to form the past perfect (pluscuamperfecto) and in the impersonal form "había/habían" meaning "there was/were."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegamos, ya habían terminado la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we arrived, they had already finished the meeting.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary in the past perfect (pluscuamperfecto).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya habías terminado cuando llegué.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had already finished when I arrived.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mamá hace café todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mom makes coffee every morning.

definitions.note: Used in time expressions (hace + amount of time) to say how long ago something happened.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salí de casa hace diez minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left home ten minutes ago.

definitions.note: Command form (vosotros). Used in Spain; in most of Latin America, people usually use “hagan” instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Haced la tarea antes de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do the homework before dinner.

definitions.note: Plural affirmative command (vosotros) with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si ya tenéis tiempo, hacedlo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have time already, do it now.

definitions.note: Informal command using voseo (common in Argentina/Uruguay): hacé + lo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si querés terminar rápido, hacelo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you want to finish quickly, do it now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy hacemos la tarea juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we do the homework together.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "hacer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos hacen la tarea después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They do their homework after dinner.

definitions.note: Very common verb; often means “do” (an action/task) or “make” (create/prepare) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hacer la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to do the homework.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“it” or “her”, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a hacerla mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to do it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to him, to her, or to you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hacerle una pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to ask him/her a question.

definitions.native: to do for them, to make for them
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “les” (“to them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a hacerles una cena esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to make them dinner tonight.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "hacer" with the attached direct-object pronoun "lo" (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a hacerlo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to do it now.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “los” = “them” (typically masculine plural, or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que hacerlos hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do them today.

definitions.note: Includes the attached object pronoun “me” (= me). Often used before another word/phrase, e.g., “hacerme un favor” = “do me a favor.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes hacerme un favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you do me a favor?

definitions.native: to make us, to do to us
definitions.note: Object pronoun “nos” is attached: it means “us.” Often used after another verb (e.g., “vamos a hacernos…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a hacernos esperar otra hora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to make us wait another hour.

definitions.note: Reflexive use of "hacer": used for changes in state or becoming something (often with an adjective or noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con el tiempo, se hizo más paciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Over time, he became more patient.

definitions.native: to make you, to do to you
definitions.note: Direct object pronoun + infinitive: hacer + te (“you”, informal singular). Often used with another verb, e.g., “hacerte reír” = “make you laugh.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hacerte una pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to ask you a question.

definitions.note: Present tense tú form (informal singular): “you do/make.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué haces hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you doing today?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un hacha para cortar leña.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need an axe to cut firewood.

definitions.note: Used to indicate direction or movement toward a place, person, or goal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Caminamos hacia la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked toward the station.

definitions.note: Used with time to mean “around/approximately.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegamos hacia las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived around eight.

definitions.note: Often refers to a large country property (especially in Latin America).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pasamos el fin de semana en una hacienda cerca del lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We spent the weekend on an estate near the lake.

definitions.note: Used in Spain to refer to the public treasury/tax office (often capitalized: Hacienda).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to file these documents with the tax office.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "hacer"; used with "estar" for the progressive (e.g., "estoy haciendo...") or to mean "by doing/making".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy haciendo la tarea ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am doing my homework now.

definitions.note: Gerund of "hacer" with the direct object pronoun "lo" ("it") attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy haciéndolo ahora mismo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm doing it right now.

definitions.note: Informal command (vos form), common in Argentina/Uruguay and some other regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hacé la tarea ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do the homework now.

definitions.note: Informal plural (vosotros/vosotras) present tense, used mainly in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué hacéis este fin de semana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you (plural) doing this weekend?

definitions.note: Used with vos (voseo), common in Argentina, Uruguay, and parts of Central America.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué hacés hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you doing today?

definitions.native: was doing, used to do, made
definitions.note: Imperfect tense of “hacer.” It can mean an ongoing/repeated past action (“was doing/used to do”) or “made” in contexts like “made a decision.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, hacía la tarea después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to do my homework after dinner.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense, third-person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Antes, mis abuelos hacían pan en casa todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before, my grandparents used to make bread at home every day.

definitions.native: you were doing, you used to do
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué hacías ayer por la tarde?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What were you doing yesterday afternoon?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La hada del cuento ayuda al niño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fairy in the story helps the boy.

definitions.note: Plural of "hada".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el cuento, las hadas ayudan al niño perdido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the story, the fairies help the lost boy.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “hacer” (used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es importante que…”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que haga la tarea ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want (him/her/you) to do the homework now.

definitions.note: First-person plural present subjunctive of “hacer”; often used to make suggestions (like “let’s …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hagamos la tarea ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s do the homework now.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes). Also used for commands (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que hagan la tarea hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you do the homework today.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) form of “hacer”; often used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es importante que…”, or “no creo que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que hagas la tarea hoy.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take my coat with me because it’s cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me llevo bien con mis compañeros de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get along well with my classmates.

definitions.native: to take you, to carry you
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun "te" = "you" (informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedo llevarte al aeropuerto mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can take you to the airport tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) future tense of “llevar” (also used with “usted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella llevará el paquete a la oficina mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will take the package to the office tomorrow.

definitions.native: will take, will carry, will wear

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will take the boxes to the warehouse.

definitions.native: I will take, I will carry
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana llevaré el libro a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will take the book to school.

definitions.note: Used for clothing or accessories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy hace frío; llevaré un abrigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold today; I will wear a coat.

definitions.native: would take, would carry, would wear
definitions.note: Conditional form of "llevar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo llevaría una chaqueta si hiciera frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would wear a jacket if it were cold.

definitions.native: you wear, you carry, you take
definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense of "llevar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Llevas abrigo hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you wearing a coat today?

definitions.native: you took, you carried, you wore
definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) preterite (simple past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué no llevaste el paraguas?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why didn’t you take the umbrella?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo) or formal command (usted) of "llevar"; it can also be the present subjunctive of "llevar" for other persons depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que lleve su chaqueta porque hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you wear your jacket because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or formal command) form of “llevar” for “ustedes” (and also present subjunctive for “ellos/ellas”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que lleven sus pasaportes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you bring your passports.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "llevar"; also used as the affirmative informal command when preceded by "no" (negative tú command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que lleves tu chaqueta porque hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you bring your jacket because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Often used with a gerund (-ando/-iendo) to say how long something has been happening (llevar + gerund).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevo estudiando dos horas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I've been studying for two hours.

definitions.native: I carry, I wear, I take
definitions.note: Present tense (yo) of "llevar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevo una chaqueta porque hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m wearing a jacket because it’s cold.

definitions.native: we were taking, we were carrying
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (we). Often used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevábamos las maletas al coche cuando empezó a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were carrying the suitcases to the car when it started to rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevé el libro a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took the book to school.

definitions.note: Used for wearing clothes or accessories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer llevé una camisa azul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I wore a blue shirt.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite) form meaning a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella llevó el libro a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She took the book to school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi bebé llora mucho por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My baby cries a lot at night.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, lloraba mucho por las noches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to cry a lot at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lloramos cuando vemos una película triste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We cry when we watch a sad movie.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "llorar" (they cry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los bebés lloran cuando tienen hambre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Babies cry when they are hungry.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "llorar"; used with "estar" or to describe an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy llorando porque extraño a mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am crying because I miss my family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella empieza a llorar cuando ve la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She starts to cry when she watches the movie.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) or negative imperative (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No llores, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t cry, please.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A veces lloro cuando veo películas tristes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes I cry when I watch sad movies.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lloré cuando vi la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cried when I saw the movie.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella lloró cuando vio la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cried when she saw the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy va a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s going to rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana lloverá por la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow it will rain in the afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha llovido mucho hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It has rained a lot today.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "llover"; used with "estar" (e.g., "está lloviendo") or to describe an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está lloviendo mucho hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining a lot today.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "llover"; often used after "si" (if) and in hypothetical or dependent clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lloviera mañana, cancelaríamos el picnic.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it rained tomorrow, we would cancel the picnic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer llovió todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday it rained all day.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense of "llover"; describes ongoing or habitual rain in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer por la tarde llovía y hacía frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday afternoon it was raining and it was cold.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “llover”; often used after expressions like “Espero que…”, “Ojalá…”, or “Es posible que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no llueva mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it doesn’t rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used to talk about the weather; it doesn’t refer to a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy llueve mucho en la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining a lot in the city today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lluvia no para desde ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain hasn’t stopped since yesterday.

definitions.note: Plural of "lluvia".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This week's rains caused flooding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy está muy lluvioso y hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s very rainy and it’s cold.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los días lluviosos me hacen querer quedarme en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rainy days make me want to stay at home.

definitions.native: call him, call her, call it
definitions.note: Informal affirmative command (tú). "-le" is an indirect object pronoun (to him/her/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si necesitas ayuda, llámale ahora mismo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you need help, call him/her right now.

definitions.note: Command (tú) form with a direct object pronoun (-lo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no contesta, llámalo otra vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he doesn't answer, call him again.

definitions.note: Affirmative informal (tú) command + object pronoun “me”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llámame mañana por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Call me tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) with an attached object pronoun (nos).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tienes preguntas, llámanos mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have questions, call us tomorrow.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, llámeme mañana por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please call me tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Command form (ustedes); used to address more than one person or as a formal command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tienen preguntas, llámenme mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have questions, call me tomorrow.

definitions.note: Command (tú) form with attached object pronoun "la".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévala al médico, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take her to the doctor, please.

definitions.native: take (it) to him/her, take (it) to you (formal)
definitions.note: Command form of “llevar” with the indirect object pronoun “le” attached (“to him/her/you formal”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévale el libro a Ana, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take the book to Ana.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú): "Take it."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te gusta, llévalo contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you like it, take it with you.

definitions.note: Command (tú) + "me" (to me). Often "bring me" when the destination is where the speaker is going; "take me" when focusing on going somewhere else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévame a casa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take me home, please.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) with the object pronoun “nos” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, llévanos al hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take us to the hotel.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) with “se” (often used like “take it with you” / “go ahead and take it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévate el paraguas; va a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take the umbrella with you; it’s going to rain.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) with the pronouns "te" (to yourself) and "lo" (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te gusta, llévatelo a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you like it, take it home with you.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with the object pronoun "me" attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, lléveme al hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take me to the hotel.

definitions.note: Command (ustedes) with the reflexive pronoun: “take yourselves off / leave” or “take [something] with you” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si ya terminaron, llévense sus cosas y vámonos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you’re already finished, take your things with you and let’s go.

definitions.note: Formal (usted) command; often used with "se" to mean taking something with you/for yourself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévese este paraguas, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take this umbrella with you.

definitions.note: Neuter form of the definite article; used before adjectives or phrases to turn them into a noun (often translated as “what …” or “the … thing”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo mejor es estudiar un poco cada día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The best thing is to study a little every day.

definitions.note: Neuter article used with adjectives/adverbs or clauses to talk about something abstract or unspecified (e.g., "lo bueno" = "the good thing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo importante es descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The important thing is to rest.

definitions.note: masculine singular direct object pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No lo sé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El lobo vive en el bosque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wolf lives in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el bosque viven lobos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wolves live in the forest.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana está loca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is crazy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busco un restaurante local para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking for a local restaurant for dinner.

definitions.note: Often refers to a business location or venue (a physical space).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El restaurante cambió de local el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The restaurant changed premises last year.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay varios restaurantes locales cerca del hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several local restaurants near the hotel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta localidad es pequeña, pero muy bonita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This town is small, but very pretty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La localización del hotel está cerca del centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel’s location is close to downtown.

definitions.note: Often used for finding the exact position of something (a place, an object, or a person).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enamoraron locamente.

definitions.note: feminine plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are crazy about music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me puse loción en las manos porque estaban secas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put lotion on my hands because they were dry.

definitions.note: Often used informally; it can be playful among friends, but can also be insulting depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estás loco si crees que voy a pagar eso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re crazy if you think I’m going to pay that.

definitions.note: Commonly used informally; can be insulting depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese loco está gritando en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That crazy guy is shouting in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigos están locos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are crazy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue una locura aceptar ese trabajo sin pensarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was madness to accept that job without thinking about it.

definitions.note: Often used for a radio or TV host; can also refer to a voice-over speaker.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El locutor presentó las noticias en la radio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The announcer presented the news on the radio.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la lluvia, el camino estaba lleno de lodo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, the path was full of mud.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "lograr"; it often means succeeding in doing something.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por fin logró terminar el proyecto a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She finally managed to finish the project on time.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a lot of effort, they managed to finish the project on time.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) informal singular (tú).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You did it!

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I manage to finish the report today.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Winning the prize was a great achievement for her.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We celebrate your achievements this year.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I managed to finish the project on time.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The parrot talks and repeats words.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boys are playing in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los veo todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see them every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los vi ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw them yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré un lote de manzanas para hacer pastel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a batch of apples to make pie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese lote está en venta desde el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That plot of land has been for sale since last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré un boleto de lotería.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a lottery ticket.

definitions.note: Often used for how something looks (e.g., clothing) or for the sun shining.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sol luce hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun is shining today.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fight was long, but we didn’t give up.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister fights for her rights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He luchado por mis sueños.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fight for their rights.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are fighting for their rights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella lucha para llegar a fin de mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She struggles to make ends meet.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) of "luchar" for "they/you all" (Spain).

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Luché por mis sueños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fought for my dreams.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/it fought; you (formal) fought.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fought for his family.

definitions.native: to look good, to show off (something)

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese vestido te hace lucir muy bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That dress makes you look very good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del concierto, marcharon a casa en silencio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the concert, they walked home in silence.

definitions.note: Reflexive form used to mean leaving (often from a place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me marcho ahora porque es tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm leaving now because it's late.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached pronoun “te” (marcharse = to leave/go away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que marcharte ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to leave now.

definitions.note: Often appears in the present subjunctive (e.g., "que yo/él marche") and can also be a formal command for usted ("Marche").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que él marche con nosotros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he walks with us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que marches en el desfile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to march in the parade.

definitions.note: Often used in the negative command “no marches” = “don’t leave.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No marches todavía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t leave yet.

definitions.note: Very commonly used with the pronoun “me”: “me marcho” = “I’m leaving.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me marcho ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm leaving now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Marcho en el desfile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I march in the parade.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/it left or marched; you (formal) left or marched.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la reunión, marchó sin decir nada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the meeting, he/she left without saying anything.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something related to war, soldiers, or military style.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El desfile tuvo un aire marcial.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The parade had a martial air.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el desfile hubo demostraciones marciales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the parade there were martial demonstrations.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse la foto en un marco de madera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the photo in a wooden frame.

definitions.native: mark (coin; former currency of several European countries)
definitions.note: Used mainly in historical or foreign-currency contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esa época, pagaban en marcos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that era, they paid in marks.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/it marked; you (formal) marked.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor marcó las respuestas correctas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher marked the correct answers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La marea está alta hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tide is high today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy mareado y necesito sentarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dizzy and I need to sit down.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (me/te/le) in Spanish: «Me mareo…» = «I get dizzy…».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me mareo cuando leo en el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get dizzy when I read in the car.

definitions.note: Less common than the ‘I get dizzy’ meaning; usually takes a direct object: «Te mareo…» = «I make you dizzy…».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te mareo con tantas preguntas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I make you dizzy with so many questions.

definitions.note: Plural of "mar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los mares están tranquilos hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The seas are calm today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quieres mantequilla o margarina?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want butter or margarine?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse una margarita en un jarrón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put a daisy in a vase.

definitions.note: In Spanish, this usually refers to the tequila-based cocktail.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a pedir una margarita, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to order a margarita, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las margaritas son mis flores favoritas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Daisies are my favorite flowers.

definitions.note: Refers to the cocktail (often made with tequila and lime).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomamos dos margaritas después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had two margaritas after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escribe una nota en el margen de la página.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write a note in the margin of the page.

definitions.note: Vulgar and highly offensive slur for a gay man in Spanish. Avoid using it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No uses la palabra “marica”; es ofensiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t use the word “marica”; it’s offensive.

definitions.note: Strongly offensive homophobic slur in Spanish; avoid using it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No uses la palabra "maricón"; es un insulto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t use the word “faggot”; it’s an insult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi marido trabaja en un hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My husband works in a hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis maridos son muy amables.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My husbands are very kind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La marihuana es ilegal en algunos países.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marijuana is illegal in some countries.

definitions.note: Usually used in phrases like “la marina” or “la marina de guerra” (the navy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano trabaja en la marina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother works in the navy.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La biología marina estudia los organismos del mar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marine biology studies the organisms of the sea.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las aves marinas vuelan sobre el océano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marine birds fly over the ocean.

definitions.note: Usually used as a feminine noun in Spanish: la marina.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo trabajó en la marina muchos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather worked in the navy for many years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo fue marinero durante muchos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather was a sailor for many years.

definitions.note: Masculine plural; refers to male sailors or a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los marineros trabajan en el barco durante meses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sailors work on the ship for months.

definitions.note: Often used to describe things related to the sea (e.g., life, environment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estudiamos la vida marina en clase de ciencias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We study marine life in science class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño juega con una marioneta de madera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy plays with a wooden puppet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mariposa tiene alas de colores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The butterfly has colorful wings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En primavera, vemos muchas mariposas en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, we see many butterflies in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used as a military rank (e.g., field marshal) or an official title.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El mariscal dirigió el desfile militar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The marshal led the military parade.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural when talking about seafood as a category or a dish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a pedir mariscos para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to order seafood for dinner.

definitions.note: Can be the present subjunctive form of “marcar” (e.g., “Es importante que marque la respuesta correcta”) or a formal command (usted) meaning “mark!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que marque la respuesta correcta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you mark the correct answer.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo unos zapatos marrones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have some brown shoes.

definitions.note: Often used for color; it doesn’t change for gender (el coche marrón, la mesa marrón).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una chaqueta marrón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a brown jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El martes tengo una reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Tuesday I have a meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un martillo para colgar el cuadro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a hammer to hang the picture.

definitions.note: Written with an accent: “más” (not to be confused with “mas” meaning “but,” which is less common).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero más agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want more water, please.

definitions.note: This is the form without an accent; it’s usually written as “más”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero mas agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want more water, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La panadera mezcla la masa para hacer pan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baker mixes the dough to make bread.

definitions.note: In science and general use, it refers to the amount of matter in something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La masa de la Tierra es enorme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mass of the Earth is enormous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La masacre conmocionó al país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The massacre shocked the country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del entrenamiento, me hice un masaje en la espalda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After training, I got a massage on my back.

definitions.note: Often used for a medical or protective face mask.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ponte la mascarilla antes de entrar al hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put on your mask before entering the hospital.

definitions.note: Also used for a skin-care product applied to the face.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me pongo una mascarilla facial una vez a la semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on a facial mask once a week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mascota se llama Luna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My pet is named Luna.

definitions.note: Plural of “mascota”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis mascotas son un perro y un gato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My pets are a dog and a cat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El nombre "Carlos" es masculino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The name "Carlos" is masculine.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los nombres masculinos suelen terminar en -o.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Masculine nouns usually end in -o.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La campaña masiva empezó esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The massive campaign started this week.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "masticar"; often used with "estar" to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy masticando chicle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am chewing gum.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que masticar bien la comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to chew your food well.

definitions.note: Can be present tense (he/she/it kills; you formal kill) or the tú command “kill”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato mata a los ratones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat kills the mice.

definitions.native: they were killing, they used to kill
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (3rd person plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Antes, en esa zona mataban animales para vender la carne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before, in that area they used to kill animals to sell the meat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El mosquito fue matado por Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mosquito was killed by Ana.

definitions.note: Can be either present (we kill) or preterite (we killed), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si vemos una serpiente, la matamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we see a snake, we kill it.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they kill / you all kill).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los mosquitos matan a muchos animales pequeños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mosquitoes kill many small animals.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "matar"; often used with "estar" to form "is/are killing".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato está matando un ratón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is killing a mouse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La matanza de animales está prohibida en esta zona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The slaughter of animals is prohibited in this area.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero matar a nadie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to kill anyone.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “matar”, often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., after “si”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si él matara a la serpiente, estaríamos a salvo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he killed the snake, we would be safe.

definitions.note: Often used in the past subjunctive, especially after expressions like "quería que" or in "si" clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez pidió que no mataran a nadie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge asked that they not kill anyone.

definitions.note: Includes the attached direct object pronoun “la” (“her/it”, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero matarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to kill her.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “le” (“to him/her/you formal”). In many places you may also hear “matarlo/matarla” instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero matarle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to kill him/her.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (him/it) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero matarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to kill him.

definitions.note: Object pronouns attached to the infinitive: los = “them” (masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero matarlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to kill them.

definitions.note: Infinitive with attached object pronoun “me” (= “me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No vas a matarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're not going to kill me.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with "nos" ("ourselves").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No vamos a matarnos por un error.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re not going to kill ourselves over a mistake.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural: “they killed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mataron al dragón al final del cuento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They killed the dragon at the end of the story.

definitions.note: Contains the pronoun “os” (= you plural, informal, used in Spain) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quieren mataros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to kill you (all).

definitions.note: Reflexive form of “matar”; can refer to suicide or accidentally dying (depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se mató en un accidente de coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He died in a car accident.

definitions.note: Uses the informal singular object pronoun “te” (= you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero matarte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to kill you.

definitions.note: Can be reflexive, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedes matarte por ese error.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can't kill yourself over that mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si entra, lo matará.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he comes in, he will kill him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si entran, los guardias los matarán.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they come in, the guards will kill them.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me atacas, te mataré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you attack me, I will kill you.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "matar" (used for hypotheticals or polite statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si alguien entrara en mi casa, lo mataría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If someone came into my house, I would kill him.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú), simple past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué mataste al insecto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you kill the insect?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato mate al ratón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat killed the mouse.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a surface or finish that is not glossy or shiny.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prefiero la pintura mate para las paredes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer matte paint for the walls.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La matemática es importante en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mathematics is important in school.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural in Spanish when referring to the school subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo examen de matemáticas mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a math exam tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este problema es muy matemático.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This problem is very mathematical.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi tío es matemático y trabaja en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is a mathematician and works at the university.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "matar" (used after phrases like "Espero que...", "Es posible que...", etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no maten al animal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they don’t kill the animal.

definitions.note: Used for an academic subject or a school/university class.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi materia favorita es historia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My favorite subject is history.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos comprar material para el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to buy material for the project.

definitions.note: Plural of "material".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos comprar materiales para el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to buy materials for the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es muy materialista y siempre quiere comprar cosas caras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very materialistic and always wants to buy expensive things.

definitions.note: Usually refers to school or academic subjects.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este semestre tengo cinco materias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This semester I have five subjects.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tiene una actitud materna con sus alumnos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a maternal attitude with her students.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often used in the phrase “lengua materna”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El español es mi lengua materna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spanish is my mother tongue.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El amor materno puede ser muy fuerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maternal love can be very strong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No mato animales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't kill animals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero problemas con esos matones.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su matrimonio es muy feliz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their marriage is very happy.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city, many marriages are celebrated in summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta tabla está organizada en una matriz de 3 por 3.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This table is organized in a 3-by-3 matrix.

definitions.note: Often used for enrolling/registering in a school or course; can also refer to the fee paid for it.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Enrollment for the course starts on Monday.

definitions.note: First-person singular, simple past (pretérito): "I killed" / "I did kill."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo maté por accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I killed him by accident.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cazador mató al lobo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hunter killed the wolf.

definitions.note: Often refers to a violent or intimidating person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El matón del barrio amenazó a un chico en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighborhood thug threatened a boy in the street.

definitions.note: Present participle (gerund) of “maullar”; used to describe an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato está maullando en la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is meowing at the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ponle mayonesa al sándwich, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put mayonnaise on the sandwich, please.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "grande" (big/large).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a bigger table for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Baraja el mazo antes de repartir las cartas.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana tengo una reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have a meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana es mi cumpleaños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow is my birthday.

definitions.note: Often used in the expression "por la mañana" = "in the morning."

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the morning I study Spanish.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me with the homework?

definitions.note: Vulgar/impolite in many contexts; "orinar" is more neutral.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que mear.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This mechanism opens the door automatically.

definitions.note: Masculine plural noun.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo murió el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather died last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no encontramos agua, moriremos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we don’t find water, we will die.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an indirect object pronoun; often used to mean “to die (myself)” or “to be dying.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandpa died last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no bebes agua, morirás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t drink water, you will die.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “morir” (used for hypotheticals or polite statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sin agua, moriría en el desierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without water, I would die in the desert.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sin agua, las plantas morirían en pocos días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without water, the plants would die in a few days.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La morsa vive en aguas frías del Ártico.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El accidente no fue mortal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esas heridas pueden ser mortales si no recibes tratamiento.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer morí en el videojuego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I died in the video game.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first-person singular: “I died.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morí de miedo cuando vi la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was scared to death when I saw the movie.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): describes an ongoing situation or a repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegó la ambulancia, él moría en el suelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the ambulance arrived, he was dying on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay una mosca en la cocina.
