definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchas moscas en la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many flies in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos mosquitos en el jardín por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are a lot of mosquitoes in the yard at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos mosquitos en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many mosquitoes in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quieres mostaza en el sándwich?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want mustard on the sandwich?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all were showing); can describe an ongoing or repeated action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el museo, los guías mostraban las pinturas a los visitantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the museum, the guides were showing the paintings to the visitors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya te he mostrado mi pasaporte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already shown you my passport.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a shop or service counter (e.g., in a store, bar, or hotel).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cajera está detrás del mostrador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cashier is behind the counter.

definitions.note: Rioplatense (vos) affirmative command form; equivalent to “muéstrame” in many other varieties.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mostrame la foto, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Show me the photo, please.

definitions.note: Present tense: “we show.” Also used in the preterite: “we showed” (context usually makes it clear).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te mostramos cómo funciona la aplicación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We show you how the app works.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Me puedes mostrar tu pasaporte, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you show me your passport, please?

definitions.native: show him, show her, show you (formal)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to him/her/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a mostrarle la foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to show you the photo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero mostrarles una foto de mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to show them a photo of my family.

definitions.note: Attached object pronoun: "me" = "to me" / "me".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes mostrarme tu pasaporte?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you show me your passport?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me mostraron el camino al hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They showed me the way to the hotel.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “te” (“you”, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero mostrarte una foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to show you a photo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El guía mostrará el museo a los visitantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide will show the museum to the visitors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te mostraré las fotos mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will show you the photos tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te mostré las fotos ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I showed you the photos yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "mostrar" (he/she/it showed; you (formal) showed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella me mostró una foto de su familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed me a photo of her family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos quedamos en un motel cerca del aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We stayed at a motel near the airport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito motivación para estudiar todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need motivation to study every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy muy motivado para aprender español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very motivated to learn Spanish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo ningún motivo para mentir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no reason to lie.

definitions.note: Plural of "motivo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo varios motivos para quedarme en casa hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have several reasons to stay at home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia lo motivó a estudiar más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news motivated him to study more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy al trabajo en moto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to work by motorcycle.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother goes to work on a motorcycle.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car’s engine makes a lot of noise.

definitions.note: Plural of "motor".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los motores del avión son muy potentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane's engines are very powerful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta calle hay muchas motos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On this street there are many motorcycles.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (move something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a mover la mesa a la izquierda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to move the table to the left.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun “me” (to move myself / to get moving).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito moverme un poco después de estar sentado todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to move a little after sitting all day.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun “nos” (“us/ourselves”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que movernos si no queremos llegar tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to move if we don’t want to arrive late.

definitions.note: Reflexive: often means changing position or moving oneself (e.g., get moving).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito moverme un poco después de estar sentado todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to move a little after sitting all day.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the reflexive pronoun “te” attached; often used after another verb (e.g., “necesitas moverte”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que moverte más durante el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to move more during the day.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “mover.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy moviendo la mesa para limpiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m moving the table to clean.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren está moviendo muy despacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is moving very slowly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El movimiento del agua es relajante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movement of the water is relaxing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus movimientos fueron rápidos y precisos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His movements were fast and precise.

definitions.note: Common in banking/finance contexts (e.g., account activity).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revisé los movimientos de mi cuenta bancaria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I reviewed the transactions on my bank account.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; often translates as “moving” or “moving around.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato está moviéndose debajo de la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is moving under the table.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of “mover” for él/ella/usted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella movió la mesa para limpiar el suelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She moved the table to clean the floor.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past). Often used with reflexive pronouns (me/te/se/nos/os/se) when it means “to move (oneself)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De niño, me movía mucho cuando escuchaba música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I moved around a lot when I listened to music.

definitions.note: Common in Spain; in many Latin American countries, “mesero” is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El mozo nos trajo el menú y el agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter brought us the menu and the water.

definitions.note: feminine singular form; used with feminine singular nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo mucha tarea hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of homework today.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used with feminine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo mucha tarea hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of homework today.

definitions.note: Often used for a young woman; in some places it can also refer to a female servant (context-dependent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La muchacha está en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl is in the park.

definitions.note: Refers to a young female; often used similarly to “girl” or “young woman.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La muchacha está en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl is in the park.

definitions.note: plural; often used for girls/young women in a friendly, informal way
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las muchachas están en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese muchacho vive en mi barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That boy lives in my neighborhood.

definitions.note: Plural of “muchacho”. Often used informally to address a group of male friends or a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muchachos, ¿vamos al cine después de clase?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guys, are we going to the movies after class?

definitions.note: Used before feminine plural nouns (agreement with the noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchas amigas en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many friends in Madrid.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; used with feminine plural nouns (e.g., “muchas cosas”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchas preguntas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many questions.

definitions.note: Refers to a large group of people gathered together.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Una muchedumbre se reunió en la plaza para escuchar el concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A crowd gathered in the square to listen to the concert.

definitions.note: Often used to intensify verbs (Me gusta mucho = “I like it a lot”). Also used with comparatives (mucho mejor = “much better”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta mucho esta canción.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this song a lot.

definitions.note: As a determiner, it agrees with the noun: mucha, muchos, muchas.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay mucho ruido aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a lot of noise here.

definitions.note: As a pronoun, it refers to an unspecified large amount (e.g., “much of it,” “a lot”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have much.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used before plural masculine (or mixed-gender) nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos estudiantes en la clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many students in the class.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used before a masculine plural noun (e.g., “muchos libros”) or as a pronoun (“muchos”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muchos piensan que es una buena idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people think it's a good idea.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form used before a feminine singular noun (e.g., “muchísima agua”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchísima tarea hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of homework today.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; often used for emphasis.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchísimas personas en el parque hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are so many people in the park today.

definitions.note: Emphatic form of “mucho”; means “a lot/very much.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta muchísimo esta canción.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this song very much.

definitions.note: Emphatic form of "mucho" (means "a whole lot").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchísimo trabajo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of work today.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; emphasizes a large number (stronger than "muchos").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchísimos estudiantes en la biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are very many students in the library.

definitions.note: Often used with "mudarse" to mean moving to a new home (change residence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me he mudado a un apartamento nuevo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve moved to a new apartment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El plan ha mudado con el tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan has changed over time.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” to mean changing from one thing to another (e.g., “mudar de ropa”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En invierno mudamos de ropa y usamos abrigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter we change clothes and wear coats.

definitions.note: For moving house, Spanish more commonly uses “mudarse” (reflexive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy mudamos los muebles al otro cuarto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we move the furniture to the other room.

definitions.note: Often used for moving house ("mudarse") or changing clothes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos mudando de casa este fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re moving house this weekend.

definitions.note: Usually refers to changing residence and/or the process of transporting belongings.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mudanza a nuestro nuevo apartamento fue agotadora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The move to our new apartment was exhausting.

definitions.note: Often used for the service of moving house (a moving company).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana hacemos las mudanzas a nuestro nuevo apartamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we’re moving into our new apartment.

definitions.note: Often used as "mudarse" when talking about moving to a new home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a mudar la oficina al centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to move the office downtown.

definitions.note: Literally “to move myself” (with the pronoun “me”); used for moving house/apartments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a mudarme el mes que viene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to move next month.

definitions.note: Usually refers to changing residence; in some contexts it can mean to change something (like clothes), but the most common beginner meaning is moving house.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El año pasado mudaron a un apartamento más grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year they moved to a bigger apartment.

definitions.native: to move (house), to move (to a new place)
definitions.note: Reflexive form used when someone changes where they live.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me voy a mudar a Madrid el mes que viene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to move to Madrid next month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El teléfono está en modo mudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is on mute mode.

definitions.note: Most commonly means you changed clothes or moved (to a new place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer mudé de apartamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I moved to a new apartment.

definitions.note: Often used as "mudarse" to mean "to move (to a new home/city)."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se mudó a Madrid el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She moved to Madrid last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos un mueble nuevo para la sala.

definitions.note: Plural form of "mueble"; usually used as a collective noun for furniture in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos comprar muebles para el salón.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duele una muela.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather has died.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi teléfono está muerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone is dead.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos muestran sus fotos a la clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They show their photos to the class.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please show your passport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que usted mueva el coche mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you move the car tomorrow.

definitions.note: Usually used with a reflexive pronoun (me/te/se/nos/os/se).

definitions.note: Used with "te" (reflexive) in "moverse".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted him/her/you (formal) to swim more often.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they swam in the lake.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swim every day in the pool.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like "nado sincronizado" (synchronized swimming).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta el nado porque es un buen ejercicio.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer nadé en el mar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I swam in the sea.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer, ella nadó en la piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, she swam in the pool.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nana cuida a los niños después de la escuela.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it’s invariable: naranja for masculine and feminine, singular and plural.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré naranjas en el mercado.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay un naranjo en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an orange tree in the patio.

definitions.note: Usually refers to illegal drugs; in medical contexts it can mean strong painkillers (opioids).

definitions.note: Plural of "nariz".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Clowns wear red noses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duele la nariz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My nose hurts.

definitions.note: Usually means the thick dairy cream used in cooking; in some regions it can refer to whipped cream (often called “nata montada”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Add a little cream to the soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La natación es mi deporte favorito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Swimming is my favorite sport.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “país natal” (birth country) or “ciudad natal” (hometown).

definitions.note: Used especially in demographics/statistics.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The birth rate has gone down in recent years.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "nativo".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is native to Peru.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estas plantas son nativas de esta región.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These plants are native to this region.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El español es mi idioma nativo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spanish is my native language.

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone who is native to a place (e.g., un nativo de México).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es nativa de Colombia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a native of Colombia.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also be used for a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los idiomas nativos de mis abuelos son el quechua y el español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents' native languages are Quechua and Spanish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los nativos de la isla conocen muy bien estas rutas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The natives of the island know these routes very well.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "líder nato" to mean someone is naturally good at something.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a born leader.

definitions.note: Japanese food; commonly used in Spanish just as the loanword “natto”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried natto for the first time at a Japanese restaurant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prefiero comida natural, sin aditivos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer natural food, without additives.

definitions.note: Plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These juices are natural.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me encanta la naturaleza, especialmente las montañas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love nature, especially the mountains.

definitions.note: Often refers to behaving in a relaxed, unforced way.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke naturally during the interview.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Naturalmente, puedes venir con nosotros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Of course, you can come with us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El naufragio ocurrió cerca de la costa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shipwreck happened near the coast.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a folding knife.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nave llegó al puerto por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship arrived at the port in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La navegación por el río es peligrosa en invierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Navigation on the river is dangerous in winter.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about using websites or moving around in an app or on the internet (e.g., “navegación por internet”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Web browsing is faster with this connection.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a web browser in computing contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi navegador no abre esa página.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My browser won't open that page.

definitions.note: A person or device that guides a route (e.g., on a ship or in a car).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship's navigator checked the map.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos navegando hacia una isla pequeña.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m browsing the internet to look for a hotel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos gusta navegar por el mar en verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We like to sail on the sea in the summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a navegar por internet para buscar información.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to browse the internet to look for information.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form: “he/she/it sailed” or “you (formal) sailed.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship sailed all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las naves llegaron al puerto al amanecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ships arrived at the port at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En Navidad, mi familia cena junta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At Christmas, my family has dinner together.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective in Spanish too (e.g., “régimen nazi”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My great-grandfather fought against the Nazis in the war.

definitions.note: Plural form of "nazi".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los nazis llegaron al poder en 1933.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Nazis came to power in 1933.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por la mañana hay neblina en la carretera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the morning there is mist on the road.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es necesaria una copia de tu pasaporte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A copy of your passport is necessary.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “not necessarily” in phrases like “no necesariamente”.

definitions.note: feminine plural form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tools are necessary for the job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es necesario estudiar para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is necessary to study for the exam.

definitions.note: masculine plural form

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo la necesidad de descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the need to rest.

definitions.note: Plural of "necesidad".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have many needs right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesita ayuda con la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Needs help with the homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitaba ayuda para terminar el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I needed help to finish the project.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all needed).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were students, they needed more time to study.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you lived in the countryside, you needed a car to go to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He necesitado ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have needed help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos comprar comida para la semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to buy food for the week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito ayuda con esta tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need help with this assignment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana necesitaremos más tiempo para terminar el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will need more time to finish the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella necesitará ayuda mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will need help tomorrow.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana necesitarás tu pasaporte para viajar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito ayuda con esta tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need help with this homework assignment.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I needed help with the homework.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He denied the accusation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo negarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't deny it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos negaron las acusaciones.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La respuesta fue negativa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El resultado de la prueba fue negativo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The test result was negative.

definitions.note: feminine singular form

definitions.note: feminine plural form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boots are black.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; also used for mixed-gender groups.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two black cats.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form. In some contexts it can be offensive; use with care.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él negó haber dicho eso.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl is playing in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students are nervous before the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The milk is in the refrigerator.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una razón particular para venir hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a particular reason for coming today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta el chocolate, particularmente el negro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like chocolate, especially dark chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La partida empieza a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The game starts at eight.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los partidarios del equipo celebraron la victoria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team's supporters celebrated the victory.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a sports match/game.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El partido empieza a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The match starts at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es miembro de un partido político.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a member of a political party.

definitions.note: Past participle of "partir" used with "haber" to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He partido temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have left early.

definitions.note: Past participle of "partir" used as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El vaso está partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is broken (split).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos dos partidos de fútbol ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We watched two soccer matches yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En España hay muchos partidos políticos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Spain there are many political parties.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): “they/you all left.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partieron temprano para llegar antes del anochecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left early to arrive before nightfall.

definitions.native: we left, we split, we divided
definitions.note: Can mean either leaving (e.g., departing) or dividing something, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partimos temprano para llegar a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We left early to arrive on time.

definitions.note: Used as a noun meaning “the act of leaving,” but it’s uncommon in everyday Spanish (more often you’ll see a verb form like “partir” meaning “to leave”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su partir fue repentino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His departure was sudden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que partir ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to leave now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a partir la pizza en ocho pedazos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to split the pizza into eight pieces.

definitions.native: we will leave, we will depart
definitions.note: Future tense (nosotros). Often used for leaving on a trip or departing at a certain time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partiremos mañana por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will leave tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite): he/she/you (formal) left.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partió temprano para llegar a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She left early to arrive on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El parto fue rápido y sin complicaciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The childbirth was quick and without complications.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "partir" (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Partí temprano para llegar a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left early to arrive on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay partículas de polvo en el aire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are dust particles in the air.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los perros pueden tener parásitos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dogs can have parasites.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Paré el coche en el semáforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stopped the car at the traffic light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pon esa frase entre paréntesis, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put that sentence in parentheses, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular of "parar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El autobús paró frente a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus stopped in front of the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren pasa por aquí todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train passes by here every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué pasa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What’s happening?

definitions.native: was happening, was passing, used to go by
definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "pasar" (it describes something ongoing in the past or something that used to happen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pasaba el tiempo y no recibía respuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time was going by and I wasn’t getting an answer.

definitions.native: they were passing, they used to pass
definitions.note: Imperfect tense of “pasar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos pasaban por mi casa todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They used to pass by my house every day.

definitions.note: Often used for a pass in sports (like soccer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hizo una pasada perfecta al delantero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a perfect pass to the forward.

definitions.note: Colloquial (especially in Spain): "una pasada" means something is amazing or unbelievable.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡El concierto fue una pasada!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert was amazing!

definitions.note: Often used with time words (e.g., "la semana pasada" = "last week").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La semana pasada fui al cine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last week I went to the movies.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las semanas pasadas fueron muy ocupadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The past weeks were very busy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pasadizo es muy estrecho y oscuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The passageway is very narrow and dark.

definitions.note: Often used in time expressions like "la semana pasada" (last week).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El mes pasado viajé a México.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last month I traveled to Mexico.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me gusta hablar del pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like talking about the past.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pasar"; often used with "haber" to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He pasado por tu casa esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I passed by your house this morning.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En los años pasados, vivíamos en otra ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In past years, we lived in another city.

definitions.note: Often used for travel tickets (bus, plane, train).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré un pasaje de ida y vuelta a Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a round-trip ticket to Madrid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pasajero mostró su boleto al entrar al autobús.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The passenger showed his ticket when getting on the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los pasajeros ya están en el avión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The passengers are already on the plane.

definitions.note: Commonly used for transport (e.g., plane, bus, train) tickets.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré dos pasajes de tren para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two train tickets for tomorrow.

definitions.native: we pass, we go by, we spend (time)
definitions.note: First-person plural present tense of “pasar” (also used for “we passed” in the simple past, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pasamos por tu casa todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go by your house every day.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "pasar" (also used for "you" plural in Spain: "vosotros pasáis").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los días pasan muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The days go by very fast.

definitions.note: Usually used as a gerund (-ing form), often with "estar" to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy pasando por tu casa ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m passing by your house now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito mi pasaporte para viajar a Estados Unidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need my passport to travel to the United States.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos nuestros pasaportes para viajar a Canadá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need our passports to travel to Canada.

definitions.note: Often used for time passing or something/someone passing by.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tiempo pasa muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time goes by very fast.

definitions.note: Common with time expressions: "pasar el día/la noche".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a pasar el fin de semana en la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to spend the weekend at the beach.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "pasar" (yo/él/ella/usted): often used after "si" (if) or after past-tense expressions (e.g., "quería que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si pasara algo, llámame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If something happened, call me.

definitions.native: we will pass, we will go, we will spend (time)
definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros) future tense of “pasar.” Meaning depends on context (e.g., passing by, going somewhere, or spending time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana pasaremos por tu casa antes de ir al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we’ll go by your house before going to work.

definitions.note: Often used with an adverb like “bien” (well) or “mal” (badly): “pasarla bien/mal”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a pasarla bien en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to have a good time at the party.

definitions.native: to pass (something) to him, to pass (something) to her
definitions.note: "le" means "to him/to her/to you (formal)" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes pasarle la sal a tu mamá?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass the salt to your mom?

definitions.native: to happen to him, to happen to her
definitions.note: "le" means "to him/to her/to you (formal)" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero que le pase nada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want anything to happen to him/her.

definitions.native: to pass me, to hand me
definitions.note: Infinitive of “pasar” with the indirect object pronoun “me” attached (e.g., to pass something to me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes pasarme la sal, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pass me the salt, please?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural of “pasar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pasaron dos horas muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two hours went by very quickly.

definitions.native: to overdo it, to go too far
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero pasarme con el azúcar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to overdo it with the sugar.

definitions.native: to miss (a stop), to go past (where you should get off)
definitions.note: Often used for missing a bus/metro stop or going past the place you meant to stop.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bájate aquí para no pasarte de la parada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get off here so you don’t miss the stop.

definitions.native: to overdo it, to go too far
definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “te” (“you”, informal), as in “pasarse” = to go too far / overdo it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No debes pasarte con el azúcar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn't overdo it with the sugar.

definitions.native: will happen, will pass, will go by
definitions.note: Third-person singular (él/ella/usted) future tense of “pasar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé qué pasará mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know what will happen tomorrow.

definitions.native: will pass, will go by, will happen
definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) future form of "pasar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana pasarán por mi casa a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will come by my house at eight.

definitions.native: you will pass, you will go (by), you will spend (time)
definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense of "pasar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana pasarás por mi casa después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will stop by my house after work.

definitions.native: I will pass, I will go by, I will spend (time)
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) future tense of “pasar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana pasaré por tu casa después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’ll stop by your house after work.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "pasar"; often used for hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tuviera tiempo, pasaría por tu casa esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had time, I would stop by your house this afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gustan las pasas en la ensalada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like raisins in the salad.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) form of “pasar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué pasas por aquí todos los días?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you pass by here every day?

definitions.native: you passed, you went by, you spent (time)
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "pasar" for "tú".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Pasaste por mi casa ayer?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you go by my house yesterday?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leer es mi pasatiempo favorito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Reading is my favorite hobby.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis pasatiempos son leer y cocinar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hobbies are reading and cooking.

definitions.note: Used as a formal (usted) command and also as the present subjunctive form of "pasar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pase por aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come this way, please.

definitions.note: Often used for an entry pass (like for an event, museum, or transportation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un pase para entrar al concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a pass to get into the concert.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "pasear"; often used for taking a leisurely walk (sometimes with a pet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella pasea por el parque todas las tardes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She walks through the park every afternoon.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “pasear”; often used with “estar” to mean “to be walking/going for a walk.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy paseando por el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m walking through the park.

definitions.native: to take a walk, to go for a walk
definitions.note: Often used for a leisurely walk; can also mean to walk someone/something (like a dog) as in “pasear al perro.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta pasear por el parque después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to take a walk through the park after dinner.

definitions.note: First-person plural present subjunctive, often used to make a suggestion ("let’s...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pasemos al siguiente tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s move on to the next topic.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite command or invitation (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, pasen y tomen asiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come in and take a seat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dimos un paseo por el parque después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took a walk through the park after dinner.

definitions.note: Often used after expressions like "espero que..." or "quiero que..." (subjunctive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que pases por mi casa mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you stop by my house tomorrow.

definitions.note: Plural of "pase" (noun). Often used for tickets or entry passes to an event or place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes dos pases para el concierto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have two passes for the concert?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pasillo es muy estrecho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hallway is very narrow.

definitions.note: Also commonly used about a person who doesn’t take initiative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En clase, Pedro es muy pasivo y casi no participa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In class, Pedro is very passive and hardly participates.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento una gran pasión por la música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a great passion for music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Paso por tu casa después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go by your house after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da un paso hacia atrás, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a step back, please.

definitions.note: Plural of "paso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Di dos pasos hacia atrás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took two steps back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy comimos pasta con salsa de tomate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we ate pasta with tomato sauce.

definitions.note: Often used for a thick mixture (for example toothpaste).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprar pasta de dientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy toothpaste.

definitions.note: In some regions (especially Mexico), it can mean a frosted cake, often for birthdays.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré un pastel de chocolate para el cumpleaños de Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a chocolate cake for Ana’s birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré pasteles para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought cakes and pastries for the party.

definitions.note: Often used for medicine; it can also mean a lozenge (like a cough drop) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que tomarme una pastilla después de comer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take a pill after eating.

definitions.note: Commonly used for medicine (e.g., painkillers). It can also mean lozenges/tablets depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que tomar dos pastillas al día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take two pills a day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pasto del parque está muy verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grass in the park is very green.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pastor cuida a las ovejas en el campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shepherd takes care of the sheep in the countryside.

definitions.note: Religious leader, especially in a Protestant church.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pastor habla con la comunidad después del servicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pastor talks with the community after the service.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los pastores cuidan a las ovejas en el campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shepherds take care of the sheep in the countryside.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of "pasar" for "yo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer pasé por tu casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I went by your house.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “pasar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren pasó a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train passed at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro tiene una pata herida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog has an injured paw.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dio una patada a la pelota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She kicked the ball.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dieron varias patadas a la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave the door several kicks.

definitions.note: Often used for animals (paws/legs). For people it can be informal/slang for “legs.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro tiene las patas sucias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog has dirty paws.

definitions.note: In many parts of Latin America, people more commonly say "papa" for this.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero una patata asada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a baked potato.

definitions.note: Common in Spain; in much of Latin America, “papas” is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero patatas con huevos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want potatoes with eggs.

definitions.note: Often used for a driver’s license in many Latin American countries; in Spain, “driver’s license” is usually “carné de conducir.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que renovar la patente este mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to renew my license this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa registró una patente para su nuevo invento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company registered a patent for its new invention.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él pateó la pelota y marcó un gol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kicked the ball and scored a goal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta el patinaje sobre hielo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like ice skating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta patinar en el parque los fines de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to skate in the park on weekends.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me compré unos patines nuevos para ir al parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some new skates to go to the park.

definitions.note: In Spanish, “patio” often refers to an inner courtyard (sometimes inside a building), not only an outdoor terrace like in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños juegan en el patio de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids play in the school courtyard.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "pato" (duck); often used as a cute or affectionate term.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El patito nada en el estanque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The duckling swims in the pond.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pato nada en el lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The duck swims in the lake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay patos en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are ducks in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre lleva a su patria en el corazón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always carries his homeland in his heart.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo era un patriota y amaba mucho a su país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather was a patriot and loved his country very much.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El patriotismo es fuerte durante las fiestas nacionales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Patriotism is strong during national holidays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por la noche, las patrullas recorren el barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, the patrols go around the neighborhood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi patrón me dio el día libre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss gave me the day off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un patrón para hacer esta camisa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a pattern to make this shirt.

definitions.note: Insult: a rude, ill-mannered person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas patán; pide perdón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't be a jerk; apologize.

definitions.note: Often used to criticize something as pitiful or embarrassingly bad.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su excusa fue patética.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His excuse was pathetic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situación mejoró paulatinamente con el tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation improved gradually over time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hagamos una pausa de cinco minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's take a five-minute break.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para Navidad, comemos pavo en familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Christmas, we eat turkey as a family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El payaso hizo reír a todos en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The clown made everyone laugh at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la fiesta había muchos payasos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the party there were many clowns.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queremos vivir en paz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to live in peace.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: España es un país de Europa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spain is a country in Europe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He visitado muchos países en Europa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have visited many countries in Europe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos comprar pañales para el bebé.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to ask them for help.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to order it at the restaurant.

definitions.native: to ask me for, to request from me

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you ask me for help if you need it?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes pedirnos ayuda si la necesitas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can ask us for help if you need it.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun "te" (= you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero pedirte un favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to ask you a favor.

definitions.native: I will ask for, I will request

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana pediré ayuda si la necesito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will ask for help if I need it.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo), future tense (e.g., at a restaurant).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the restaurant I will order a soup and a salad.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "pedir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo pediría una pizza, pero no tengo dinero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would order a pizza, but I don't have money.

definitions.native: you asked for, you requested, you ordered

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you order a pizza for dinner?

definitions.note: Informal and a bit vulgar.

definitions.note: Informal / vulgar.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I farted twice and opened the window.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form used for completed actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pedí un café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ordered a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted). Often implies a repeated or ongoing action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, siempre pedía más tiempo para jugar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a kid, I always asked for more time to play.

definitions.note: A very serious and offensive term for an adult sexually attracted to children.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó a un pedófilo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested a pedophile.

definitions.note: Very informal; often used in phrases like “me pierdo” (“I’m getting lost”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m getting lost in these streets.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta cinta no pega bien.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano me pega cuando se enoja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother hits me when he gets angry.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), describing an ongoing or habitual action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, pegaba a mis hermanos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a kid, I used to hit my siblings.

definitions.note: Often used for something physically attached or hard to separate; can also mean “glued.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El chicle está pegado debajo de la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gum is stuck under the table.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something attached to a surface.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cartel está pegado a la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The poster is stuck to the wall.

definitions.note: From the verb "pegar". Depending on context it can mean "to stick" (attach) or "to hit".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las pegatinas no pegan bien en esta pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stickers don’t stick well on this wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está pegando a la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is hitting the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy pegando las fotos en el álbum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sticking/gluing the photos in the album.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a pegar esta foto en el cuaderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to stick this photo in the notebook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No debes pegar a tu hermano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not hit your brother.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “le” (“to him/her/it”), commonly used to mean “hit (someone)” in many Spanish-speaking regions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No vayas a pegarle a tu hermano.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedes pegarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can’t hit me.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The T-shirt can stick to me with sweat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pegaron a la puerta muy fuerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They hit the door very hard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me insultas, te pego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you insult me, I hit you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pego la foto en el cuaderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stick (glue) the photo in the notebook.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No pegue a su hermano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't hit your brother.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pegue esta etiqueta en la caja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stick this label on the box.

definitions.native: I hit, I stuck (on), I glued
definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), first person singular of "pegar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer pegué el póster en la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I stuck the poster on the wall.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun: "pegarle a alguien" = to hit someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño le pegó a su hermano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy hit his brother.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: "pegarse a" = to stick to.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El chicle se pegó a mi zapato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gum stuck to my shoe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta tu peinado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your hairstyle.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “valer la pena” (to be worth it) or “a duras penas” (with difficulty).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog's fur is very soft.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm peeling an orange.

definitions.note: Often used for peeling fruit/vegetables (e.g., bananas, potatoes).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That road is dangerous at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño juega con una pelota en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy plays with a ball in the park.

definitions.note: Plural of “pelota”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños juegan con pelotas en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids play with balls in the park.

definitions.note: Also used in expressions like “depende de” (“it depends on”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abrigo pende de un gancho en la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coat hangs from a hook on the wall.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" or "quedar" to mean something hasn’t been done or resolved yet.

definitions.note: This is a direct anatomical term and is considered vulgar/offensive in many everyday contexts.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense; used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past, ongoing/habitual).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They thought the exam was going to be easy.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past, ongoing/habitual).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mientras caminaban, pensaban en sus planes para el verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While they were walking, they were thinking about their plans for the summer.

definitions.native: you were thinking, you used to think

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "bien pensado" (well thought out) or "algo pensado" (something planned).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have thought about you all day.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His way of thinking is very different from mine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchos pensamientos hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many thoughts today.

definitions.note: Simple past / preterite (nosotros/nosotras).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer pensamos en ti todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we thought about you all day.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was important that I thought before speaking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana pensaremos en una solución.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will think about a solution.

definitions.note: Object pronoun "lo" = "it" (masculine singular).

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular (tú).
