definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want us to get nervous before the exam.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "poner" with the attached pronoun "os" (you all, informal Spain). Often used for clothing: "poneros" + a garment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenéis que poneros el abrigo porque hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to put on your coats because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Reflexive form of "poner" used especially for putting clothing on yourself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante ponerse el cinturón de seguridad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to put on your seat belt.

definitions.note: Often used with emotions or temporary states (e.g., "ponerse nervioso" = to get nervous).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puede ponerse nervioso antes de una entrevista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can get nervous before an interview.

definitions.note: Reflexive with an indirect object pronoun: “ponerte” = “to put on (for yourself) / to put on (you)” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a ponerte el abrigo porque hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to put your coat on you because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Dónde pones las llaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you put the keys?

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted): “Ponga…” = “Put…”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ponga el libro en la mesa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the book on the table, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (nosotros), often used to make a suggestion (like an affirmative “let’s…” command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pongamos los libros en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s put the books on the table.

definitions.note: Commonly used to introduce an example or assumption.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pongamos que mañana llueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s suppose it rains tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que pongan las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you put the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) form of "poner"; commonly used after expressions like "quiero que" or "es importante que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que pongas el libro en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to put the book on the table.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo) form of “poner”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pongo el libro en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book on the table.

definitions.note: Gerund of “poner”; used to form progressive tenses (e.g., “estoy poniendo” = “I am putting”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy poniendo los platos en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am putting the plates on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los ponis son pequeños pero muy fuertes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ponies are small but very strong.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) affirmative command. "la" refers to a feminine direct object ("it"/"her").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ponla en la mesa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put it on the table, please.

definitions.note: Affirmative command with the indirect object pronoun “le” (to him, her, it, or you formal), often used like “add (it) to …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ponle azúcar al café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put sugar in the coffee, please.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) affirmative command of “poner” + direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ponlo en la mesa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put it on the table, please.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) with the pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ponme un café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get me a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command; reflexive form of "poner" ("ponerse").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ponte la chaqueta, hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put on your jacket, it’s cold.

definitions.note: Informal "vos" command (common in Argentina/Uruguay).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Poné el libro en la mesa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the book on the table, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense of “poner” (used for ongoing actions in the past or habitual past actions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre ponía la mesa antes de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always used to set the table before dinner.

definitions.note: Used mainly to describe music, art, or culture connected to popular mass culture.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta la música pop.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like pop music.

definitions.note: Commonly used in some Spanish-speaking regions as an English loanword; more generally you’ll also hear “refresco” or “gaseosa.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quieres un pop o un jugo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a pop or a juice?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese cantante es muy popular en España.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That singer is very popular in Spain.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine), used with plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos restaurantes son muy populares en la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These restaurants are very popular in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La popularidad del cantante creció después de la gira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The singer's popularity grew after the tour.

definitions.note: Diminutive of “poco”; often used to sound more informal, softer, or more affectionate.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solo quiero un poquito de agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only want a little bit of water.

definitions.note: Commonly used with de + noun (e.g., “un poquito de agua”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solo necesito un poquito de agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only need a little bit of water.

definitions.note: Often used to express cause/reason or motivation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo hice por ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did it for you.

definitions.note: Used to indicate the agent in passive sentences or the means/method.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro fue escrito por Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was written by Ana.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Caminamos por el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked through the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La taza es de porcelana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cup is made of porcelain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos sentamos en el porche para tomar aire fresco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sat on the porch to get some fresh air.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos tres porciones de pizza para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need three portions of pizza for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero una porción de pizza, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a slice (a serving) of pizza, please.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial; short for “pornografía.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero ver porno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to watch porn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero ver pornografía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to watch pornography.

definitions.note: Used to give a reason. Don’t confuse with “por qué” (two words) meaning “why?” in questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No fui a la fiesta porque estaba cansado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t go to the party because I was tired.

definitions.note: Often used to complain about something dirty or messy; can also be a mild insult for something considered low-quality.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Qué porquería hay en el suelo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a mess there is on the floor!

definitions.note: Informal; used to say something is very bad or worthless.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta comida es una porquería.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This food is crap.

definitions.note: Colloquial and often rude; used for something dirty, gross, or of very poor quality.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡No quiero porquerías en mi cuarto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want disgusting things in my room!

definitions.note: Usually used as a noun, often with an article: "el porqué" = "the reason (why)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entiendo el porqué de su decisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't understand the reason for his decision.

definitions.note: It’s a noun meaning “the reason”; it’s usually used with an article (el/los) and can be plural (porqués).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entiendo el porqué de su decisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand the reason for his decision.

definitions.note: Slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la fiesta, alguien estaba fumando un porro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the party, someone was smoking a joint.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts to mean “to wear” (clothing, accessories) or “to carry” (something you have with you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella porta una chaqueta negra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a black jacket.

definitions.note: Often refers to the front cover of a book, magazine, or newspaper.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La portada de la revista es muy bonita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cover of the magazine is very pretty.

definitions.note: Past participle, most commonly used with the reflexive verb "portarse" (to behave), often with "haber" (e.g., "se ha portado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Juan se ha portado muy bien hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Juan has behaved very well today.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., “portador de documentos” = “bearer of documents”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El portador de la tarjeta debe firmar aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cardholder must sign here.

definitions.note: Often sounds formal; in everyday speech, Spanish commonly uses "llevando" for "carrying/wearing."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está portando una caja muy pesada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is carrying a very heavy box.

definitions.note: Often refers to someone’s way of carrying themselves (posture or presence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su porte elegante llamó la atención.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His elegant bearing drew attention.

definitions.note: Used especially in expressions like “gastos de porte”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El precio no incluye el porte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price doesn’t include the shipping cost.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El portero abrió la puerta y nos saludó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doorman opened the door and greeted us.

definitions.note: Used in soccer and other sports.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El portero detuvo el penalti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The goalkeeper saved the penalty.

definitions.note: feminine form (used with feminine nouns or for a woman/girl).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesora es portuguesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Portuguese.

definitions.note: Usually refers to something from Portugal; it can also refer to the Portuguese language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La comida portuguesa es deliciosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Portuguese food is delicious.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective too (e.g., "comida portuguesa"), but here it’s the noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vecino es portugués y habla portugués.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Portuguese and speaks Portuguese.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to a laptop computer ("ordenador portátil" / "computadora portátil").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un cargador portátil para mi teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a portable charger for my phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi portátil está en la mochila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My laptop is in the backpack.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) of "portar" (él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella portó un vestido rojo en la ceremonia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wore a red dress at the ceremony.

definitions.note: Often refers to a large, heavy gate (for a yard, building entrance, or garage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El portón está cerrado con llave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gate is locked.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about someone’s future prospects or what lies ahead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El porvenir de la empresa depende de las ventas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company’s future depends on sales.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of "poseer" (he/she/it owns; you formal own).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella posee una casa cerca de la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She owns a house near the beach.

definitions.note: Used for possession/ownership; often sounds more formal than “tenemos.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nosotros poseemos una casa cerca del mar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We own a house near the sea.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “poseer.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos poseen una casa cerca del mar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They own a house near the sea.

definitions.note: Often sounds more formal than "tener" (to have).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella posee una casa cerca del mar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She owns a house near the sea.

definitions.note: Used with "tú" (informal singular "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué posees además de tu coche?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you own besides your car?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Poseo una pequeña casa en el campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I own a small house in the countryside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa está en mi posesión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is in my possession.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted): “I/he/she/you (formal) used to own / was owning.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era joven, poseía un coche viejo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was young, I owned an old car.

definitions.note: Often used to mean possessed by a spirit/demon, or acting as if under someone’s control.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dicen que el hombre está poseído.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They say the man is possessed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Existe la posibilidad de que llueva mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a possibility that it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Plural of "posibilidad".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchas posibilidades para resolver este problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many possibilities to solve this problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Es posible terminar hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is it possible to finish today?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Posiblemente lleguemos tarde por el tráfico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We might arrive late because of traffic.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay varias soluciones posibles para este problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several possible solutions for this problem.

definitions.note: Plural of "posición".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El equipo cambió de posiciones durante el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team changed positions during the match.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cambia de posición para ver mejor la pantalla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Change position to see the screen better.

definitions.note: Often used for a viewpoint in a discussion or debate (e.g., political or personal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No estoy de acuerdo con tu posición sobre ese tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't agree with your stance on that topic.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su respuesta fue positiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her answer was positive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante mantener una actitud positiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to keep a positive attitude.

definitions.note: Often used for medical tests (for example, COVID or pregnancy tests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La prueba salió positiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The test came back positive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pospondré la reunión hasta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will postpone the meeting until tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decidimos posponer la reunión hasta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We decided to postpone the meeting until tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El partido quedó pospuesto por la lluvia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The game was postponed because of the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pospusimos la reunión hasta el lunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We postponed the meeting until Monday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pospuso la reunión hasta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He postponed the meeting until tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for a guard post or a designated position (especially in some Latin American contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El soldado está en la posta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldier is at the post.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un código postal para completar el formulario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a postal code to complete the form.

definitions.note: Commonly used as shorthand for “trabajador(a) postal” or “empleado(a) de correos.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El postal llegó con las cartas esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The postal worker arrived with the letters this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré postales para mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought postcards for my friends.

definitions.note: Often refers to a utility pole (for electricity, lights, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El poste de luz está roto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light pole is broken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De postre, voy a pedir helado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dessert, I'm going to order ice cream.

definitions.note: Commonly used for applying for a job, scholarship, or program; also used for running for a position in some countries.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a postular a una beca este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to apply for a scholarship this year.

definitions.note: Often used for applying for a job, scholarship, or position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María postuló a una beca el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María applied for a scholarship last year.

definitions.note: Used when someone is proposed as a candidate (e.g., for an award or election).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El partido lo postuló como candidato a alcalde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The party nominated him as a candidate for mayor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mantén una buena postura cuando te sientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep a good posture when you sit down.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "posar"; often used for someone sitting for a photo or painting, or placing their body in a certain position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella posó para la foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She posed for the photo.

definitions.note: Used mostly for water (e.g., “agua potable”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta agua es potable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This water is drinkable.

definitions.note: Often used for power in the sense of strength/capacity, or electrical power; in math it can also mean an exponent/power (e.g., 2 a la tercera potencia).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este coche tiene mucha potencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This car has a lot of power.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este proyecto tiene mucho potencial.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This project has a lot of potential.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este motor es muy potente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This engine is very powerful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay un pozo en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a well in the courtyard.

definitions.note: Can also be the informal (tú) command “practice.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella practica yoga todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She practices yoga every day.

definitions.note: gerund (used like “-ing” in English)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy practicando español todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am practicing Spanish every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito practicar mi español todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to practice my Spanish every day.

definitions.note: Often used with sports and activities (e.g., practicar fútbol, practicar yoga).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano practica fútbol los fines de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother plays soccer on weekends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos sentamos en el prado para hacer un picnic.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sat in the meadow to have a picnic.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Toma precauciones cuando conduzcas de noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take precautions when you drive at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por precaución, llevé un paraguas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a precaution, I brought an umbrella.

definitions.note: Used to describe someone who takes precautions to avoid problems.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soy muy precavido cuando manejo de noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very cautious when I drive at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No hay precedente para una situación así.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is no precedent for a situation like this.

definitions.note: Often used in formal writing as a polite way to address someone (e.g., in letters or emails).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estimada señora, su opinión es muy preciada para nosotros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear Madam, your opinion is very valued to us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El precio de este libro es muy alto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price of this book is very high.

definitions.note: Plural of "precio".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los precios en este supermercado son bajos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prices in this supermarket are low.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu hija es preciosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your daughter is beautiful.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las flores del jardín son preciosas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flowers in the garden are beautiful.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is very beautiful or charming; can also be used affectionately about a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Qué vestido tan precioso!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a beautiful dress!

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los collares son preciosos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The necklaces are beautiful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tuvieron cuidado al caminar cerca del precipicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were careful when walking near the cliff.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue un comentario precipitado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a hasty comment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se precipitó hacia la puerta cuando oyó el timbre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rushed to the door when he heard the doorbell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia precipitó una discusión en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news triggered an argument at the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eso es precisamente lo que quería decir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is precisely what I wanted to say.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize coincidence in time or place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegaste precisamente cuando íbamos a salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You arrived just as we were about to leave.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos instrucciones precisas para no equivocarnos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need precise instructions so we don’t make mistakes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más precisión en las medidas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more precision in the measurements.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos una cifra precisa para el informe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need an exact figure for the report.

definitions.note: Often used with the verb “ser”: “es preciso” = “it’s necessary.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es preciso estudiar para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s necessary to study for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los científicos intentan predecir el clima para la próxima semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Scientists try to predict the weather for next week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis predicciones para este año son optimistas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My predictions for this year are optimistic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi predicción es que mañana va a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My prediction is that it’s going to rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “predecir” (to predict).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El meteorólogo predijo lluvia para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meteorologist predicted rain for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para mí, es preferible salir temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For me, it's preferable to leave early.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta es mi opción preferida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my preferred option.

definitions.note: Used to describe someone or something you like the most or that you choose over others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El helado de chocolate es mi sabor preferido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Chocolate ice cream is my favorite flavor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferimos quedarnos en casa esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We prefer to stay at home tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preferiría quedarme en casa esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would prefer to stay home tonight.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past habitual/ongoing): “used to prefer / was preferring,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, prefería el chocolate a la vainilla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a kid, I preferred chocolate over vanilla.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal you (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella prefiere el té.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prefers tea.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense (they/you all prefer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos prefieren el té al café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They prefer tea to coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prefiero el té al café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer tea over coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una pregunta para ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a question for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella me pregunta la hora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She asks me the time.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), used for ongoing/repeated actions or background descriptions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, siempre preguntaba por qué el cielo es azul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a kid, I always used to ask why the sky is blue.

definitions.note: Past participle of "preguntar"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect (e.g., "he preguntado"). Not related to English "pregnant".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya he preguntado al profesor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already asked the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preguntamos al profesor si hay tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ask the teacher if there is homework.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "preguntar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos preguntan si hay una mesa libre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They ask if there is a free table.

definitions.note: This is the gerund form (used like “asking” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy preguntando por la dirección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m asking for the address.

definitions.note: Usually followed by “por” for what you’re asking about (e.g., “preguntar por algo”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero preguntarte algo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to ask you something.

definitions.native: to ask him, to ask her
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (“to him/to her/to you” formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a preguntarle a Ana si viene mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to ask Ana if she's coming tomorrow.

definitions.note: The ending “-les” means “to them” (indirect object pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero preguntarles si tienen tiempo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to ask them if they have time tomorrow.

definitions.note: Object pronoun attached to the infinitive (preguntar + me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes preguntarme cuando quieras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can ask me whenever you want.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), they/you (plural, formal) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preguntaron la hora en la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They asked the time at the station.

definitions.note: Literally “to ask you” (infinitive + indirect object pronoun “te”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero preguntarte algo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to ask you something.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana preguntaré al profesor sobre la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will ask the teacher about the homework.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo le preguntaría al profesor, pero tengo vergüenza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would ask the teacher, but I'm embarrassed.

definitions.note: Plural of “pregunta”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo dos preguntas para el profesor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two questions for the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué preguntas eso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you ask that?

definitions.note: Informal (tú) preterite form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué preguntaste eso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you ask that?

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (“Ask...”), and also as the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope,” “it’s important that,” etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, pregunte si tiene dudas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please ask if you have questions.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "preguntar"; also can be negative informal command (tú): "no preguntes".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me preguntes si necesitas ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you ask me if you need help.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of "preguntar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre pregunto cuando no entiendo algo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always ask when I don’t understand something.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le pregunté al profesor una duda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked the teacher a question.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular (he/she/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella preguntó dónde estaba el baño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She asked where the bathroom was.

definitions.native: ask him, ask her, ask you (formal)
definitions.note: Command (tú) + indirect object pronoun "le".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pregúntale a tu profesor si hay tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ask your teacher if there is homework.

definitions.note: Command (tú) form. "-les" is an indirect object pronoun meaning "to them".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pregúntales si quieren venir mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ask them if they want to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tienes dudas, pregúntame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have questions, ask me.

definitions.note: Affirmative tú command with attached pronouns: se (= to him/her/you formal) + lo (= it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no lo sabes, pregúntaselo al profesor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don't know, ask the teacher.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with an indirect object pronoun attached (le = to him/her/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pregúntele al profesor si hay tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ask the teacher if there is homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante reconocer y combatir el prejuicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to recognize and fight prejudice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus prejuicios le impiden conocer a gente nueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His prejudices keep him from getting to know new people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ganó el primer premio en el concurso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She won first prize in the contest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los premios se entregan al final del evento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prizes are given out at the end of the event.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprar una prenda nueva para la entrevista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy a new item of clothing for the interview.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse las prendas en el armario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the clothes in the closet.

definitions.note: Also commonly means “catches” (e.g., fire) or “takes/grabs,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella prende la luz cuando entra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She turns on the light when she comes in.

definitions.note: Commonly used for turning on lights or lighting a fire/cigarette; in many regions, "encender" is more common for this meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes prender la luz, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you turn on the light, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano prendió la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother turned on the light.

definitions.note: Often refers to news media/journalists as a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La prensa llegó temprano para cubrir el evento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The press arrived early to cover the event.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les): e.g., “Me preocupa…” = “It worries me / I’m worried about …”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me preocupa el examen de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm worried about tomorrow's exam.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; it can describe an ongoing past situation (“was worrying”) or a repeated past action (“used to worry”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me preocupaba mucho el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was very worried about the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchas preocupaciones en este momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many worries right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una preocupación por mi examen de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a worry about my exam tomorrow.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy preocupada por mi examen de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm worried about my exam tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy preocupado por el examen de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m worried about tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos preocupados por el examen de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are worried about tomorrow’s exam.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "preocupar" (they worry/concern). Often used with an indirect object (me/te/le/nos/les).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me preocupan tus notas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your grades worry me.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an indirect object pronoun: “me” = “to me.” Often used in phrases like “me preocupa…” or “no te preocupes.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me preocupa el examen de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow's exam worries me.

definitions.native: to worry us, to concern us
definitions.note: Reflexive form ("preocuparnos") is often used to mean "for us to worry" or "to worry about."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No debemos preocuparnos por eso ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We shouldn't worry about that now.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; often used with "por" (to worry about).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te preocupes, todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't worry, everything is going to turn out fine.

definitions.note: Often used with “por” to say what you’re worried about.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te preocupes por mí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry about me.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached object pronoun “te” (“you”). Often used with “por” (to worry about).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tienes que preocuparte por mí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t have to worry about me.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué te preocupas tanto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you worry so much?

definitions.note: Usually used with the subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “Es normal que…”), or as a formal command: “No se preocupe.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es normal que te preocupe el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s normal that the exam worries you.

definitions.note: Used with ustedes (present subjunctive) or as an affirmative command (imperative) for ustedes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No se preocupen por mí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry about me.

definitions.note: Often used with “no” as “No te preocupes” = “Don’t worry.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te preocupes, todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, everything is going to turn out fine.

definitions.note: Often used with "me": "me preocupo" = "I worry" / "I get worried."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me preocupo por mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worry about my family.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite) form meaning “(he/she/it) worried” or “(you, formal) worried.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia lo preocupó mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news worried him a lot.

definitions.note: Common in Mexico and some other countries as a shortened form of "preparatoria".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana va a la prepa cerca de su casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister goes to the high school near her house.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present (he/she/it) or informal command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella prepara la cena todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prepares dinner every day.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo preparaba la cena cuando llegaste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was preparing dinner when you arrived.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La preparación para el examen me tomó dos semanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The preparation for the exam took me two weeks.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy preparada para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m prepared for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy preparado para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am ready for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya estoy preparado para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m already prepared for the exam.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Están preparados para el examen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you prepared for the exam?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre preparamos la cena juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We always prepare dinner together.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ando form), used for actions in progress (often with "estar").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy preparando la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m preparing dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a preparar la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to prepare dinner.

definitions.native: to prepare myself, get myself ready
definitions.note: Reflexive form with an attached object pronoun: me (“myself”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito prepararme para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to prepare myself for the exam.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with "nos" (“ourselves”); often used to talk about getting ready for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que prepararnos para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to prepare ourselves for the exam.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; it means the subject prepares themselves (often: to get ready).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que prepararme para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get ready for the exam.

definitions.native: to prepare you, to get you ready
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun "te" (you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que prepararte para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to prepare you for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana prepararé la cena para mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will prepare dinner for my family.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural to talk about things done to get ready for an event or activity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya están listos los preparativos para la boda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The preparations for the wedding are already ready.

definitions.note: In Mexico and some other countries, this refers to the last stage of secondary education, often similar to grades 10–12.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana va a la preparatoria cerca de nuestra casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister goes to the high school near our house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preparo la cena todas las noches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prepare dinner every night.

definitions.note: Reflexive gerund: describes someone is in the process of getting themselves ready.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se está preparando para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is getting ready for the exam.

definitions.note: First-person singular, simple past (pretérito) of "preparar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Preparé la cena para mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prepared dinner for my family.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/you (formal) prepared.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella preparó la cena para su familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prepared dinner for her family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la frase "Voy a casa", "a" es una preposición.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the sentence "I go home," "a" is a preposition.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú); reflexive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prepárate, ya nos vamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get ready, we’re leaving now.

definitions.note: Command form used to address a group (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Prepárense, el examen empieza en cinco minutos!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get ready, the exam starts in five minutes!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La presa está llena después de las lluvias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dam is full after the rains.

definitions.note: Common in Spain; in much of Latin America, "enchufe" or "tomacorriente" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No hay ninguna presa cerca de la cama para cargar el móvil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There isn’t any socket near the bed to charge the phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las presas ayudan a controlar el nivel del agua del río.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dams help control the water level of the river.

definitions.note: Animals hunted by another animal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los leones buscan presas por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lions look for prey at night.

definitions.native: to do without, to dispense with
definitions.note: Often used with “de”: “prescindir de algo” = “to do without something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Podemos prescindir del coche y ir en metro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can do without the car and go by subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su presencia me tranquiliza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her presence calms me down.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella presenció el accidente desde la acera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She witnessed the accident from the sidewalk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor presenta a la nueva estudiante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher introduces the new student.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana tengo una presentación en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I have a presentation in class.

definitions.note: Often used for introducing people or presenting something formally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por la presentación; es un placer conocerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for the introduction; it’s a pleasure to meet you.

definitions.note: Past participle of "presentar"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses (e.g., "ha presentado" = "has presented").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El director ha presentado el nuevo plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director has presented the new plan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy presentamos el proyecto al equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we present the project to the team.

definitions.note: Often used for introducing people or presenting something (like an idea, plan, or document).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a presentar a mi amiga a mis padres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to introduce my friend to my parents.

definitions.native: to introduce (to him/her), to present (to him/her)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” = “to him,” “to her,” or formal “to you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero presentarle a mi amiga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to introduce my friend to him/her (to you, formal).

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object pronoun: -les = “to them” (or “to you” formal plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero presentarles a mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to introduce my friends to them.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun “me” (“myself”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hola, soy Ana. Quiero presentarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hi, I'm Ana. I want to introduce myself.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “they” or “you (plural, Spain)” did this action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los profesores presentaron al nuevo director.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teachers introduced the new principal.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used when you say who you are (e.g., in a meeting or at school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hola, me llamo Ana. Me presento: soy la nueva estudiante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hi, my name is Ana. Let me introduce myself: I’m the new student.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” to introduce you to someone: “presentarte a …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero presentarte a mi amiga Laura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to introduce you to my friend Laura.

definitions.native: I will introduce, I will present
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana te presentaré a mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will introduce you to my sister.

definitions.note: Verb form of “presentar” (as in introducing someone or presenting something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que te presente a mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want him/her to introduce you to my friends.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" (e.g., "estar presente") to mean being present/attending.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos los estudiantes están presentes hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the students are present today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por el presente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for the gift.

definitions.note: Refers to the current time, not a gift.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en el presente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in the present.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos estamos presentes en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are all present at the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Traje presentes para todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brought gifts for everyone.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts, like meetings or ceremonies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los presentes aplaudieron al final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The people present applauded at the end.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tuve un presentimiento de que algo iba a salir mal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a premonition that something was going to go wrong.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) present tense of "presentar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me presento: soy Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I introduce myself: I'm Ana.
