definitions.note: Often used as a past participle/adjective, frequently with "estar" (e.g., "está resuelto").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El problema ya está resuelto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problem is already solved.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El problema ya está resuelto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problem is already resolved.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted); also the formal command (usted) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que resuelva el problema hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you solve the problem today.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "resolver" (for él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella resuelve el problema en diez minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She solves the problem in ten minutes.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce surprising or newly discovered information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Resulta que el museo está cerrado hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It turns out that the museum is closed today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El resultado del examen fue muy bueno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The result of the exam was very good.

definitions.note: Past participle of "resultar"; often used with "haber" (e.g., "ha resultado") or as an adjective (e.g., "resultado exitoso").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El experimento ha resultado exitoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The experiment has turned out to be successful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los resultados del examen salen mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exam results come out tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used to express how something ends up being (e.g., 'resulta difícil' = 'it turns out to be difficult').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El plan resultó mejor de lo que esperábamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan turned out better than we expected.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las pruebas resultaron negativas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tests turned out negative.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si sigues practicando, resultará más fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you keep practicing, it will turn out to be easier.

definitions.note: Conditional form (often used for hypotheses, conclusions, or reported information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no estudiaras, el examen resultaría muy difícil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you didn’t study, the exam would turn out to be very difficult.

definitions.note: Simple past (él/ella/usted). Often used to say how something ended up being.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al final, la solución resultó más simple de lo que pensábamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, the solution turned out to be simpler than we thought.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un resumen del capítulo para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a summary of the chapter for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La resurrección de Jesús es una creencia central en el cristianismo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The resurrection of Jesus is a central belief in Christianity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retamos a nuestros amigos a una carrera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We challenge our friends to a race.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él retira el dinero del cajero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He withdraws the money from the ATM.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La retirada de las tropas fue rápida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The withdrawal of the troops was quick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo está retirado desde hace cinco años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather has been retired for five years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en un pueblo retirado de la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in a town secluded from the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He retirado dinero del banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have withdrawn money from the bank.

definitions.note: Often used to say someone has stopped working (retired).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo está retirado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is retired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, retire los zapatos antes de entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please remove your shoes before coming in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a retirar dinero del cajero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to withdraw money from the ATM.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: "retirarse" = to leave/withdraw.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la reunión, decidió retirar su candidatura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the meeting, he decided to withdraw his candidacy.

definitions.native: they removed, they withdrew, they took away
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retiraron el coche de la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They removed the car from the street.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving a place or withdrawing from an activity; also commonly used for retiring from work (e.g., "retirarse" = "to retire").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me voy a retirar temprano porque estoy cansado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to leave early because I’m tired.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted) or in the present subjunctive of "retirar". Not related to English "retire" (= stop working).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, retire la tarjeta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please remove the card.

definitions.note: Often used for withdrawing money (e.g., from an ATM).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retiro dinero del cajero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I withdraw money from the ATM.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi padre está en retiro desde el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father has been in retirement since last year.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “he/she/it removed” or “you (formal) removed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico retiró la venda con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor removed the bandage carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprender un nuevo idioma es un reto, pero vale la pena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Learning a new language is a challenge, but it’s worth it.

definitions.note: Often used for things (like a train, a delivery, or a plan). Avoid using it for people; it can be offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren va retrasado diez minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is delayed by ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo un retraso de veinte minutos en el tren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a twenty-minute delay on the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tráfico retrasó el autobús.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Traffic delayed the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El retrato de mi abuela está en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother's portrait is in the living room.

definitions.note: Common in Spain; in much of Latin America, “inodoro” is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Dónde está el retrete?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where is the toilet?

definitions.note: Often used as a command to a group (or to you formal plural): “(you all) back up / move back.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, retrocedan un paso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, back up one step.

definitions.native: to move back, to back up, to go back
definitions.note: Often used for physical movement (people/vehicles) or for retreating in a more general sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche tuvo que retroceder porque la calle estaba cerrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car had to back up because the street was closed.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular (he/she/it) of “retar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella lo retó a una carrera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She challenged him to a race.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El grupo está reunido en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The group is gathered in the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hemos reunido toda la información.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have gathered all the information.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "reunir"; often used with "estar" to form the present continuous.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos reuniendo a todos en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are gathering everyone in the room.

definitions.note: Third person plural, simple past (pretérito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se reunieron en el parque para hablar del proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gathered in the park to talk about the project.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros/as) of "reunir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos reunimos en el parque para hablar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We meet up in the park to talk.

definitions.note: Plural of "reunión".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo tres reuniones hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have three meetings today.

definitions.note: Often used for gathering people or collecting things into one place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a reunir a todos en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to gather everyone in the room.

definitions.native: we will gather, we will bring together
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana reuniremos a todos los estudiantes en el aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will gather all the students in the classroom.

definitions.note: Reflexive form meaning the action involves the speaker; commonly used for arranging a meeting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes reunirte conmigo mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you meet up with me tomorrow?

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “nos” (“us”), meaning the action is done with/for “us” (e.g., “to meet up”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a reunirnos mañana por la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to meet up tomorrow afternoon.

definitions.native: to meet up, to get together
definitions.note: Reflexive verb used when people meet (often meaning they meet each other).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos vamos a reunir mañana para estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to meet up tomorrow to study.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El guía reunirá al grupo en la entrada del museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide will gather the group at the entrance of the museum.

definitions.note: Often used with things like information, documents, money, or evidence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella reunirá la información necesaria para el informe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will collect the necessary information for the report.

definitions.note: Often used for bringing people together in one place (like gathering a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El director reunió al equipo para hablar del proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The manager brought the team together to talk about the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una reunión a las tres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a meeting at three.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El informe revela datos importantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report reveals important data.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La revelación de la verdad sorprendió a todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The revelation of the truth surprised everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El secreto fue revelado ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The secret was revealed yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo revelar el secreto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't reveal the secret.

definitions.note: Used for processing photographic film or photos.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a revelar las fotos esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to develop the photos this afternoon.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “he/she/you (formal) revealed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El periodista reveló la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist revealed the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El globo reventó de repente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon burst suddenly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hizo una reverencia al final del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a bow at the end of the concert.

definitions.note: Often used for showing respect in a formal or religious context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mostró reverencia en la iglesia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed reverence in the church.

definitions.note: Title used for a male member of the clergy; often used as a form of address.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El reverendo habló con la familia después de la misa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Reverend spoke with the family after Mass.

definitions.note: Often used for checking something to make sure it’s correct or OK.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella revisa el correo todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She checks her email every morning.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “revisar”; often used with “estar” to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy revisando el informe ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m reviewing the report now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a revisar mi correo antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to check my email before leaving.

definitions.native: I will check, I will review
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo), simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revisaré el correo esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will check the email this afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo revise el informe antes de enviarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I reviewed the report before sending it.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive or affirmative command (ustedes) of "revisar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revisen la tarea antes de entregarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Check the homework before turning it in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hicimos una revisión del documento antes de enviarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We did a review of the document before sending it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compro una revista en el quiosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy a magazine at the newsstand.

definitions.note: Plural of “revista”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compro revistas en el aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy magazines at the airport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revisé el informe antes de enviarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked the report before sending it.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “(he/she/you formal) checked/reviewed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La profesora revisó mi tarea ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher checked my homework yesterday.

definitions.native: to revive, to bring back to life
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los médicos lograron revivir al paciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctors managed to revive the patient.

definitions.note: Often used with memories or experiences (e.g., “revivir un momento”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A veces revivo ese día en mi mente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes I relive that day in my mind.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El paciente revivió después de unos minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patient came back to life after a few minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su idea fue revolucionaria para la época.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her idea was revolutionary for the time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los revolucionarios tomaron la plaza principal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The revolutionaries took the main square.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La revolución cambió la historia del país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The revolution changed the country's history.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revolvió el café con una cuchara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stirred the coffee with a spoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El viento revolvió las hojas en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind messed up the leaves in the yard.

definitions.native: the opposite side, the wrong way around
definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “al revés” = “the other way around / in reverse.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo pusiste al revés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You put it in the wrong way around.

definitions.note: Often used as “un revés” meaning an unexpected bad event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perder el trabajo fue un revés para ella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Losing her job was a setback for her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía encontró un revólver en el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found a revolver in the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El rey vive en el palacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king lives in the palace.

definitions.note: Plural of "rey".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los Reyes Magos traen regalos a los niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Three Wise Men bring gifts to the children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella reza todas las noches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prays every night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rezamos antes de comer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We pray before eating.

definitions.note: Gerund of "rezar"; often used with "estar" to mean "to be praying."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy rezando por mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am praying for my family.

definitions.note: Often used for religious prayer; can also mean to say a prayer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas las noches rezo antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every night I pray before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo) form of "rezar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cada noche rezo antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every night I pray before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "rezar" for él/ella/usted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anoche rezó antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she prayed before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of "reír".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer reí mucho con esa película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I laughed a lot at that movie.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella reía con sus amigas en el café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was laughing with her friends at the café.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (third person plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando contabas esa historia, todos reían.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you told that story, everyone laughed.

definitions.note: Past participle of "reír" (to laugh).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nunca he reído tanto en mi vida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve never laughed so much in my life.

definitions.note: Present tense of "reír" (also used as the preterite: "we laughed").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre reímos con sus chistes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We always laugh at his jokes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me hace reír ese chiste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That joke makes me laugh.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an indirect object pronoun: “me” = “(to) me” (as in “it makes me laugh”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa película siempre logra reírme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That movie always manages to make me laugh.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used with “de” (reírse de alguien/algo) to mean “to laugh at someone/something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me reí mucho con esa película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I laughed a lot at that movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella reúne a todos en la sala para empezar la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gathers everyone in the room to start the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi jefe se reúne con los clientes los lunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss meets with the clients on Mondays.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “reunir” (used for “they” or “you all” in Latin America).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se reúnen en el parque todos los domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They meet in the park every Sunday.

definitions.note: Likely a misspelling or missing accent of “río” (river).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El río pasa por la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river goes through the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos sentamos en la ribera del río para comer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sat on the riverbank to eat.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “rico.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi tía es rica y vive en una casa grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My aunt is rich and lives in a big house.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "rico"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las familias ricas viven en esa zona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rich families live in that area.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "rico"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las galletas están muy ricas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cookies are very tasty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su familia es muy rica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her family is very rich.

definitions.note: Commonly used to talk about food and drinks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta sopa está muy rica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This soup is very delicious.

definitions.note: Often used with an article, especially in plural: “los ricos” = “the rich (people)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El rico no quiere pagar más impuestos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rich person doesn't want to pay more taxes.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or mixed group); can also be used after a verb like "ser"/"estar" to describe people or things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis abuelos son ricos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are rich.

definitions.note: Often used for food.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos tacos están ricos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These tacos are tasty.

definitions.note: Plural form; refers to people who are rich.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los ricos a veces pagan menos impuestos que la clase media.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rich people sometimes pay fewer taxes than the middle class.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa idea es ridícula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That idea is ridiculous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ridículo pagar tanto por una botella de agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s ridiculous to pay so much for a bottle of water.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the phrase “hacer el ridículo” (“to make a fool of yourself”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hiciste el ridículo delante de todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You made a fool of yourself in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “regar” (to water).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella riega las plantas todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She waters the plants every day.

definitions.note: Not a standard Spanish word in modern usage; it is commonly a misspelling of “tiempo”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo riempo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jinete agarró las riendas del caballo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rider grabbed the horse's reins.

definitions.note: Present participle (gerund) of "reír".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy riendo con tus chistes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am laughing at your jokes.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of “reír”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella siempre riene cuando ve esa película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She always laughs when she watches that movie.

definitions.note: Used with "tú" (informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué ríenes tanto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you laughing so much?

definitions.note: This is not a standard form of "tener" in modern Spanish; the usual form for "you have" is "tienes".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si rienes tiempo, ven conmigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have time, come with me.

definitions.note: Third-person plural preterite (they/you all laughed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos rieron mucho en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They laughed a lot at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay un riesgo de lluvia esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a risk of rain this afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos riesgos en este trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many risks in this job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El policía lleva un rifle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer carries a rifle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Secuestraron al empresario cuando salía del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They kidnapped the businessman when he was leaving work.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating the kidnapping of a businessman.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase "escuela secundaria" (secondary school). In many Spanish-speaking countries, it generally refers to the level after primary school.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This information is secondary.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “not the main one” or “less important.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This problem is secondary; the main thing is your health.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These topics are secondary in this project.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "secar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sol secó la ropa en el balcón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun dried the clothes on the balcony.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo sed.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m thirsty.

definitions.note: This is an old, literary form of «ser», found mostly in fixed expressions like «sea como fuere» or «sed de buena conducta» and in older texts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sed prudentes y respetad las normas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be prudent and follow the rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este vestido es de seda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress is made of silk.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a medicine/drug that calms you or makes you sleepy.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor prescribed me a sedative so I could sleep.

definitions.note: Often used for the main office or official location of an institution or company.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sede de la empresa está en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company's headquarters are in Madrid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de correr, estoy sediento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After running, I'm thirsty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este segmento del programa es mi favorito.

definitions.note: Plural informal command (vosotros).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow the instructions, please.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “en seguida.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you right away.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “seguidas” to mean “in a row / consecutively,” especially with time expressions (e.g., “dos horas seguidas”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was studying for three hours in a row.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase "a menudo" or "muy seguido" (especially in Latin America) to mean "often."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy al gimnasio muy seguido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to the gym very often.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ladrón fue seguido por la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief was followed by the police.

definitions.note: Often used for followers on social media.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many followers on Instagram.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jugamos tres partidos seguidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We played three games in a row.

definitions.note: Often used with a gerund (e.g., “seguimos + -ando/-iendo”) to mean “keep/continue doing something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguimos estudiando para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We keep studying for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguimos estudiando después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We keep studying after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguimos al guía por el museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We follow the guide through the museum.

definitions.note: Often used as an auxiliary in the structure “seguir + gerundio” to mean continuing an action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sigo estudiando español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I keep studying Spanish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro sigue a su dueña por todas partes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog follows its owner everywhere.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a seguir estudiando mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to continue studying tomorrow.

definitions.native: we will continue, we will follow
definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros/as) future tense of "seguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguiremos trabajando hasta terminar el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will keep working until we finish the project.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “las” = “them” (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo verlas bien, pero voy a seguirlas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't see them well, but I'm going to follow them.

definitions.native: to follow him/her/it, to keep up with him/her/it
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (to him/her/it; also formal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo seguirle el ritmo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't keep up with him.

definitions.native: to follow him, to follow it
definitions.note: "lo" is a direct object pronoun meaning “him” or “it.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a seguirlo hasta su casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to follow him to his house.

definitions.native: to continue it, to keep doing it
definitions.note: "lo" refers to something already mentioned (an activity, plan, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si funciona, vamos a seguirlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it works, we’re going to continue it.

definitions.note: "-los" means "them" (direct object, usually masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a seguirlos hasta la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to follow them to the station.

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun "me" is attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes seguirme, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you follow me, please?

definitions.note: Can also mean "to continue following me," depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te pierdes, intenta seguirme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you get lost, try to keep following me.

definitions.note: Auxiliary use of "seguir" + gerund to express that an action will keep happening.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguirá lloviendo toda la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will keep raining all afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana seguirá el mismo camino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will follow the same path.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (ellos/ellas/ustedes) future tense of "seguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguirán trabajando hasta terminar el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will keep working until they finish the project.

definitions.note: Often used as an auxiliary with a gerund (seguir + -ando/-iendo) to mean “to keep/continue doing something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguiré estudiando mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will keep studying tomorrow.

definitions.native: I will continue, I will keep going, I will follow
definitions.note: Simple future tense (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguiré estudiando español mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will continue studying Spanish tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "seguir"; often used for hypothetical situations or polite statements.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella vive en la segunda casa a la derecha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lives in the second house on the right.

definitions.note: Often used in time expressions (e.g., “un segundo” = “a second”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es la segunda vez que lo intento, pero esta es la primera vez que lo logro en menos de un segundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the second time I’m trying, but this is the first time I manage to do it in less than a second.

definitions.note: As an adverb, it’s used in time expressions meaning “a second” (a moment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuelvo en un segundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be back in a second.

definitions.note: Unit of time; also used for ordinal numbers (e.g., “el segundo” = “the second”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait a second, please.

definitions.note: plural masculine form of the ordinal number (used for ranking or order)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos llegaron segundos en la carrera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They finished second in the race.

definitions.note: Plural of "segundo" (a unit of time).

definitions.note: feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy seguro de que tienes razón.

definitions.note: Often used to express confidence or reassurance (similar to “sure”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguro que mañana llueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Surely it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to agree or confirm something (like “sure” or “okay”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: —Can you help me tomorrow? —Sure.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), first-person singular of "seguir".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was still studying when you arrived.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo seguía a mi hermana en el parque.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We explored the jungle for two days.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This week I have a lot of work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a estar de viaje por dos semanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to be traveling for two weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to sow tomato seeds in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo sembró maíz en el campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather planted corn in the field.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for a solution similar to the one we used last year.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This semester I have history and math classes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planted a seed in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city there are many traffic lights downtown.

definitions.note: Shortened form of “senador,” commonly used in political/news contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sen habló en el Congreso hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The senator spoke in Congress today.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The senate approved the new law.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The senators voted in favor of the new law.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "sencillo".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I simply don’t have time today.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las instrucciones son sencillas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The instructions are simple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta la sencillez de este diseño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the simplicity of this design.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a simple recipe.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exercises are simple.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked along a trail in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡La película estuvo sensacional!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was sensational!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tuve la sensación de que alguien me miraba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had the feeling that someone was watching me.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a sensible decision.

definitions.note: Often refers to being emotionally sensitive or easily affected.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very sensitive to criticism.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense of “sentar”; often describes a habitual or ongoing past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas las tardes, mi abuelo se sentaba en el patio a leer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está sentada en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is seated on the sofa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño está sentado en el suelo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a sentar al niño en la silla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to sit the child on the chair.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “sentar”, often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., after “si” = “if”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me sentara aquí, podría ver mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I sat here, I could see better.

definitions.note: Reflexive form: "me" = "myself" (I sit down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a sentarme aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to sit down here.

definitions.note: reflexive + us: “sit down” (ourselves).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a sentarnos aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's sit down here.

definitions.note: Third-person plural simple past (pretérito) of "sentar". Often used reflexively as "se sentaron" = "they sat down."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños se sentaron en el suelo para escuchar el cuento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children sat down on the floor to listen to the story.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb (used with reflexive pronouns like me/te/se).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a sentarme aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to sit down here.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “te” (“yourself/you,” informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mejor sentarte un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better to sit down for a moment.

definitions.note: Future tense (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me sentaré aquí un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will sit down here for a moment.

definitions.note: Informal command used with vos (common in Argentina/Uruguay); equivalent to "siéntate" (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentate acá, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit down here, please.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts to mean a judge’s ruling or verdict.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez dictó sentencia ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge issued the ruling yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ladrón fue sentenciado a cinco años de cárcel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief was sentenced to five years in prison.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something (like a loss or criticism) that affects people deeply.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue una pérdida muy sentida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a deeply felt loss.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "tener sentido" (to make sense) or "en el sentido de" (in the sense of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta frase no tiene sentido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sentence doesn't make sense.

definitions.note: Past participle of "sentir"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect (e.g., "he sentido").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He sentido mucho frío hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have felt very cold today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo los cinco sentidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the five senses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta palabra tiene dos sentidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This word has two meanings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo se pone sentimental cuando ve fotos antiguas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather gets sentimental when he sees old photos.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un sentimiento extraño sobre esto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a strange feeling about this.

definitions.note: Often used for emotions or attitudes (for example, "sentimientos" can mean "feelings").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus palabras reflejan un sentimiento de esperanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His words reflect a feeling of hope.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchos sentimientos encontrados sobre ese tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of mixed feelings about that topic.

definitions.native: we feel, we regret, we are sorry
definitions.note: From "sentir". Often used to express apologies or sympathy (e.g., "Lo sentimos" = "We’re sorry").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo sentimos mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re very sorry.

definitions.note: Often used for emotions or physical sensations; also used in expressions like “sentir + noun” for “to smell/hear” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel cold.

definitions.note: Used to apologize or express sympathy, often in “lo siento”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo siento, llegué tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm sorry, I arrived late.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” = “it” (for something masculine or an idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedo sentirlo en el aire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can feel it in the air.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an attached object pronoun (“me” = myself). Often used to talk about how you feel physically or emotionally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy voy a sentirme mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm going to feel better.

definitions.note: Reflexive form used to talk about how someone feels physically or emotionally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me siento cansado hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel tired today.

definitions.note: Used with a reflexive pronoun (te). Commonly appears after another verb (e.g., "quiero sentirte") or in commands (e.g., "déjame sentirte").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero sentirte cerca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to feel you close.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (él/ella/usted) future tense of “sentir”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella sentirá alivio cuando termine el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will feel relieved when the exam is over.

definitions.note: Future tense (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentirás alivio después de hablar con ella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will feel relief after talking with her.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “sentir”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentiría mucha tristeza si perdiera a mi perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would feel very sad if I lost my dog.

definitions.native: we sat down, we would sit down
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (nosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegábamos al parque, siempre sentábamos a la sombra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we arrived at the park, we would always sit down in the shade.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun “me” as in “me senté” = “I sat down.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me senté en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sat down on the sofa.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 1st person singular of "sentir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentí mucho frío anoche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt very cold last night.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing/repeated past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, sentía miedo en la oscuridad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I felt afraid in the dark.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all felt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando escuchaban esa canción, sentían nostalgia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they listened to that song, they felt nostalgia.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of “sentar” (he/she/it sat down; you formal sat down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se sentó en la silla y esperó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sat down in the chair and waited.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “saber” (used after expressions of doubt, desire, or uncertainty).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que él lo sepa mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he knows it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (nosotros) of "saber"; often used after expressions like "es importante que" or "quiero que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que sepamos la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that we know the truth.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “saber” used with “que…”, after expressions of doubt, desire, or necessity, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que ellos sepan la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they know the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él separa la ropa blanca de la de color.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He separates the white clothes from the colored ones.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La separación fue difícil para toda la familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The separation was difficult for the whole family.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La basura está separada por tipo de material.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trash is separated by type of material.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las sillas están separadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chairs are separated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están sentados separado de los adultos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are sitting separate from the adults.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los libros están separados por tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The books are separated by topic.

definitions.native: separated (as a couple), not together anymore
definitions.note: Often used to say a couple is separated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis padres están separados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents are separated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Separamos la basura para reciclarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We separate the trash to recycle it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a separar la ropa blanca de la ropa de color.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to separate the white clothes from the colored clothes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos decidieron separar después de muchos años juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They decided to break up after many years together.

definitions.native: separate from each other, split up
definitions.note: Infinitive with an attached indirect object pronoun: “to separate ourselves / to split up.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mejor separarnos un rato para calmarnos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better for us to separate for a while to calm down.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se separaron después de diez años juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They separated after ten years together.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito): he/she/it separated; you (formal) separated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Separó la ropa blanca de la de color.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She separated the white clothes from the colored ones.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "saber" (used after expressions of doubt, desire, or in certain clauses like "cuando...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que sepas la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you know the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi cumpleaños es en septiembre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in September.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tesoro estaba sepultado bajo la arena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The treasure was buried under the sand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sequía ha afectado a los cultivos este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drought has affected the crops this year.

definitions.note: used with a past participle to form the passive voice
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La puerta va a ser abierta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is going to be opened tomorrow.

definitions.note: As a noun, it refers to a living being or to a person’s essence/nature.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ser humano necesita dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Human beings need to sleep.

definitions.note: Used for identity, inherent characteristics, origin, occupation, and telling time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soy estudiante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am a student.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the future passive (e.g., "será + participle").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La reunión será cancelada mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting will be canceled tomorrow.

definitions.note: Future tense of "ser" (to be).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana seremos más cuidadosos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will be more careful.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a calm mood, attitude, or atmosphere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella respondió con una voz serena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She replied with a calm voice.

definitions.note: Plural form of “ser” meaning a living being or entity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos seres vivos en el océano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many living beings in the ocean.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo sería más feliz con menos estrés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would be happier with less stress.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “serio”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situación es seria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is serious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablemos seriamente sobre lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s talk seriously about what happened.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las conversaciones serias pueden ser difíciles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Serious conversations can be difficult.

definitions.note: Often used for a TV series or a series of things (events, numbers, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy viendo una serie nueva en Netflix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m watching a new series on Netflix.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos hablar con seriedad sobre el presupuesto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to talk seriously about the budget.

definitions.note: Plural of "serie".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis series favoritas están en Netflix.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My favorite series are on Netflix.

definitions.note: Often used for a sequence of related events, games, or items (e.g., una serie de partidos).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El equipo ganó la serie de tres partidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team won the series of three games.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un asunto serio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a serious matter.

definitions.note: Often used informally; more commonly you’ll hear “en serio” for “seriously.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te lo digo serio: no tengo tiempo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m telling you seriously: I don’t have time today.

definitions.note: Often used with an article (e.g., el serio, la seria) to mean “the serious one/person.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él es el serio del grupo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is the serious one in the group.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos son serios y responsables en el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are serious and responsible at work.

definitions.native: to be it, to be him
definitions.note: Infinitive with the direct object pronoun “lo” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero serlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to be it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sacerdote dio un sermón sobre la paciencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The priest gave a sermon about patience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos una serpiente en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a snake in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay serpientes en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are snakes in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por su servicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your service.

definitions.note: Often used for customer support in phrases like "servicio al cliente".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito llamar al servicio al cliente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to call customer service.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ofrecemos servicios de limpieza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We offer cleaning services.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cena está servida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dinner is served.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El café ya está servido en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffee is already served on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya he servido la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already served dinner.

definitions.note: Can refer to a computer/server machine or to a waiter/server in a restaurant, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El servidor está caído, así que no funciona la página web.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The server is down, so the website isn’t working.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Hay servilletas en la mesa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are there napkins on the table?

definitions.note: Commonly used for serving food/drinks or providing a service.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El camarero va a servir la cena a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter is going to serve dinner at eight.

definitions.native: to be useful, to work (for a purpose)
definitions.note: Often used with "para" to say something is useful for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esto me sirve para estudiar español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is useful for me to study Spanish.

definitions.native: to serve him, to serve her, to serve you (formal)
definitions.note: “-le” is an indirect object pronoun (to/for him, her, or you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero servirle un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to serve you a coffee.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (él/ella/usted) future tense of “servir”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este mapa te servirá para llegar al hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This map will be useful to you for getting to the hotel.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) in the simple future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te serviré un café en un minuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will serve you a coffee in a minute.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of “servir” (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer serví la cena a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I served dinner at eight.

definitions.note: Often used as an auxiliary to form the passive voice with a past participle (ser + participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El informe será revisado mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report will be reviewed tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future of “ser” (can also be used for “you will be” in formal address).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana será un buen día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow will be a good day.

definitions.note: Future tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes). Used as an auxiliary to form the passive voice or other constructions with a past participle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las puertas serán abiertas a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doors will be opened at eight.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense of “ser.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana serás más fuerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will be stronger.

definitions.note: Future tense of "ser" (to be), used for identity, origin, characteristics, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana seré más paciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will be more patient.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vosotros/vosotras), future tense; used mainly in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana seréis responsables del proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will be responsible for the project.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “ser” (to be).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tuviera más tiempo, sería más paciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had more time, I would be more patient.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sin el tráfico, serían puntuales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without the traffic, they would be on time.

definitions.note: Second person singular (tú), conditional; can also be used for polite address (usted) in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Serías tan amable de ayudarme?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you be so kind as to help me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo sesenta minutos para terminar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have sixty minutes to finish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sesión empieza a las nueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The session starts at nine.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the phrase “romperse los sesos” (to rack your brains).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me estoy rompiendo los sesos para recordar su nombre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm racking my brains trying to remember his name.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela tiene setenta años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother is seventy years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Publicó la novela con el seudónimo de “Luna Roja”.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She published the novel under the pseudonym “Red Moon”.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La maestra es severa, pero justa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher is strict, but fair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez lo castigó severamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge punished him severely.

definitions.note: Often used for people, rules, or punishments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor es severo, pero justo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher is strict but fair.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los profesores son severos con las reglas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teachers are strict about the rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el formulario, tienes que indicar tu sexo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the form, you have to indicate your sex.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella vive en la sexta planta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lives on the sixth floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy es mi sexto día en este trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is my sixth day at this job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La educación sexual es importante en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sex education is important in school.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más educación y derechos sexuales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more sexual education and rights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La enfermedad se transmite sexualmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The disease is transmitted sexually.

definitions.note: Common loanword in Spanish; often invariable, but sometimes pluralized as “sexys” in informal use.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese vestido es muy sexy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That dress is very sexy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa señal indica que no puedes estacionar aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That sign indicates that you can’t park here.

definitions.note: Often used for pointing with a finger or indicating something to others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella señaló el mapa para mostrar dónde está el hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She pointed at the map to show where the hotel is.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El informe señala un aumento en las ventas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report indicates an increase in sales.

definitions.note: Plural of “señal”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay señales de tráfico en esta calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are traffic signs on this street.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “he/she/you (formal) pointed out/indicated.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor señaló el error en mi tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher pointed out the mistake in my homework.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “dar señas” (to give directions/clues) or “hacer señas” (to gesture).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me hizo señas para que me acercara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She signaled to me to come closer.

definitions.note: Polite title or form of address for an adult man; can be used before a last name or on its own.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sí, señor, tiene razón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yes, sir, you’re right.

definitions.note: Often capitalized (Señor) when referring to God in religious contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Creo en el Señor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believe in the Lord.

definitions.note: Used as a polite form of address for a woman, often married.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buenos días, señora García.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good morning, Mrs. García.

definitions.note: Plural of "señora"; often used as a polite form of address for adult women.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Señoras, por favor, tomen asiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ladies, please take a seat.

definitions.note: Plural of “señor”; used as a polite form of address for men or a group (mixed or all male) in formal contexts.
