definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo sudor en la frente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have sweat on my forehead.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesora es sueca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Swedish.

definitions.note: male person from Sweden; the feminine form is "sueca".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sueco vive en Estocolmo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Swede lives in Stockholm.

definitions.note: Can refer to the Swedish language; often used as "(el) sueco".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habla sueco en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks Swedish at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi suegra viene a cenar esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother-in-law is coming to dinner tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi suegro vive cerca de nosotros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father-in-law lives near us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La suela de mis zapatos está muy gastada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sole of my shoes is very worn.

definitions.note: Usually refers to regular pay from a job (often monthly), especially for employees.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi sueldo no alcanza para pagar el alquiler este mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My salary isn’t enough to pay the rent this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los sueldos en esa empresa son buenos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The salaries at that company are good.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to talk about what someone usually does.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana suele levantarse temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister usually gets up early.

definitions.note: From the verb "soler"; it’s used to talk about what someone typically does.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella suele caminar al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She usually walks to work.

definitions.note: Used to talk about a habitual action; often followed by an infinitive (e.g., "suelen + infinitive").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los estudiantes suelen estudiar en la biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students usually study in the library.

definitions.note: Used to talk about what people generally do; typically followed by an infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suelen cenar a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They usually have dinner at eight.

definitions.note: From the verb "soler"; used to talk about what you typically do.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suelo desayunar a las siete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually eat breakfast at seven.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo) of the verb "soler"; it’s used with an infinitive to talk about what you usually do.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suelo levantarme temprano los lunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually get up early on Mondays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El suelo de la cocina está limpio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen floor is clean.

definitions.note: It can also be used as an informal (tú) command: “¡Suelta!” = “Let go!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella suelta mi mano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lets go of my hand.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) or affirmative command (usted) of “soltar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero que suelte mi mano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want you to let go of my hand.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes) or affirmative command (ustedes) of “soltar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No suelten al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t let go of the dog.

definitions.note: Often used for something not tied, fastened, or attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro está suelto en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is loose in the yard.

definitions.note: Used to describe someone who has been released.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de dos días, quedó suelto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After two days, he was free.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "suelto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los cables están sueltos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cables are loose.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eso suena bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That sounds good.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "sonar" (they sound).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las campanas suenan a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bells sound at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suenas cansado hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You sound tired today.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) of “sonar”; often used after expressions of doubt, desire, or recommendation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No creo que suene bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't think it sounds good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Buena suerte en el examen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good luck on the exam!

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Eres muy suertudo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're very lucky!

definitions.note: Present tense, third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) of "soñar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella sueña con viajar por el mundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dreams of traveling around the world.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Sueñas a menudo con volar?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you often dream about flying?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sueño con viajar a España algún día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dream of traveling to Spain someday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tuve un sueño muy extraño anoche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a very strange dream last night.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of “sleepiness” (e.g., tener sueño = to be sleepy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo sueño y me voy a dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sleepy and I’m going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis sueños son muy extraños a veces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dreams are very strange sometimes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo suficiente dinero para comprar el boleto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have enough money to buy the ticket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya hemos comido suficiente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ve already eaten enough.

definitions.note: It agrees in gender/number with the noun (e.g., suficiente, suficientes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes suficiente dinero para el billete?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have enough money for the ticket?

definitions.note: Often used with ser/estar (e.g., “es suficiente”) to mean “it’s enough.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con eso es suficiente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With that, it's enough.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Está suficientemente caliente el café?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is the coffee hot enough?

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tenemos suficientes sillas para todos?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do we have enough chairs for everyone?

definitions.note: Plural form used with plural nouns (e.g., “suficientes + plural noun”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tenemos suficientes sillas para todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don't have enough chairs for everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella sufre mucho por el estrés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She suffers a lot from stress.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos sufren mucho en invierno por el frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They suffer a lot in winter because of the cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He sufrido mucho este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have suffered a lot this year.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "sufrir"; often used with "estar" to describe an ongoing action/state.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está sufriendo mucho por la pérdida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She is suffering a lot because of the loss.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): third-person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos sufrieron mucho durante la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They suffered a lot during the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sufrimiento de la guerra afecta a muchas familias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suffering from the war affects many families.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sufrimos mucho cuando no dormimos bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We suffer a lot when we don’t sleep well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero sufrir más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to suffer anymore.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of “sufrir.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella sufrió mucho después del accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She suffered a lot after the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sufro mucho cuando estoy enfermo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suffer a lot when I am sick.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, sufría mucho por las alergias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a kid, I suffered a lot from allergies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tu sugerencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for your suggestion.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tus sugerencias para mejorar el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for your suggestions for improving the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te sugiero que descanses un poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suggest that you rest a little.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te sugerí que llegaras temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suggested that you arrive early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te sugiero que hables con tu profesor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suggest that you talk to your teacher.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico sugirió descansar unos días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor suggested resting for a few days.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; often used with "se" (e.g., "se suicidó").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante buscar ayuda si alguien está pensando en suicidarse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to seek help if someone is thinking about committing suicide.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La familia busca ayuda después del suicidio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The family is seeking help after the suicide.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito): used for a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lamentablemente, se suicidó el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sadly, he/she committed suicide last year.

definitions.note: Describes something or someone from Switzerland; it changes form for gender/number (e.g., suiza, suizos, suizas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesor es suizo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Swiss.

definitions.note: Plural form; can refer to mixed groups when used generically.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los suizos hablan alemán, francés, italiano o romanche, dependiendo de la región.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Swiss people speak German, French, Italian, or Romansh, depending on the region.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella sujeta la puerta para que no se cierre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She holds the door so it doesn’t close.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past habitual/ongoing): “was holding/used to hold.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella sujetaba la cuerda con fuerza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was holding the rope tightly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprar un sujetador nuevo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy a new bra.

definitions.note: Often used for physically holding something in place (e.g., with your hand, a clip, a strap, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sujeta bien la caja para que no se caiga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold the box tightly so it doesn't fall.

definitions.note: Used with “a” to mean being under the authority, control, or effect of something (e.g., rules, conditions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy sujeto a las reglas del contrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am subject to the rules of the contract.

definitions.note: Often used in grammar (the subject of a sentence) or in general to mean a person under discussion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sujeto de esta oración es "mi hermana".
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The subject of this sentence is “my sister.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía detuvo a dos sujetos cerca de la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested two individuals near the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella sujetó la bolsa con fuerza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She held the bag tightly.

definitions.native: hold it, hold on to it
definitions.note: Affirmative tú command of “sujetar” with the object pronoun “lo” (“it”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sujétalo bien para que no se caiga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold it tightly so it doesn’t fall.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command; reflexive form (literally “hold yourself”). Often used to tell someone to brace themselves or to hold tight.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Sujétate bien, que vamos a pasar por un bache!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold on tight, we’re going to go over a bump!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La suma de 5 y 3 es 8.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sum of 5 and 3 is 8.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "sumo"; used in formal phrases like "autoridad suma" (supreme authority).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La corte tiene la autoridad suma para decidir el caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The court has the supreme authority to decide the case.

definitions.note: Often used to intensify adjectives or adverbs; common in more formal Spanish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy sumamente cansado hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m extremely tired today.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) of “sumergir.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El submarino se sumergió rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The submarine submerged quickly.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) present tense of "suministrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa suministra agua potable a la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company supplies drinking water to the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El suministro de agua se cortó por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water supply was cut off at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más suministros para el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more supplies for the project.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like "sumo cuidado" (utmost care).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este asunto es de suma importancia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This matter is of the highest importance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos un torneo de sumo en la televisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We watched a sumo tournament on television.

definitions.native: I found out, I learned, I knew
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "saber" (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supe la verdad ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found out the truth yesterday.

definitions.note: Informal; used to intensify meaning or to say something is very good.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La película estuvo super bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella supera sus miedos poco a poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She overcomes her fears little by little.

definitions.note: Past participle of "superar"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses, or with "estar" to describe a state.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He superado mis miedos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have overcome my fears.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to mean someone has gotten over (a situation, person, or problem).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya estoy superado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m over it now.

definitions.note: Often used for overcoming difficulties, obstacles, or emotions (e.g., superar un problema, superar una ruptura).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito superar este problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to overcome this problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su análisis fue muy superficial y no consideró los detalles importantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His analysis was very superficial and didn’t consider the important details.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La superficie del lago es muy grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The surface area of the lake is very large.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi superhéroe favorito es Spider-Man.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My favorite superhero is Spider-Man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis superhéroes favoritos son Spider-Man y Wonder Woman.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My favorite superheroes are Spider-Man and Wonder Woman.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este modelo es superior al anterior.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This model is superior to the previous one.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to someone higher in rank (e.g., at work or in the military).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que hablar con mi superior antes de tomar una decisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to talk to my superior before making a decision.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los pisos superiores tienen una mejor vista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The upper floors have a better view.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy al supermercado a comprar leche y pan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the supermarket to buy milk and bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habla con tu supervisor si tienes alguna duda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Talk to your supervisor if you have any questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La supervivencia de la especie depende del agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The survival of the species depends on water.

definitions.note: plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los supervivientes del accidente fueron llevados al hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The survivors of the accident were taken to the hospital.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of "superar" (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella superó el miedo y habló en público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She overcame her fear and spoke in public.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted form) of "saber"; often used after expressions like "quería que..." or in "si" (if) clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que supiera la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted him/her to know the truth.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (ellos/ellas/ustedes) of “saber”; often used after expressions like “quería que…”, “dudaba que…”, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que supieran la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted them to know the truth.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (tú form); often used after expressions like “si…” (if…) or to express doubt, wishes, or hypotheticals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si supieras la verdad, no dirías eso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you knew the truth, you wouldn’t say that.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) of "saber" for "we".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supimos la verdad ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found out the truth yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te suplico que me ayudes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I beg you to help me.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite): he/she/it begged; you (formal) begged.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella suplicó que la ayudaran.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She begged for them to help her.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “saber”; often used for finding out or learning information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando lo supo, se enojó mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he found out, he got very angry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eso supone que todos están de acuerdo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That assumes that everyone agrees.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cambiar de ciudad supone empezar de nuevo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Changing cities means starting over.

definitions.note: First-person plural present subjunctive; commonly used to propose a hypothetical situation (“let’s say…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supongamos que mañana llueve: ¿qué hacemos?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's suppose it rains tomorrow—what do we do?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supongo que mañana va a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suppose it's going to rain tomorrow.

definitions.native: I/he/she used to suppose, I/he/she was supposing
definitions.note: Imperfect tense; the exact subject (I/he/she) depends on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo suponía que la tienda abría a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought the store opened at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu suposición no es correcta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your assumption is not correct.

definitions.note: Used to indicate that something is said to be true but is not confirmed (and sometimes the speaker doubts it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supuestamente, el paquete llega mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Supposedly, the package arrives tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun to mean “alleged” (e.g., "el supuesto ladrón").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó al supuesto responsable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the alleged person responsible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eso es solo un supuesto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is just an assumption.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form meaning a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supuse que ya habías llegado a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I assumed that you had already gotten home.

definitions.note: Informal command form (tú) of “suponer.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supón que mañana llueve: ¿qué hacemos?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suppose it rains tomorrow—what do we do?

definitions.note: Often used with nouns to mean “southern” (e.g., viento sur = south wind).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El viento sur es cálido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The south wind is warm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sur de España es muy cálido en verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The south of Spain is very warm in summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A veces surgen problemas inesperados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes unexpected problems arise.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De repente, surgieron varios problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly, several problems arose.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form meaning “(he/she/it) arose/came up” or “you (formal) arose/came up.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De repente surgió un problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly a problem came up.

definitions.note: Plural possessive determiner (agrees with the noun that follows). Can mean “your” in formal address (usted/ustedes), and it’s ambiguous without context (his/her/their/your).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus amigos están aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their friends are here.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (e.g., “suscrito a” = “subscribed to”). In formal writing, it can also mean “undersigned.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy suscrito al boletín de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m subscribed to the school newsletter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta el sushi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like sushi.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a suspender el partido por la lluvia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to suspend the match because of the rain.

definitions.note: Common in Spain; in much of Latin America, people often say "reprobar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no estudias, vas a suspender el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t study, you’re going to fail the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El partido está suspendido por la lluvia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The game is suspended because of the rain.

definitions.note: Common in Spain when talking about exams or school subjects.

definitions.note: Commonly used with "la basura" (take out/throw away the trash) or "fotos" (take photos), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tire la pelota al aire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She throws the ball into the air.

definitions.note: Verb form of "tirar". Not related to the English word "tire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre tiro la pelota al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always throw the ball to the dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escuché un tiro en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a shot in the street.

definitions.note: Often used for a throw (for example, in sports).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su tiro fue muy preciso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His throw was very accurate.

definitions.note: Plural of "tiro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escuché tiros en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard shots in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiré la pelota al jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I threw the ball into the yard.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular of "tirar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él tiró la pelota al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threw the ball to the dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dame un tirón de la cuerda, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give the rope a pull, please.

definitions.note: Often used for a sudden muscle injury, especially in the leg or back.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me dio un tirón en la pierna mientras corría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a muscle strain in my leg while I was running.

definitions.note: Often used for the person whose name is officially on an account, document, or position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La titular de la cuenta vive en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The account holder lives in Madrid.

definitions.note: Commonly used for news or newspaper headlines.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leí los titulares esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the headlines this morning.

definitions.note: Used for someone who officially holds something (like an account, a card, or a position).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los titulares de la cuenta deben firmar el formulario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The account holders must sign the form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor escribió en la pizarra con tiza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher wrote on the board with chalk.

definitions.note: Plural of "tiza".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito tizas de colores para la pizarra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need colored chalk for the board.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "teñir"; often used with "estar" to describe an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy tiñendo mi cabello en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dyeing my hair at home.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/it dyed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tiñó su pelo de rojo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dyed her hair red.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una toalla limpia después de ducharme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a clean towel after showering.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más toallas para el baño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more towels for the bathroom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me torcí el tobillo jugando al fútbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I twisted my ankle playing soccer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No toca eso, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t touch that, please.

definitions.note: Used with musical instruments (e.g., tocar la guitarra).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano toca el piano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother plays the piano.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often used for ongoing or habitual past actions (e.g., playing an instrument).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tocaba el piano cuando era niño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to play the piano when I was a child.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often used for ongoing or habitual past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tocaba la pared para ver si estaba fría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was touching the wall to see if it was cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He tocado el botón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have touched the button.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He tocado la guitarra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have played the guitar.

definitions.note: Can mean either “we play” (music/instrument) or “we touch,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tocamos la guitarra después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We play the guitar after dinner.

definitions.note: Present tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes). Often used with instruments (play) or physical contact (touch).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tocan la guitarra en una banda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They play the guitar in a band.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "tocar"; often used with "estar" to describe an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy tocando la guitarra en mi cuarto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am playing the guitar in my room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No toques el vidrio, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t touch the glass, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Sabes tocar la guitarra?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you know how to play the guitar?

definitions.note: Used especially for bells, doorbells, or phones.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Están tocando el timbre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re ringing the doorbell.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of “tocar”; often used after “si” to talk about hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tocara el piano, practicaría todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I played the piano, I would practice every day.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of “tocar”; often used after “si” to talk about hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tocara esa olla, me quemaría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I touched that pot, I would burn myself.

definitions.note: Includes the attached object pronoun “me” = “me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedes tocarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can't touch me.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "tocar" for "they/you all" (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tocaron la puerta y nadie abrió.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They knocked on the door and nobody opened.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached object pronoun “te” (“you,” informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero tocarte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to touch you.

definitions.note: Often used for playing a musical instrument.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana tocaré la guitarra en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will play the guitar at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tocaré nada sin permiso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I won't touch anything without permission.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué tocas mi teléfono?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you touching my phone?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of "tocar" for "tú".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tocaste el piano ayer?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you play the piano yesterday?

definitions.note: In some regions it can also refer to pork fat/lard, but the most common meaning is bacon.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para el desayuno, quiero huevos con tocino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For breakfast, I want eggs with bacon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No toco la pantalla con las manos sucias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t touch the screen with dirty hands.

definitions.note: Used with musical instruments (e.g., tocar la guitarra).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Toco la guitarra todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play the guitar every day.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "tocar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tocó el piano en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She played the piano at the party.

definitions.note: Often used colloquially for emphasis, especially with feminine reference (e.g., "toda mojada" = "all wet").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la lluvia, estoy toda mojada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, I'm all wet.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “todo”; used before a feminine singular noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Toda la noche estudié para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I studied for the exam all night.

definitions.note: used before feminine plural nouns (e.g., todas las casas)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas las preguntas son importantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the questions are important.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; used for groups of women/girls or feminine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas están listas para salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone is ready to go out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todavía no he terminado la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still haven’t finished the homework.

definitions.note: As an adverb, it can emphasize “completely/entirely” (e.g., “todo listo” = “all ready”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya lo sé todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already know everything.

definitions.note: Often used with an article: todo el / todo la = “the whole …”. Without an article, it can mean “every …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He leído todo el libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve read the whole book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo perdí todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost everything.

definitions.note: Used as a pronoun to refer to a whole thing or the total of things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todo está listo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is ready.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "todo"; used with masculine plural nouns (e.g., "todos los días").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos los estudiantes están aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the students are here.

definitions.note: Masculine plural pronoun; often refers to a mixed group (men and women) or to people/things in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos llegaron temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone arrived early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más tolerancia en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more tolerance at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis padres son muy tolerantes con mis ideas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents are very tolerant of my ideas.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis vecinos son muy tolerantes con el ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are very tolerant about the noise.

definitions.native: to tolerate, to put up with
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo tolerar ese ruido toda la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't tolerate that noise all night.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “toma de control” (takeover of control) or “toma de rehenes” (hostage-taking).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía evitó la toma del edificio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police prevented the takeover of the building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella toma el autobús todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She takes the bus every day.

definitions.note: Often used with beverages (e.g., café, agua) to mean “drink.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él toma café por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drinks coffee in the morning.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, tomaba el autobús a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to take the bus to school.

definitions.note: Used to address a group informally (vosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomad una foto aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a photo here, please.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "tomar"; used with passive voice or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La foto fue tomada ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photo was taken yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "tomar"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses (e.g., "he tomado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He tomado un café esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a coffee this morning.

definitions.note: Most commonly: “we take” in general; “we drink” when talking about beverages.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomamos un café después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a coffee after class.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "tomar" (they/you all take/drink).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos toman café todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They drink coffee every morning.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “tomar”; commonly used with “estar” to mean “(to be) taking/having” something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy tomando un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having a coffee.

definitions.note: Often used with food/drink to mean “to have” (e.g., tomar un café = to have a coffee).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomar el autobús a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to take the bus at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero tomar agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to drink water, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form, often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., with "si" = "if").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tomara el autobús, llegaría más temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I took the bus, I would arrive earlier.

definitions.native: I will take, I will drink
definitions.note: This is a rare/archaic future form in modern Spanish. Today you usually say “tomaré” (with an accent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana tomare el tren temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will take the train early.

definitions.native: we will take, we will have (food/drink)
definitions.note: Future tense (nosotros). Often used for having food or drinks in context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana tomaremos el tren a Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will take the train to Madrid.

definitions.note: Object pronoun “lo” = “it” (masculine singular) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomarlo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to take it now.

definitions.native: to take (for myself), to have (for myself)
definitions.note: Reflexive/indirect object form: literally “to take me” / “to take for myself,” often used with drinks or medicine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomarme un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to have a coffee.

definitions.note: Reflexive with an indirect object pronoun: “tomarnos” often means “to have/drink (something)” and “nos” indicates it’s for/among us (e.g., “let’s have a coffee”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a tomarnos un café después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s have a coffee after class.

definitions.note: Third-person plural preterite (they/you all took).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos tomaron el autobús a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; very common with food/drinks (e.g., tomarse un café = to have a coffee).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me tomo un café por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a coffee in the morning.

definitions.note: Reflexive form used to say how long something takes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El viaje se toma dos horas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trip takes two hours.

definitions.native: to have (something to drink), to take (something)
definitions.note: Often used with drinks (e.g., “tomarte un café” = “to have a coffee”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomarte un café antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to have a coffee before leaving.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (él/ella/usted) future tense of “tomar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tomará el autobús mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will take the bus tomorrow.

definitions.native: you will take, you will have
definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana tomarás el autobús a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will take the bus at eight.

definitions.native: I will take, I will have (drink)
definitions.note: First-person singular future tense of “tomar”. Often used for choosing a drink (“I’ll have…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomaré un café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll have a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "tomar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo tomaría un café, pero ya es muy tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would have a coffee, but it’s already very late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tomas el autobús todos los días?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you take the bus every day?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tomaste el café esta mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you drink the coffee this morning?

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) of “tomar” with the attached pronoun “te” (= yourself). Often used to tell someone to have/eat/drink something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomate un café y seguimos hablando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have a coffee and we’ll keep talking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un tomate para la ensalada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a tomato for the salad.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré tomates para la ensalada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought tomatoes for the salad.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted): “tome” = “take”. It can also be present subjunctive (e.g., “Espero que tome…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tome este medicamento dos veces al día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take this medicine twice a day.

definitions.note: Used to suggest doing something together (nosotros command / present subjunctive). Often used as an invitation, e.g., to have a drink.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomemos un café después de la clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's have a coffee after class.

definitions.note: Command form used for “you” (ustedes), and also the present subjunctive for “you” (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, tomen asiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, have a seat.

definitions.note: Often used after expressions like “no” (negative command) or “que…” (subjunctive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tomes esto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t take this.

definitions.note: From the verb "tomar". Often used for taking something (like medicine) or drinking (especially beverages).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomo un café por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a coffee in the morning.

definitions.note: Informal command form used with voseo (common in Argentina, Uruguay, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomá este libro, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take this book, please.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of "tomar". It often means "I took" (took something) or "I had" (food/drink).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer tomé un café antes de ir al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I had a coffee before going to work.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (preterite) of “tomar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él tomó un café esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took (had) a coffee this morning.

definitions.note: Plural of “tonelada” (metric tons in most Spanish-speaking contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El camión transporta diez toneladas de arena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck carries ten tons of sand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me gustó el tono de tu mensaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't like the tone of your message.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La canción tiene tonos suaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The song has soft tones.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas tonta; ya hiciste tu parte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't be silly; you already did your part.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No digas cosas tontas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t say silly things.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about something trivial or foolish; can be mild or insulting depending on tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deja de decir tonterías y escucha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop saying nonsense and listen.

definitions.note: Plural; often used to dismiss something as unimportant or stupid.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No digas tonterías; eso no es verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't say nonsense; that's not true.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person or behavior; can be insulting depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas tonto; mira por dónde caminas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be silly; watch where you’re walking.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult; can also be used more lightly (like “silly”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas tonto, ponte el abrigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be an idiot, put on your coat.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No digas cosas tontas, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't say silly things, please.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also be used for mixed-gender groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No hagas caso a esos tontos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t pay attention to those fools.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He topado con Ana en el supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran into Ana at the supermarket.

definitions.native: we run into, we bump into
definitions.note: Often used with "con" to mean meeting someone/something unexpectedly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Topamos con Ana en el supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ran into Ana at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Often used with "con" (e.g., "topé con...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer topé con Ana en el supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ran into Ana at the supermarket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer topó con un viejo amigo en el supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, he/she ran into an old friend at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “espero que…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no toque eso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don’t touch that.

definitions.note: Often used for a brief or light touch (e.g., “un toque suave”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dio un toque en el hombro para llamar su atención.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave him a tap on the shoulder to get his attention.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for formal commands with ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que toquen la guitarra esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you play the guitar tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero que toques eso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want you to touch that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mejor que no toques el piano ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better if you don’t play the piano now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dale dos toques a la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give the door two taps.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer toqué el piano en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I played the piano at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El clavo está torcido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nail is bent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Torció la tapa del frasco para abrirlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He twisted the jar lid to open it.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
